b.why:
DECIDABLE in form, with a stated undecidable residue.

The claim is "the progeny of CD56bright are CD56dim" — a precursor-product statement, which the rubric puts on the decidable side. More importantly, its principal rival (Phase A's alternative: a pre-existing CD56dim population is selected/expanded, not converted; and the two-independent-pathway model) is a PURE CLONAL-STRUCTURE statement, and clonal structure is exactly what the primitive returns. "Do the CD56dim cells recovered descend from the CD56bright cells put in, or from a contaminating dim cell?" is answerable with shared-ancestor information and nothing else — it is the one question the barcoding primitive is definitionally competent to settle. Likewise "are CD56bright and CD56dim the same or different lineage" is the rubric's explicit DECIDABLE case, and it has already been posed and answered this way in a primate (Wu 2018, Sci Immunol, PMID 30389798: barcoded macaque HSPC transplant, CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+ NK repertoires "remained distinct under homeostatic conditions over several years").

The load-bearing part of the primitive here is HOW RECENTLY, not merely WHETHER. Every NK cell in one person shares an HSPC ancestor, so bare ancestor-sharing is trivially TRUE under all models. The discriminating readout is whether a bright cell and a dim cell share a recent, post-NK-commitment ancestor (consistent with bright->dim) or only a distant progenitor-level one (two pools branching upstream, the Ding 2024 ENKP/ILCP architecture).

UNDECIDABLE RESIDUE, stated explicitly. Surface NCAM1 density is an activation-modulable variable, so part of this claim is a reversible-state claim, and for that part both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure: a clone spanning both compartments is produced equally by (a) irreversible bright->dim maturation, (b) dim->bright, and (c) cells oscillating between two states. Lineage cannot order a reversible state. It also cannot separate "dim descend from bright" from "bright and dim are clonal siblings branching a few divisions upstream" at the resolution obtainable in a polyclonal human steady state — mtDNA marks label clades, not division events, and PMID 40134031 (Genome Biol 2025) shows mtDNA variants have "limited discriminatory power among different genuine lineages under weak clonal expansion," which is precisely the healthy-adult NK regime. So: the NEGATIVE is decisive (clonally discordant repertoires falsify the arrow), the POSITIVE is confounded on both direction and sibling-vs-parent. Decidable, but one-sidedly.
b.action_if_yes:
IF YES (bright and dim share recent, post-commitment clones; bright-marked clones later appear in dim):

Stated concretely, the next experiment would be to move from "there is a route" to "how fast and driven by what": longitudinal clone-level sampling in the same individual to fit a conversion rate, then a perturbation arm asking which signal drives it (the unreplicated Chan 2007 fibroblast/FGFR1 contact route vs the IL-2/IL-15/IL-12 route that Romagnani 2007 and Chan 2007 disagree about), and a translational arm barcoding a CD56bright-phenotype iPSC/CD34-derived NK product to confirm it matures in the recipient.

Why this branch is weak, written out because B2 turns on it:
(1) It is the default expectation, not a discovery. Shared clonal marks between two mature NK subsets are predicted by essentially every model on the table, including the competing one in which both subsets are fed independently from the same upstream progenitor clones. A YES therefore does not separate the claim from its main rival.
(2) The direction it appears to license is not actually licensed. Establishing bright-before-dim requires ordering within a clone, which reversibility of CD56 density confounds and which mtDNA/integration-site resolution in a polyclonal steady state does not deliver.
(3) The follow-ons are not contingent on the answer. Human in-vivo pulse-chase (the 6,6-D2-glucose sorted-subset design of Patel 2017, PMID 28606987 / PMC5502436, which has never been run on bright vs dim — the only NK deuterium study, PMID 17346281, sorted CD3-CD16+ only and did not resolve the subsets) is the assay that would actually settle direction, and it is a NON-lineage assay one would run instead of, not because of, the clonal experiment. The FGF-vs-cytokine mechanism question and the iPSC-NK maturation question are already being pursued by the field on the assumption that the answer is YES; a YES changes nobody's protocol.
Net: YES confirms the textbook arrow, is non-discriminating against the sibling model, and redirects no downstream work.
b.action_if_no:
IF NO (repertoires clonally discordant; bright-dominant clones stay bright over months-to-years and never seed dim):

This branch is genuinely rich and the next experiments are specific and forced:
(1) It replicates Wu 2018 (PMID 30389798) in the species that matters and kills the stage-4 -> stage-5 arrow of the Freud/Caligiuri five-stage human model, which is the one concrete named dependency Phase A left standing. The immediate follow-on is to look for the human counterpart of the two-pathway ontogeny reported in mouse (Ding 2024, Nat Immunol, PMID 38872000, ENKP vs ILCP): prospectively isolate the candidate human progenitors from bone marrow/tonsil and ask, clonally, which one feeds CD56dim.
(2) It removes the mechanistic explanation for the GATA2-deficiency phenotype (Mace 2013, PMID 23365458: patients maintaining a CD56dim pool with essentially no CD56bright) and makes those patients the natural human genetic test bed rather than an anomaly.
(3) It breaks a manufacturing rationale, which is the sharpest practical consequence. Current iPSC- and CD34-derived NK products come out CD56bright-phenotype and are infused on the assumption that they mature into cytotoxic CD56dim in the patient. Under NO, that assumption is void and the next experiment is defined: determine whether a CD56dim-committed product can be derived directly, and re-read existing infusion trials for whether the transferred bright product ever became dim.
(4) It reclassifies CD56 density as a state/activation variable rather than a developmental stage, which changes how every NK scRNA-seq trajectory paper that orients its pseudotime by this arrow should be read.
b.both_answers_reason:
FALSE on asymmetric payoff. The two branches are not the same experiment, so the claim does not fail the "identical follow-on" test — it fails on the other clause: the YES branch is vacuous in the sense the filter targets.

Laid out against each other: NO overturns a textbook arrow, forces a named search (human ENKP/ILCP-equivalent progenitors), converts GATA2 patients into a test bed, and voids a live cell-manufacturing rationale. YES yields "the consensus model is confirmed" and hands back a set of experiments the field is already running on the assumption that YES is true. Nothing in a lab's plan moves on a YES.

Three specific reasons the YES arm does not survive strict reading:
(a) NON-DISCRIMINATING. Shared clonal marks between two mature NK subsets from one donor are predicted by the claim AND by its principal competitor (both pools fed independently from shared upstream progenitor clones). An outcome both hypotheses predict is not an actionable outcome.
(b) RESOLUTION-LIMITED. Separating parent-child from sibling, and forward from reversible, needs within-clone ordering that the available human clonal marks do not provide in a polyclonal steady state (PMID 40134031). So the YES cannot even be reported as a clean confirmation.
(c) FOLLOW-ON IS NOT CONTINGENT. The experiment that would follow a YES — a human sorted-subset deuterium pulse-chase — is a non-lineage assay that is equally worth running today and is the design that would actually settle direction. If your positive result's next step is "now run the experiment you should have run first," the positive was not load-bearing.

This is a judgement about the decision structure only; the scientific worth of the question is out of scope for this round and I make no claim about it. Note for the shortlist: the sub-question "are CD56bright and CD56dim two separately maintained pools in humans?" — posed as a falsification test rather than as a confirmation of the arrow — would pass B2 much better than the arrow as worded, because its informative arm is the arm that is reachable. If the screen permits reframing, D3 is a candidate for restatement rather than straight elimination.
b.compartments_needed:
Two, and only two, for the core adjudication, both from peripheral blood of the same individual at the same draw:
(A) CD3- CD56bright CD16- NK cells
(B) CD3- CD56dim CD16+ NK cells

Optional compartments that strengthen but are not required:
(C) Bone marrow (aspirate) — to place the branch point relative to progenitors.
(D) Secondary lymphoid tissue where CD56bright is enriched — tonsil (routine tonsillectomy waste) or lymph node (only at surgery).
(E) The clonal-mark substrate, which is the real constraint rather than the tissue: NK cells have no rearranged antigen receptor, so there is no endogenous clone label of the kind the T/B fields get free. The mark must come from (i) somatic mtDNA or nuclear SNVs, (ii) lentiviral integration sites in HSC gene-therapy recipients, (iii) donor/recipient marks after allo-HSCT, or (iv) engineered barcodes, which in a primate means macaque.
b.compartments_obtainable:
YES — and this is the strongest feature of D3. Compartments A and B are obtainable paired from one human, from one routine venipuncture, in any healthy adult, with no procedural gate whatsoever. Not post-mortem. Not surgery-only. Not pregnancy-only. Not mouse-only. Of the compartment pairings in this screen this is close to the least constrained one available.

The gating constraint is the clonal mark, not tissue access, and even that has an existing human substrate: the lentiviral HSC gene-therapy cohort in PMID 39442556 (Nature 2024; 53 patients, MLD/WAS/beta-thalassaemia, integration sites as clonal identity, follow-up to 8 years, PB and BM). I read its Methods (archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC11618100.txt) and confirmed the relevant gap: NK cells were purified as BULK CD56+ by immunomagnetic beads ("CD56 + (CD56 Micro Beads Human, MILTENYI BIOTEC) were isolated in sequence"), with no bright/dim split anywhere in the study. So the human clonal substrate for this exact question exists and has already been banked longitudinally; what is missing is a FACS sort of bright vs dim in place of a bulk CD56 bead pull. Analogous human substrates: allo-HSCT genome-wide somatic-mutation clonal tracking (PMID 39478227).

Optional compartments: (C) bone marrow needs an aspirate — a real but routine procedural gate in transplant/GT cohorts where marrow is already drawn; (D) tonsil is available as routine surgical waste, lymph node only at surgery. Neither is required for the core bright-vs-dim adjudication.
b.compartment_notes:
SPECIES: this is a human-only claim, and the direction of the constraint is the opposite of most rows in this screen — it is not mouse-only, it CANNOT be posed in mouse. Mouse NK cells do not carry the CD56bright/CD56dim partition (NCAM1 is not a mouse NK subset marker; mouse maturation is staged on CD27/CD11b, which is claim D2). The available animal proxy is rhesus macaque, and even there the axis is not identical: macaque subsets are CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+, whereas human CD56dim are CD56+CD16+. Wu 2018 (PMID 30389798) therefore answered an analogous, not the same, question — which is exactly why the human version remains open despite a clonal-grade primate result already existing.

PURITY IS THE CRUX, AND CLONAL MARKING IS WHAT FIXES IT: CD56dim are ~90% of blood NK, so a 1-2% dim carry-over into a sorted bright fraction is, in absolute terms, a large dim population — the failure mode Phase A flagged for the Chan 2007 NOD-SCID arm. This is precisely the artefact that per-cell clonal marks neutralise, since a carry-over dim cell carries a mark and a converted one carries its parent's. Design implication: index/single-cell sorting with per-cell marks, not bulk repertoire comparison of two sorted pools.

YIELD: from a standard 50 mL draw expect ~5x10^6 NK, of which bright is ~5-10%, so ~2-5x10^5 bright cells — adequate for mtscATAC/MAESTER. For integration-site PCR at the depth used in PMID 39442556 (12 mL draws), the bright fraction is likely yield-limited and would want leukapheresis or pooled timepoints; worth costing before committing.

SETTING SELECTION MATTERS MORE THAN TISSUE ACCESS: PMID 40134031 shows mtDNA marks discriminate lineages well only under stringent clonal expansion. Healthy-adult polyclonal NK is the weak-expansion regime where they do not. If this claim is pursued, the compartments should be drawn from a stringent-expansion setting — gene-therapy or allo-HSCT recipients, aged donors with clonal haematopoiesis, or HCMV+ donors carrying large adaptive NKG2C+ clones — rather than from a young healthy donor, where the compartments are trivially obtainable but the marks will not resolve.

o.already_traced_evidence:
NOBODY HAS ADJUDICATED THE CLAIM AS POSED: no study has used a clonal/lineage primitive on HUMAN CD3-CD56bright CD16- vs CD3-CD56dim CD16+ NK cells to ask whether they share recent ancestors. Four studies come close, each missing on a different axis; I read the full text or methods of all four.

(1) NEAREST IN SUBSTRATE - Ruckert, Lareau, Mashreghi, Ludwig, Romagnani, Nat Immunol 2022, PMID 36289449 (PMC9663309, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/PMC9663309.txt). Human peripheral blood NK, ASAP-seq + CITE-seq with somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous barcodes, 4 HCMV+ and 3 HCMV- donors, longitudinal to 19 months. This is the right species, right cells, right tool, and it explicitly annotates CD56bright / early CD56dim / mature CD56dim / adaptive clusters IN THE SAME OBJECT. But the question it poses is adaptive NKG2C+ clonal expansion, not bright->dim. Its only D3-bearing sentence is an incidental control null: clonotype-cluster association by chi-square "was absent in the conventional NK cell compartment ... suggesting that mitochondrial mutations of conventional NK cells do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level." Three reasons this is not the adjudication: (a) it is a null from an association test, not a directed bright-vs-dim clone-sharing test against a null model; (b) the stated interpretation (progenitor-level marks) is the SIBLING model, i.e. it reads against the arrow rather than for it, but is offered as an aside with no quantification; (c) the clonotype caller is configured to find expansions and structurally cannot support the test - Methods state clonotypes were called by clustering on mtDNA allele frequency with parameters "empirically optimized per donor so that clonotypes were defined by approximately one mutation, and only those clonotypes were included that had at least one significantly enriched mutation," and "clonotypes only defined by differential frequency of highly abundant mutations were excluded." That pipeline discards exactly the diffuse, non-expanded clonal structure a bright->dim test needs. Data are public (GEO GSE197037; code github.com/timorueckert/Clonal_NK), so a reanalysis path exists - this is the single most important fact for the shortlist.

(2) NEAREST IN QUESTION, WRONG SPECIES AND AXIS - Wu, Espinoza, Koelle, ... Bryceson, Dunbar, Sci Immunol 2018, PMID 30389798. Lentivirally barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus macaque, >4 years. Poses the identical structural question and answers NO: CD56-CD16+ NK "remained long-term clonally uncoupled from other hematopoietic lineages, including CD56+CD16- NK cells," and "linear NK cell production from multipotent hematopoietic progenitors or less mature CD56+CD16- cells is negligible during homeostasis and moderate proliferative stress." Misses because macaque CD56+CD16-/CD56-CD16+ is not the human CD56bright/CD56dim axis - human CD56dim are CD56+CD16+, so the macaque "dim homolog" is CD56-negative. Precursor study Wu 2014 Cell Stem Cell PMID 24702997 barcoded the same model and found the CD16+/CD56- NK compartment "ontologically distinct" with limited clonal overlap with T/B/myeloid, but that is the upstream NK-vs-other-lineage question, not bright vs dim.

(3) RIGHT TOOL, HUMAN, BUT NK LUMPED - Liu, Sandor, Yan, ... Ludwig, Lareau, Satpathy, "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer" (Mitotrek), Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 (PMC13309241); preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC12330704.txt. mtscATAC-seq + mtDNA clone calling on 218,715 cells from matched tumor/non-involved tissue/blood, NSCLC and ovarian. I checked both versions: NK appears only as 3-4 lumped "NK/ILC" clusters called on NCR1, with no CD56bright/CD56dim split anywhere (the preprint contains exactly one CD56 mention). NK findings are limited to "expanded NK cell clones in NILT and peripheral blood," an "oligoclonal architecture resembling adaptive lymphocytes" in one ovarian tumor, and high innate clone sharing. The published abstract and MeSH terms (Macrophages, Dendritic Cells, Monocytes; no NK descriptor) confirm NK subsets are not the subject.

(4) BARCODES, HUMAN CELLS, BUT IN VITRO AND WRONG STAGES - Vo, Ouyang, Kanaya, ... Malmberg, Sitnicka, Blood Adv 2024, PMID 38484189 (PMC11176970, archived). CellTag lentiviral DNA-barcode clonal tracing of cord-blood Lin-CD34+ cells (~570 barcoded cells) differentiated on OP9 stroma; barcodes recovered from FACS-purified B, ILC3, S3b-NK (CD56+CD94-) and S4-NK (CD56+CD94+). Establishes S3b-NK/S4-NK clonal proximity and distance from ILC3. Misses on all three counts: in vitro, cord blood, and stage-3/4 progenitors rather than the blood CD56bright/CD56dim (stage 4/5) subsets D3 is about.

ALSO CHECKED AND NEGATIVE: Panjwani, Grassmann, ... Sun, Hsu, Front Immunol 2024, PMID 39742279 (PMC11686228, archived) argues CD56bright is a bipotential progenitor for classic CD56dim and adaptive NK and is the closest thing to a positive claim in humans - but it is a trajectory/phenotype paper (10x GEX + CITE + feature barcoding), NOT a clonal method; it cites others' mtDNA data for shared mutations between adaptive and CD56bright rather than generating any. Allan 2023 PMID 36699615 (macaque barcodes through ex vivo NK expansion), Wu 2022 PMID 36605190 (macaque barcodes, tissue-resident NK), PMID 31649681 (macaque barcodes, CMV NK repertoire) are all Dunbar-lab macaque and none split bright/dim. Penter 2024 PMID 39236287 uses mtDNA + ASAP-seq post allo-HSCT for donor/recipient chimerism and leukemia tracking, not NK subsets. No Polylox, Confetti, or CRISPR-recorder study of NK subset maturation surfaced; searches returned only generic hematopoiesis-tool reviews.

RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (why I set confidence MEDIUM, not HIGH): the negative rests on thorough but not exhaustive coverage. lit.py's PubMed backend returned empty for roughly half my queries so most recall came from EPMC (noisy) plus WebSearch; and I could not inspect Ruckert 2022's Extended Data figure panels directly, only the Results text describing them and the Methods describing the caller. A 2025-2026 bioRxiv preprint doing exactly this reanalysis is a plausible and easy-to-miss object - the parent should sweep preprint servers before treating the lane as fully open.
o.nearest_occupant:
Two occupants, near-misses on orthogonal axes; neither adjudicates the claim.

NEAREST OVERALL - PMID 36289449 (Ruckert et al., Nat Immunol 2022). Difference: right species (human), right compartments (blood CD56bright and CD56dim, both annotated in one dataset), right primitive (somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous clonal barcodes), WRONG QUESTION. They asked whether adaptive NKG2C+ NK cells are clonal expansions and answered yes. Bright-vs-dim clone sharing was never tested as such; the only bearing on D3 is a one-sentence null observation that mtDNA clonotypes fail to associate with conventional-subset identity, glossed as marks "present already on the progenitor level." Critically their clonotype caller retains only clonotypes with a significantly enriched mutation and discards those defined by differential frequency of abundant mutations - it is built to detect expansions and by construction throws away the diffuse clonal structure a bright->dim test requires. So D3 is not pre-empted; it is one purpose-built reanalysis away from being addressable in public data (GEO GSE197037).

NEAREST ON THE QUESTION ITSELF - PMID 30389798 (Wu et al., Sci Immunol 2018). Difference: asks precisely D3's structural question with lentiviral barcodes over >4 years and returns a clean NO - CD56-CD16+ NK clones stay clonally uncoupled from CD56+CD16- NK, and linear production from less mature CD56+CD16- cells is "negligible." But it is rhesus macaque, and the macaque axis is not the human one: macaque CD56+CD16- vs CD56-CD16+ maps onto human CD56bright vs CD56dim only by analogy, since human CD56dim are CD56-POSITIVE and CD16+. The species that carries the CD56bright/CD56dim partition (human) is the one where the clonal experiment has not been run, and the species where it has been run does not carry the partition. That mismatch is exactly why a primate clonal-grade answer already existing does not close the human claim.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HIGH occupancy of the STRUCTURAL question ("does phenotypically defined subset A give rise to subset B in vivo, adjudicated by clone sharing?"), across all three neighbouring fields - but zero occupancy of the human NK bright/dim instance. Importantly, the cross-field work reads as a validated TEMPLATE for D3 rather than a pre-emption of it, and it cuts against the linear-maturation reading twice.

MYELOID - ANSWERED, IN HUMANS, WITH THE EXACT TOOL D3 WOULD USE. PMID 42242233 (Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, Mitotrek; preprint 40777278) used mtscATAC-seq + mtDNA clone calling on matched human tumor/tissue/blood to establish that TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and further resolved DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones whose circulating precursors differ epigenetically. That is the monocyte->macrophage/DC arrow settled by clone sharing in human tissue - structurally identical to bright->dim, same primitive, same assay, same scale. It is a proof that the design works on a non-antigen-receptor-bearing innate compartment. Note the same senior authors (Ludwig, Lareau) are on Ruckert 2022, so the group that owns the tool has already touched human NK subsets and did not run this test.

T CELL - ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER OVERTURNED THE LINEAR MODEL. The naive->effector->memory precursor-product question is the field's most heavily lineage-traced structure, via TCR sequences as free natural barcodes, mouse single-cell fate mapping, and human mtDNA (PMID 30827679, Ludwig et al., Cell 2019, the founding human mtDNA lineage-tracing paper; PMID 39123248 used X-inactivation-directed mtDNA to resolve human T clonal structure including gamma-delta separation; PMID 33037653 reviews T fate-mapping/lineage-tracing technologies specifically for CD8 subset generation). The substantive result is the cautionary one: clonal tools showed fate segregation of short-lived effector and long-lived memory progeny begins at or near the first division rather than by sequential maturation through a phenotypic ladder. Panjwani 2024 (PMID 39742279) transposes exactly this argument onto NK, invoking the naive-memory framework to argue CD56bright is a bipotential progenitor for classic-dim AND adaptive rather than a rung on a linear ladder. So the borrowed mechanism's occupancy does live in the field it was borrowed from, and there it demoted the linear reading.

ILC / NK IN MODEL SPECIES - ANSWERED, ALSO AGAINST A SINGLE LINEAR ARROW. PMID 38872000 (Ding et al., Nat Immunol 2024) used mouse fate mapping to show NK cells arise by at least two developmental pathways - ENKP (NK-lineage-biased early progenitors) independent of the common ILC precursor ILCP - generating functionally distinct NK populations, which the authors suggest may be conserved in humans (see also review PMID 41634488). Combined with Wu 2018 in macaque, the two-independent-pools alternative to D3's arrow is the one that lineage tools have actually supported wherever they have been applied.

NET: every adjacent field has run this experiment; two of them got answers that disfavour linear maturation; the human NK bright/dim instance is the conspicuous hole, and the tooling to fill it is demonstrated and public.

b.why:
TRUE, with one scope condition and one design condition, both stated below.

FORM. The claim is "the progeny of A are B" (A = conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ NK; B = adaptive NK), not "A becomes functionally B-like". It is therefore in the decidable class — PROVIDED compartment B is operationalised as a SORT GATE (NKG2C+, and per Liu 2016 PMID 27117418 the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate: FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+, demethylated IFNG CNS1) rather than as a function ("memory", "recall"). If B were defined by recall capacity, lineage could not decide it. Note the naming problem this exposes: NKG2C is dispensable (11/44 KLRC2-/- HCMV+ donors have bona fide adaptive expansions), so a barcoding study gated only on NKG2C would decide a narrower claim than the one the field actually holds. The gate must be the adaptive signature, not the receptor.

WHY THE PRIMITIVE IS NOT TRIVIALLY SATISFIED. All NK cells in one person share an HSPC ancestor, so "do A and B share an ancestor?" is trivially YES and carries no information. The claim is decidable only through the RECENCY half of the primitive — which is exactly what the primitive supplies. The three live models make non-overlapping predictions about MRCA depth: (i) CONVERSION — an expanded adaptive clone's MRCA with a contemporaneous conventional NKG2C- cell sits at mature-NK depth, so one recent, NK-private clonotype contains both conventional and adaptive cells; (ii) SELECTION of a pre-existing already-NKG2C+ founder (Ruckert 2022's own stated model; Bjorkstrom 2011 PMC3023129; Adams 2019) — the adaptive clone's recent relatives are all already adaptive, and the MRCA with conventional NK sits only at progenitor depth; (iii) SEPARATE PROGENITOR (Bozzano 2021; Sci Adv 2025 thymic; cILC1 route PMID 42054258) — no sharing with the conventional NK pool even at NKP depth. Three distinguishable depth signatures; the tool is doing real work, not confirming a tautology.

RECENCY CALIBRATION IS THE CRUX AND IS AVAILABLE. A shared mtDNA variant is informative only if progenitor-level origin can be excluded — Ruckert 2022 warns of precisely this ("mitochondrial mutations of conventional NK cells ... might instead be present already on the progenitor level"). The control is co-profiling autologous T/B/monocytes from the same draw: a variant also carried by unrelated lineages is progenitor-level; a variant private to NK and confined to a tight clone is recent. Feasibility precedent exists: PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) reconstructs cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour/tissue/blood; PMID 38253266 (Nature 2024) does deep mtDNA detection with joint state readout.

NOT A REVERSIBLE-STATE CLAIM (checked explicitly). The reversible-state exclusion does not fire here. The adaptive endpoint is a stably heritable epigenetic configuration (IFNG CNS1 demethylation, FCER1G/SYK/ZBTB16 silencing) that Ruckert 2022 shows persisting within the SAME mtDNA clonotypes over 7, 11 and 19 months; and Bjorkstrom 2011 reports the authors tested and could not induce NKG2C on NKG2C- cells. So it is not an oscillating state where both answers yield the same clonal structure.

DESIGN CONDITION (the honest limit). The barcode alone locates the branch point but does not ORIENT it: a recent clonotype containing both conventional and adaptive cells is equally consistent with A->B, B->A, and a bifurcating common parent. Direction requires the longitudinal form of the same primitive — which clonotype carried which phenotype at t1 versus t2. A single cross-sectional timepoint decides branch DEPTH only; the directional arrow needs repeat sampling across the infection/expansion. Decidable, but only in the longitudinal design.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = adaptive clones share recent, NK-private MRCAs with contemporaneous conventional NKG2C-/FcRg+ cells, and at the pre-expansion baseline the founder variant is carried by a phenotypically conventional cell.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: identify WHICH conventional NK cell is licensed to convert — a question the YES result poses and does not answer. Use the mtDNA clonotype as an index back into the baseline sample already in hand and read out the pre-conversion cell's own chromatin/surface state: CD56bright vs CD56dim, NKG2A+ vs KIR+, whether it is the CXXC5+ immature precursor nominated by PMC11686228 (Front Immunol 2024, which places an adaptive-NK precursor present at equal frequency in CMV+ and CMV- people), and critically whether KLRC2-locus accessibility or IFNG CNS1 demethylation is ALREADY partially present before infection (i.e. whether "conventional" founders are in fact pre-primed).

Then convert descriptive to prospective: from an HCMV-seronegative donor, FACS-sort the nominated precursor gate versus its complement, and challenge in the autologous HCMV-infected fibroblast/monocyte coculture system (Guma 2006 / Rolle 2014 PMC4348979) or a humanised-mouse HCMV model, scoring adaptive output by the NKG2C-INDEPENDENT signature so the readout does not depend on the receptor Liu 2016 showed to be dispensable. This is the sort-the-precursor experiment nobody has run: Phase A records that no study anywhere purified an NKG2C-depleted conventional population and followed it for acquisition of the adaptive phenotype.

TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (different from the NO branch): conversion being real makes "adaptive" a MANUFACTURABLE STATE rather than a donor property. ADAPT-NK (Blood Adv 2022, PMC9628692) currently screens CMV-seropositive "superdonors" for large pre-existing adaptive subpopulations; under YES that screening step is an inefficiency to be engineered away, and the induction protocol — which conventional subset plus which signal — becomes the defined development target.
b.action_if_no:
NO = adaptive clones' recent relatives are exclusively adaptive/NKG2C+; the MRCA with conventional NK appears only at progenitor depth (variant also present in autologous T/B/monocyte lineages); the pre-expansion baseline already carries the founder variant in an NKG2C+/adaptive-primed cell.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT — and it is not the YES experiment, because NO leaves TWO sub-hypotheses standing that this dataset cannot separate: (a) the founder is a mature but already-adaptive-primed cell inside the conventional NK developmental stream, versus (b) the founder descends from a SEPARATE progenitor branch. Separating them requires acquiring a compartment the YES branch never needs: bone marrow aspirate (CD34+ HSPC, CLP, NKP, stage 3-4 NK precursors) plus the circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursor of Bozzano 2021 (PMID 33493558) and circulating ILC1s (PMID 42054258), from the same individual, asking whether the adaptive founder clonotype maps to a progenitor branch distinct from the one feeding conventional NK. A positive result there promotes Bozzano 2021 / the Sci Adv 2025 thymic progenitor (PMID 40779632) from "alternative explanation" to "the actual origin".

SECOND, PROSPECTIVE AND QUANTITATIVE: if the founder pool pre-exists, its SIZE and CLONAL DIVERSITY before infection should predict the magnitude and clonal composition of the post-infection expansion. Testable in a D+/R- transplant cohort with banked baseline draws, and it already has a human precedent to confirm or refute — Bjorkstrom 2011 (PMC3023129) found CMV-IgG-negative hantavirus patients had low baseline NKG2C+ numbers and never expanded despite identical acute viral insult. That is a pre-registered, falsifiable prediction, not a conclusion.

TRANSLATIONAL CONSEQUENCE (opposite to YES): the problem stops being induction and becomes repertoire selection. Superdonor screening is then the correct irreducible design rather than a workaround, and the target shifts to identifying and sorting the founder pool in seronegative donors. Separately, the diagnostic use of NKG2C to call clonally restricted NK populations non-neoplastic (Mod Pathol 2026, PMID 41786213) rests on adaptive NK being a normal expansion of the conventional NK lineage and would need restating if the origin is a distinct progenitor.
b.both_answers_reason:
TRUE — the two branches are not the same experiment, and neither is vacuous. Tested against the three failure modes:

(1) SAME EXPERIMENT? No. YES stays in peripheral blood, looks BACKWARD into data already collected (index the clonotype into the archived baseline to profile the pre-conversion cell), then forward to an induction protocol. NO forces acquisition of a compartment YES never needs — bone marrow / progenitors — plus a prospective pool-size predictor in a transplant cohort. Different tissue, different assay, different analysis.

(2) ONE BRANCH VACUOUS? No. The YES branch is not "conversion is real, done": YES establishes THAT conversion happens and leaves entirely open WHICH conventional cell converts, which is the question with the manufacturing payoff. The NO branch is not "selection, as expected, move on": NO leaves two live sub-hypotheses (already-primed mature founder vs separate progenitor branch) that the same primitive can separate one level deeper in the tree, and it hands over a falsifiable quantitative prediction (baseline pool size/diversity gates expansion magnitude) with an existing human observation to test it against.

(3) DIVERGENT DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE? Yes, and they are opposite in direction: YES makes adaptive NK an inducible state and makes superdonor screening obsolete; NO makes it a selectable pre-existing repertoire, makes superdonor screening correct and irreducible, and puts a live question mark over the NKG2C-based benign/neoplastic diagnostic call.

ONE HONEST CAVEAT, recorded rather than suppressed: a third outcome is possible — MRCA depth unresolvable, i.e. shared variants that cannot be assigned to progenitor versus recent origin. Ruckert 2022 flags exactly this for the conventional NK compartment. That outcome is neither YES nor NO; it is a coverage/depth failure and is what the Phase C power thresholds (chrM coverage, informative-variant count, cells per donor per compartment) exist to catch in advance. It does not make either branch vacuous, but it is the most likely way this claim dies at Phase C rather than at Phase B.
b.compartments_needed:
CORE (all four required for the primary readout):
1. Peripheral blood CONVENTIONAL NK — CD3-CD14-CD19-CD56+ NKG2C- FcRg+ sort gate.
2. Peripheral blood ADAPTIVE NK — NKG2C+ AND, per Liu 2016, the NKG2C-independent adaptive gate (FcRg-/SYK-/CD57+/LILRB1+). Gating on NKG2C alone decides a narrower claim than the field holds.
3. Autologous NON-NK leukocytes from the SAME draw (T, B, monocytes). Not optional garnish — this is the progenitor-depth calibrator. Without it a shared mtDNA variant cannot be assigned to "recent conversion" versus "inherited from a common HSPC", and the whole readout is uninterpretable (Ruckert 2022's own stated caveat).
4. A PRE-EXPANSION TIMEPOINT from the SAME individual (baseline PBMC before primary HCMV infection or before reactivation). Required for the DIRECTIONAL claim only; the branch-depth version can be run cross-sectionally.

ADDITIONAL, ONLY IF THE ANSWER IS NO:
5. Bone marrow CD34+ HSPC / CLP / NKP / stage 3-4 NK precursors.
6. Circulating Lin-CD34+DNAM-1bright CXCR4+ precursors (Bozzano 2021) and circulating ILC1 (PMID 42054258) — both blood, so free.
7. Thymus (only to test the Sci Adv 2025 thymic-progenitor origin).
8. Secondary lymphoid organ NK (only to test the Blood 2025 "transitional precursor in SLO" model).
b.compartments_obtainable:
YES for the core, and this is the unusual case in this screen where the two compartments are both in blood.

Items 1-3 are three FACS gates on a SINGLE peripheral blood draw from one living human. No surgery, no post-mortem, no pregnancy, no mouse. Precedent that the paired sort plus mtDNA readout actually works on exactly these cells: Ruckert 2022 (PMC9663309) sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- NK 1:1 from the same donors and ran mtscATAC/ASAP-seq; PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) resolved cross-compartment mtDNA clonal relationships across 218,715 cells from matched tumour, tissue and blood in the same patients; PMID 39236287 tracked mtDNA-marked populations at 0.1-1% frequency in post-HSCT clinical samples.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT ACTUALLY BITES IS TIME, NOT TISSUE. Item 4 — the pre-expansion baseline — cannot be obtained opportunistically, because primary HCMV infection is unpredictable in healthy adults. It exists only where a baseline draw is banked by protocol: (a) D+/R- solid-organ transplant recipients (Lopez-Verges 2011's own design); (b) allo-HSCT/UCBT recipients with cryopreserved pre-transplant PBMC (precedent: PMC11686228, an MSKCC cohort of 267 HCT patients with protocolised weekly CMV monitoring from D14); (c) congenital/infant primary-infection cohorts. Of these, D+/R- SOT is the CLEAN one: in allo-HSCT the reconstituting NK cells arise de novo from grafted HSPC rather than from mature conventional NK, so the "A" being followed is a progenitor, not a conventional NK cell, and the arrow being tested silently changes. Lymphodepletion and immunosuppression are confounds in both.

Item 5 (bone marrow) requires an aspirate — invasive but routine, obtainable from the same living human, easiest in patients already undergoing marrow sampling or in HSCT donors. Item 6 is free (blood). Item 7 THYMUS IS SURGICAL-ONLY (paediatric cardiac surgery) and in practice cannot be paired with an adult blood adaptive compartment from the same individual. Item 8 SLO NK is SURGICAL OR POST-MORTEM/deceased-donor only. None of 7-8 is needed for the primary readout; both sit behind the NO branch.

UNVERIFIED FEASIBILITY ASSUMPTION, flagged rather than assumed: every banked baseline is cryopreserved, and mtscATAC-seq is a fixed-cell, intact-mitochondria protocol. The Nat Protoc method paper (PMID 36792778) covers primary haematopoietic cells and several cell-processing/flow workflows, but I did not confirm a validated cryopreserved-PBMC arm. Cryo-compatibility of the baseline samples must be verified at Phase C, not presumed.
b.compartment_notes:
MOUSE_ONLY = FALSE, on three independent grounds. (i) The claim text itself scopes this as HUMAN and explicitly excludes the Ly49H/MCMV homolog as a different transition. (ii) The mouse homolog has ALREADY been single-cell fate-mapped — Grassmann 2019 (PMID 31103380) and Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840, PMC8528403) transferred single retrogenic colour-barcoded Ly49H+ NK cells and read out clonal progeny — so a mouse run would re-occupy answered ground while answering a transition the claim disowns. (iii) Prereg 4.3: mtDNA barcoding is weak in young inbred mice, so the endogenous-barcode route is specifically a human strength here.

MACAQUE, considered and set aside. Truitt/Dunbar 2019 (PMID 31649681, PMC6794559) and PMC9808525 (2022, barcoded tissue NK across compartments) provide true lentiviral barcoding plus paired tissue compartments, but three things disqualify them for this arrow: the barcode tags the HSPC, so shared barcodes between conventional and adaptive NK prove common HSPC ancestry — the trivially-true answer, not mature-cell conversion; tissue compartments require necropsy; and RhCMV is not HCMV.

DEFINITIONAL NOTE THAT PROPAGATES INTO COMPARTMENT DESIGN: because NKG2C is dispensable (Liu 2016; Della Chiesa 2014; Goodier 2014), sorting compartment B on NKG2C alone would systematically miss the KLRC2-independent adaptive cells and could manufacture a spurious NO. The B gate must be the adaptive epigenetic/surface signature with NKG2C as one marker among several.

SAMPLE-ECONOMY NOTE: compartments 1, 2, 3 and 6 all come from one tube of blood, so the marginal cost of the NO-branch blood precursors is zero and they should be collected in the primary draw regardless of the expected answer — this is the one design choice that keeps both B2 branches live off a single collection.

o.already_traced_evidence:
TRUE for the primitive on this exact cell pair; NOT for the four-compartment calibrated directional design P1 specifies.

PRIMARY OCCUPANT — Ruckert et al., Nat Immunol 2022, PMID 36289449 / PMC9663309 (full text read at /home/user/aaa/refs/P1_PMC9663309.txt, methods verified, not read from abstract).
WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DID (from methods, lines 81/84/111 of the archived text): NK cells enriched from fresh blood by magnetic depletion of CD3/CD14/CD19, stained, then FACS-sorted as viable CD3-CD14-CD19-CD7+, split into NKG2C+ and NKG2C-, pooled 1:1, fixed, and run through mtscATAC-seq/ASAP-seq (plus parallel CITE-seq). mtDNA genotyping by mgatk (>=5x mt genome coverage, median 11-20x); variants filtered on >=3 cells, strand concordance >65%, VMR >0.01; clonotypes called by clustering on a mtDNA-allele-frequency neighbourhood graph. 4 HCMV+ and 3 HCMV- donors. Longitudinal re-draw of three HCMV+ donors at 7, 11 and 19 months.
WHAT THEY ADJUDICATED: (i) mtDNA clonotypes are significantly associated with adaptive NK subclusters (chi-square vs permuted clonotype-cluster matrix); (ii) the SAME association is absent in the conventional NK compartment and absent in HCMV- donors; (iii) clonotype-defining mutations and their subcluster assignment persist across the 7-19 month re-draw. So the adaptive compartment is oligoclonal, clone-stable, and epigenetically clone-inherited.
THEIR OWN STATED CAVEAT, verbatim from the results: conventional-NK mtDNA variants "do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level." That is precisely the progenitor-depth ambiguity P1's compartment 3 exists to resolve, and Ruckert could not resolve it because CD3/CD14/CD19 cells were depleted at the bench.
DIRECTIONALITY WAS INFERRED, NOT TRACED: they argue conventional origin from epigenetic residue only — adaptive subclusters split into two groups whose signatures correlate with CD56bright/early-CD56dim vs CD56dim maturation gradients, which they call "possibly reflecting the cell of origin," concluding naive NKG2C+ cells "might be recruited into the adaptive response at these different stages." No shared-clonotype test across the conventional/adaptive boundary is reported as the primary readout.

SECOND OCCUPANT, different primitive, and it DOES carry the calibrator — Corat, Schlums, Wu, Bryceson, Dunbar, Winkler, Blood 2017, PMID 27903532. Used naturally occurring somatic X-linked PIGA mutations in PNH patients as an endogenous HSPC-derived clonal mark (GPI-negative = descended from the mutant HSPC clone), and measured the GPI-negative fraction per compartment WITH autologous neutrophils and CD56bright NK as internal calibrators. Result: GPI-negative fraction in CD56dim NK is markedly lower than in neutrophils and CD56bright NK, most extreme in the PLZF-negative adaptive CD56dim population — i.e. the adaptive pool predates and is maintained independently of current HSPC output. This answers the branch-depth half of P1 with a real clonal marker and a real non-NK calibrator, four years before Ruckert.

Companion: Schlums et al., Blood 2017, PMID 28209719 — adaptive NK persist in GATA2 haploinsufficiency despite failing HSPC output. Same structural inference, no clonal marker.

BARCODE LINE (macaque, real integration-site barcodes): PMID 24702997 (Cell Stem Cell 2014, lentiviral barcoding shows NK have a distinct lineage origin from T/B/myeloid), PMID 30389798 (2018, clonal expansion and compartmentalised maintenance of macaque NK subsets), PMID 31649681 (Front Immunol 2019, CMV infection of CMV-naive barcoded macaques, explicitly the impact of CMV on NK clonal repertoire), PMID 36605190 (2022, tissue-resident NK clonal distribution).

MOUSE HOMOLOG (P1 correctly flags this as a different transition, but the structural question is answered there): PMID 31103380 (Grassmann, Immunity 2019, retrogenic colour-barcoding + single-cell adoptive transfer of Ly49H+ NK in MCMV) and PMID 34437840 (Flommersfeld, Immunity 2021, single-cell fate mapping showing TWO precursor lineages — a cNK-equivalent and an ILC1-like one — both feeding the adaptive-like MCMV response, diverging at the iNK stage). The mouse field has already used a genuine lineage tool to ask which precursor compartment the adaptive progeny are drawn from, and got a two-origin answer.

NOT occupancy, checked and excluded: PMID 39742279 (2024, CD56bright/adaptive "naive-memory relationship") is scRNA-seq + RNA velocity + flow on sorted populations from 2 donors — no clonal marker; its claim of "mitochondrial somatic mutations shared between Adaptive NK and CD56bright NK" is a discussion-level restatement of Ruckert, not new data. PMID 38484189 (Blood 2024) uses real CellTag lentiviral barcoding but in an in vitro OP9/cord-blood CD34+ system to separate NK from ILC3 — developmental, not HCMV, not adaptive. PMID 33493558 (Bozzano 2021), PMID 32930385 (CD57- NKG2C+ as putative precursors), PMID 38872000 (ENKP vs ILCP, mouse reporters) are phenotype/transfer arguments, not human clonal adjudication.
o.nearest_occupant:
PMID 36289449 — Ruckert T, et al. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022 (PMC9663309).

Same species (human), same virus (HCMV), same cell pair (NKG2C-/conventional vs NKG2C+/adaptive NK), same primitive (somatic mtDNA variants as endogenous barcodes read by mtscATAC/ASAP-seq). It is not merely adjacent — it is the same experiment class on the same claim.

FOUR CONCRETE DIFFERENCES, each traceable to a specific line of their methods or results:

1. NO AUTOLOGOUS NON-NK CALIBRATOR (P1 compartment 3). Their methods magnetically DEPLETE CD3, CD14 and CD19 cells before sorting, then sort CD3-CD14-CD19-CD7+. T cells, B cells and monocytes are physically removed from the input. Consequently a mtDNA variant shared between a conventional and an adaptive NK cell cannot be assigned to recent conversion versus inheritance from a common HSPC. They say so themselves: conventional-NK mtDNA variants "might instead be present already on the progenitor level." P1's entire compartment 3 is the fix for the gap Ruckert names.

2. NO PRE-EXPANSION BASELINE (P1 compartment 4). Their longitudinal arm is three HCMV+ donors re-drawn at 7, 11 and 19 months — both timepoints are chronic, post-expansion. It establishes clone STABILITY, not clone ORIGIN. No pre-seroconversion or pre-reactivation sample exists in the dataset, so the directional claim "conventional becomes adaptive" is never put to a temporal clonal test.

3. DIRECTION IS EPIGENETIC INFERENCE, NOT CLONAL TOPOLOGY. Their conventional-origin argument runs: adaptive subclusters split into two groups whose differential accessibility correlates with the CD56bright/early-CD56dim vs CD56dim axis, therefore "possibly reflecting the cell of origin." That is residue-of-state reasoning, exactly the kind of inference clonal barcoding is supposed to replace. The primary clonal statistic they report is clonotype-to-subcluster association WITHIN adaptive; the cross-boundary shared-ancestor test is not the reported readout, and their conventional-compartment result is a null.

4. NARROWER ADAPTIVE GATE THAN THE FIELD HOLDS (P1 compartment 2). The sort is NKG2C+/NKG2C-. FcRg is intracellular and appears only in their flow panel (anti-FcERI gamma-FITC), never in the ADT panel or the sort logic; SYK is absent entirely. Their ADT panel does carry CD57 and CD85j/ILT2, so the Liu-2016 adaptive gate is partially recoverable post hoc, but it was not a sort gate. They noticed the problem incidentally — donor P1 subcluster 4 "likely represents an NKG2C- adaptive NK cell expansion" — and did not pursue it. Gating on NKG2C alone decides a strictly narrower claim than P1 states.

NEAREST OCCUPANT THAT DOES HAVE THE CALIBRATOR: PMID 27903532 (Corat/Winkler, Blood 2017). It carries autologous neutrophils and CD56bright NK as internal clonal-depth references and answers the branch-depth half — the adaptive CD56dim/PLZF-negative pool is maintained independently of current HSPC output. It differs by being (a) bulk flow-percentage resolution of GPI-negativity per subset, not cell-by-cell shared-ancestor resolution, (b) restricted to PNH patients, a disease context with a clonally distorted HSPC pool, (c) blind to the conventional-NK-to-adaptive-NK step itself — PIGA marks HSPC descent, not intra-NK conversion, and (d) predating any NKG2C-independent adaptive gate.

The residual unoccupied space is therefore narrow and specific: the calibrated, directional version of the question. Nobody has run mtDNA clonal tracing on conventional NK + adaptive NK + autologous T/B/monocytes from one draw, and nobody has a pre-expansion clonal baseline.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
G4 applies — P1 invokes differentiation, plasticity and memory. All three neighbouring fields have answered the same structural question with lineage tools, and in two of them the answer is settled.

T CELL FIELD — FULLY OCCUPIED, AND THIS IS WHERE THE METHOD WAS BORROWED FROM. "Is compartment B the progeny of compartment A" is decided routinely in T cells by the rearranged TCR, a perfect native heritable barcode: clonotype sharing between naive and memory compartments is measured directly (naive CD4/CD8 share ~5% and ~3.5% of TCRbeta clonotypes with their memory counterparts; overlap scales with clonotype frequency), and TCR-based clonal tracking maps permitted transitions between effector/memory subsets by ontogeny versus interconversion. The NK field's whole predicament is the absence of this native barcode, which is exactly why mtDNA is pressed into service as the surrogate. So P1 is not proposing a novel structural question — it is proposing to import the T cell field's settled question into a lineage that lacks the T cell field's barcode. Ruckert's own discussion makes the borrowing explicit ("As T cells can also clonally inherit transcriptional and epigenetic diversity...").

MYELOID FIELD — NOW OCCUPIED WITH THE IDENTICAL METHOD AND A BETTER COMPARTMENT DESIGN. Mitotrek, Cancer Cell 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.07.16.665245; PMC12330704): mtDNA variants + scATAC jointly profiled in 218,715 cells from MATCHED tumour, non-involved tissue and peripheral blood of lung and ovarian cancer patients. It answers precisely "is the tissue compartment the recent progeny of the circulating compartment" — concluding intratumoral DC3 arise from circulating monocytes and that a monocyte's tumour fate is programmed peripherally, before tissue entry. That is P1's structural question, with P1's primitive, executed with the paired-compartment design P1 asks for. It also touched NK: expanded NK clones were seen in non-involved lung and blood, framed by the authors as "consistent with previous reports of adaptive-like, oligoclonal NK cell responses in human cytomegalovirus infection," and tumour-restricted NK clones absent from matched blood. It did NOT stratify HCMV serostatus, did NOT gate NKG2C or the adaptive phenotype, and did NOT use T/B cells as clonal-depth calibrators (it benchmarked against published HSC colony data instead). So the myeloid field owns the template; the HCMV/adaptive-NK application of it remains open.

ILC FIELD — OCCUPIED IN MOUSE. RORgt, T-bet, Hobit and PLZF fate-map reporters plus adoptive transfer have adjudicated ILC3-to-ILC1 conversion and the cNK/ILC1 lineage split; PLZF-reporter work showed ILC1 developmental stages overlapping those previously ascribed to cNK. PMID 38872000 (Nat Immunol 2024) used marker/reporter-defined origins to split mouse NK into ENKP-derived and ILCP-derived pathways, and found Ly49H+ MCMV-responding NK come predominantly from ENKPs. Most pointedly, PMID 34437840 (Flommersfeld, Immunity 2021) fate-mapped SINGLE NK cells through MCMV and found the adaptive-like response is fed by TWO distinct precursor lineages (cNK-equivalent and ILC1-like) that diverge at the iNK stage. So the mouse group-1 ILC field has already run P1's structural question with a true lineage tool and returned a non-unitary answer — which is a live warning that the human single-origin framing of P1 may be answering the wrong shape of question.

NET: the question shape is occupied in three neighbouring fields; the human HCMV/NKG2C instantiation is occupied by Ruckert 2022 minus the calibrator and minus the baseline.

b.why:
This is the rubric's second bullet ("A becomes functionally B-like") in its purest form, compounded by the fourth (reversible/graded state within one lineage). Four independent reasons, in order of force.

(1) B HAS NO LINEAGE-INDEPENDENT DEFINITION. "CIML NK" is scored by one thing only: enhanced IFN-gamma on restimulation. Cooper 2009 (PMC2644138) shows the cells are phenotypically indistinguishable from IL-15-only controls across CD69, CD11b, CD11c, gp49B, B220, CD122, IL-15Ralpha, IL-12Rbeta1 and CD127, are granzyme-B NEGATIVE, and kill YAC-1 no better ("all 4 groups of NK cells exhibited similar cytotoxicity"). So B is co-extensive with the assay used to define it. The barcoding primitive returns ancestry, not function; something else must still call a cell "B", and once the recall assay has called it, the barcode has added nothing to the claim's arrow.

(2) THE CONVERSION STEP INVOLVES NO CELL DIVISION, SO IT WRITES NOTHING INTO THE GENEALOGY. The protocol is 13-16 h. Cooper 2009 Fig 4 is explicit that generation-0 (never-divided) preactivated cells make as much IFN-gamma as generations 1-3. Lineage structure is created by division. A transformation that occurs without division leaves the clonal tree of the population IDENTICAL before and after — under the conversion model AND under the selection model. "Do these two cells share an ancestor, and how recently" returns the same answer either way. There is no lineage signal to read because none was generated.

(3) A AND B ARE UNCONTESTEDLY THE SAME LINEAGE. Nobody in this literature proposes that CIML NK cells are non-NK-derived; Keppel 2013 already excluded de novo endogenous NK development with Rag2-/-gc-/- hosts. The only lineage question with a live disagreement — donor vs host — is a two-population question already settled by CD45.1/CD45.2 congenics in mouse, which needs no clonal resolution at all.

(4) THE REAL DISPUTE (SELECTION vs CONVERSION) IS NOT A CLONAL QUESTION. The hypothesized pre-existing responsive compartment is a DIFFERENTIATION STAGE — CD56bright/NKG2A+/CD57-/KIR- in Romee 2012's own marker correlations, CD27hi in mouse — not a clone. Its members are distributed across clonotypes. So "selection of that subset" and "conversion of everything" both predict a broad, essentially unbiased clonotype draw. Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is exactly the rubric's disqualifying condition. Add that the state is reversible and dose/duration-graded (5 h gives a weaker effect than overnight; Keppel 2013 concedes in print it "could represent a residual priming effect, rather than a memory-like response"), so "converted then decayed" and "never converted" are also clonally identical.

STRONGEST COUNTER-CONSIDERATION, AND WHY IT DOES NOT RESCUE DECIDABILITY. There is one genuinely lineage-shaped design: barcode a proliferating NK pool, split sibling cells into preactivation vs control, and ask whether recall competence is concordant within a barcode (clone-intrinsic, i.e. pre-existing) or uncorrelated (induced). That is the primitive used correctly. But it requires clones with multiple members, which requires 10-14 days of feeder/IL-2 expansion at 300-450 fold to manufacture — precisely what Allan/Dunbar 2023 (PMID 36699615, PMC9842935) did in barcoded rhesus macaques, finding correlated clone-intrinsic proliferative behaviour across two feeder conditions (Pearson r 0.52-0.67). Running that design replaces the claim's 16 h no-division protocol with a fortnight of driven proliferation, i.e. you must change the biology to make it lineage-legible. It answers a different claim.
b.why_secondary: Note also that the human in vivo arm fails for a second, independent reason recorded in Phase A: in the post-HCT setting the reconstituting NK compartment is HLA-matched to the infused product (Berrien-Elliott 2022, PMID 35196021; Bednarski 2022, PMID 34871371), and Shapiro 2022 (PMID 35349491) states outright that "there was no traceable marker in the infused CIML NK cells." That is an identifiability failure inside compartment B, not a decidability failure of lineage per se — but it means the clinically load-bearing setting cannot even score which cells are the product.
b.action_if_yes:
Framing the most charitable decidable version: barcode or mtDNA-clonotype (mtscATAC-seq / MAESTER) the input NK pool, apply 16 h IL-12/IL-15/IL-18, and ask whether the recall-competent cells at d7-21 are clonally BROAD (an unrestricted draw from the input) — the YES / "they ARE clonally related to the bulk repertoire" branch.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT IF YES: not a lineage experiment. It is a prospective-sorting functional experiment that requires no lineage information whatsoever — FACS-sort the candidate pre-existing compartments from the SAME donor (human: CD56bright vs CD56dim; NKG2A+CD57-KIR- vs CD57+KIR+; mouse: CD27hi vs CD11bhi), preactivate each fraction separately with IL-12/15/18, rest, and measure recall IFN-gamma per sorted fraction. You are forced into this because a broad clonal draw is equally predicted by the selection model (see B1 point 4): the responsive compartment is a differentiation stage spread across clonotypes, so clonal breadth does not license "conversion."

AND THIS ANSWER IS ALREADY EFFECTIVELY IN HAND. Allan/Dunbar 2023 (PMID 36699615, PMC9842935) barcode-tracked rhesus NK cells through clinical-grade feeder/IL-2 activation-expansion — the closest existing system — and got the YES outcome: Shannon diversity preserved across culture, >50% (53-71%) of starting barcodes still detected at day 14-15, >80% of clones within 4-fold of their initial frequency despite 300-450-fold total expansion, and no dominant clone lost. The field's next move after that result was not another lineage experiment. That is the empirical demonstration that the YES branch terminates.

FOR EVERY DOWNSTREAM DEPENDENCY, YES CHANGES NOTHING: the 16 h bulk-preactivation manufacturing step, the cell dose, the Flu/Cy conditioning, the IL-2 / N-803 support, and the trial designs (Romee 2016 NCT01898793; Bednarski 2022; Gang 2020 CD19-CAR-ML-NK; WU-NK-101; the 2025 HNSCC N-803 trial) all stay exactly as they are. This is the textbook "we would conclude conversion is compatible and move on" branch.
b.action_if_no:
NO branch: the recall-competent output is clonally RESTRICTED — a real bottleneck, in which a minority of input clonotypes dominates the d7-21 recall-competent pool and Shannon diversity collapses.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT IF NO: recover what distinguishes the surviving clonotypes — i.e. go back and determine their PRE-preactivation surface/transcriptional phenotype, sort that fraction prospectively, preactivate it, and compare product potency head-to-head against the bulk-preactivated product.

That is the same prospective-sorting experiment as the YES branch. The lineage result would only have told you to run it; the sort itself, and the phenotype it identifies, is what carries all the information. Worse, the NO branch is reachable more cheaply without any lineage tool at all: Shapiro 2022 (PMID 35349491, PMC9151697) already observed the phenotypic signature of exactly this bottleneck — "Patients 3 and 4 both exhibited a dominance of NK clusters on day +28 and day +60 that constituted a minor portion of the infusion product" — from plain high-dimensional phenotyping, and Terren 2023 (PMID 37575238) independently supplies the mechanism (IL-12/15/18 stimulation itself decreases NK viability, making preactivation a survival filter). So the NO answer is already available by a route that does not need the primitive.
b.both_answers_reason:
OUT, on three separate grounds, any one of which is sufficient under a strict reading.

(1) THE TWO BRANCHES CONVERGE ON THE IDENTICAL NEXT EXPERIMENT. Both YES and NO terminate in: prospectively sort the candidate pre-existing compartments (CD56bright/CD56dim; NKG2A+CD57-KIR-/CD57+KIR+; mouse CD27hi/CD11bhi), preactivate each separately, assay recall IFN-gamma. That experiment requires no lineage information, uses one apheresis from one donor, and can be run today. When the next experiment is the same regardless of the answer, the answer is not doing work.

(2) THE YES BRANCH IS VACUOUS. Nothing downstream moves. Manufacturing (16 h bulk preactivation), dose, conditioning, cytokine support and trial design are unchanged across every dependency Phase A enumerated. It is precisely "we would conclude conversion is compatible and move on."

(3) BOTH BRANCHES ARE ALREADY OCCUPIED BY CHEAPER, NON-LINEAGE ROUTES. The YES outcome has been obtained in the nearest existing system (Allan/Dunbar 2023, PMID 36699615: diversity preserved, >50% of barcodes retained, >80% of clones within 4-fold, and no lineage follow-up ensued). The NO outcome has been obtained phenotypically (Shapiro 2022, PMID 35349491: minor infusion-product clusters dominating at d+28/+60), with a mechanism already supplied (Terren 2023, PMID 37575238). An experiment whose both outcomes have published non-lineage precedents cannot be the decisive one.

CROSS-FIELD CHECK (G4): the T-cell field answered this exact structural question — "is the memory fate selected from pre-committed precursors or induced in cells that could have gone either way?" — with single-cell fate mapping and barcoding a decade ago, and it did NOT resolve into a clean selection-vs-conversion verdict: Buchholz et al., Science 2013 (PMID 23493420, "Disparate individual fates compose robust CD8+ T cell immunity") and Gerlach et al., Science 2013 (PMID 23493421, "Heterogeneous differentiation patterns of individual CD8+ T cells") both found individual naive cells produce heterogeneous fate distributions, so the population-level answer is robust while the single-cell answer is stochastic. The borrowed mechanism's occupancy lives in the field it was borrowed from, and there the definitive lineage answer turned out to be "both, per cell, probabilistically" — which is the outcome that would make the P2 version least actionable of all. Note also that the T-cell precedent had something P2 lacks: an antigen receptor that is itself a clonal marker and a fate (effector vs memory) with lineage-independent surface definitions. NK cells have neither, as Allan/Dunbar 2023 state directly: clonal tracking "cannot be performed" via rearranged TCR/BCR segments in NK cells.
b.compartments_needed:
Compartment A = resting/unmanipulated NK cells. Compartment B = memory-like (recall-competent) NK cells. Enumerated by setting:

HUMAN IN VITRO (where the claimed arrow actually lives — Phase A: INF_INVITRO):
A1. Resting peripheral blood or apheresis NK cells, pre-preactivation (RosetteSep/FACS-purified CD56+CD3-).
B1. The same donor's NK cells at 16 h after rhIL-12 10 + rhIL-18 50 + rhIL-15 1 ng/mL.
B2. The same donor's cells after 7/14/21 d rest in 1 ng/mL IL-15, plus the paired IL-15-only control arm.

HUMAN IN VIVO (where the clinical weight sits):
B3. Recipient peripheral blood post-infusion, serial d1/3/7/8/14/21/30/60/100.
B4. Recipient bone marrow post-infusion, d8/14/30/60/100.
B5. Solid-tumor-infiltrating ML NK (the 2025 HNSCC N-803 trial setting).
A2. The matched haploidentical DONOR's pre-manufacture apheresis NK cells (the only true "A" for B3-B5 — note it is a different individual from the one B is sampled from).

MOUSE:
A3. Splenic NK from Rag1-/- or congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 donors, pre-preactivation.
B6. Donor-derived NK recovered from recipient spleen, liver, bone marrow and lung at d1/3/7/21 and out to 3-4 months.

RHESUS (the only barcoded in vivo NK system): A4/B7 = pre- and post-culture NK from barcode-transduced-HSPC-transplanted animals, with concurrently isolated monocytes as the required non-expanded reference lineage (Allan/Dunbar 2023).
b.compartments_obtainable:
YES for everything that matters in vitro — and that is exactly why compartment access is NOT this claim's binding constraint, and why the claim still fails.

FREELY PAIRED FROM ONE HUMAN, NON-INVASIVELY: A1, B1 and B2 are literally the same donor's cells in the same tube at successive timepoints, from a single blood draw or apheresis. There is no anatomical separation between A and B, no second individual, no surgery, no post-mortem requirement. The two compartments are as paired as any in this entire screen.

MOUSE: A3 and B6 are freely paired within one animal across spleen/liver/BM/lung, with CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic hosts already established (Keppel 2013, Ni 2012). B6 is post-mortem, but that is unlimited and cheap.

RHESUS: A4/B7 obtainable and already collected (Allan/Dunbar 2023) — serial peripheral blood from long-term barcoded animals, 41-76 months post-transplant, with paired monocyte reference.

CONSTRAINED: B3 (recipient blood) is obtainable serially but ONLY inside an active clinical trial in a lymphodepleted or transplanted patient — it does not exist in a healthy volunteer, so the human in vivo B compartment is trial-only by construction. B4 (marrow) is obtainable only by protocol-scheduled aspirate, invasive. B5 (tumor ML NK) requires a surgical or dedicated research biopsy. A2 is obtainable but comes from a DIFFERENT PERSON than B3-B5, so the human in vivo arm can never be truly same-individual paired.

The verdict: the compartments are obtainable, the pairing is easy, and the claim still cannot be adjudicated by lineage. The obstacle sits entirely in B1/B2 (no lineage-independent definition of B; no division to write ancestry), not in B3.
b.compartment_notes:
Four notes that matter more than the access question itself.

(1) A HARD, ACCESS-INDEPENDENT CONSTRAINT. The assay that DEFINES compartment B — restimulation followed by intracellular IFN-gamma staining — is destructive. The one pairing that would settle the claim, the same individual cell before and after preactivation, is therefore physically impossible no matter how good the tissue access is. The only workaround is a live IFN-gamma secretion-capture sort, which itself perturbs the cell. No amount of compartment availability fixes this.

(2) THE COMPARTMENTS ARE NOT SEPARATED, WHICH IS THE PROBLEM, NOT A CONVENIENCE. Lineage adjudication earns its keep when A and B sit in different places and you ask whether one seeded the other. Here A and B are the same cells in the same dish 16 hours apart. There is no spatial or temporal gap for ancestry to bridge.

(3) COMPARTMENT B IS OBTAINABLE BUT NOT IDENTIFIABLE IN THE SETTING THAT CARRIES THE CLINICAL WEIGHT. Post-HCT, the reconstituting NK compartment is HLA-matched to the infused ML product, so the anti-HLA mAb readout used in Romee 2016 fails (Berrien-Elliott 2022, PMID 35196021; Bednarski 2022, PMID 34871371, which identifies "persisting ML NK cells" purely by viSNE clustering on CD56-hi/NKG2A/CD62L). Shapiro 2022 (PMID 35349491) says it plainly: "there was no traceable marker in the infused CIML NK cells, it was not possible to use donor chimerism or other direct means to track the infused NK cells." You can draw the blood; you cannot tell which cells are the product.

(4) MAKING THE SYSTEM LINEAGE-LEGIBLE DESTROYS THE CLAIM. NK cells carry no rearranged receptor, so clonal tracking needs either transduction (which needs proliferation) or mtDNA heteroplasmy (which marks HSC-level families fixed decades earlier and is therefore uninformative about a 16 h state change). Generating clones with members to compare requires the 10-14 day feeder/IL-2 expansion of Allan/Dunbar 2023 — replacing the claim's no-division protocol with a fortnight of driven proliferation. The claim as stated is only testable by lineage after you have stopped testing the claim as stated.

o.already_traced_evidence:
PARTIALLY OCCUPIED — the human IN VIVO half of the arrow has already been adjudicated with a true clonal method; the human IN VITRO half (A1 -> B1/B2, where Phase A located the claim) has not.

DIRECT OCCUPANT (in vivo, compartments A2 -> B3): Shapiro RM, Birch G, Weng C, Gudera J, Poeschla M, Booker M, Tolstorukov M, Sheffer M, Dulery R, Nikiforow S, Koreth J, Wu CJ, Soiffer R, Ritz J, Sankaran VG, Romee R. "Development of a novel multiomic sequencing approach to characterize infused donor memory-like NK cells in an immune compatible environment." Blood (2025) 146(Suppl 1):2352 [ASH 2025 abstract; NO PMID — conference abstract only, not indexed in PubMed]. What they did, verbatim from the abstract: applied ReDeeM (Regulatory multiomics with Deep Mitochondrial profiling; the Weng/Sankaran mtDNA-mutation lineage-tracing platform, method paper PMID 38253266 / validation PMID 39229039) to longitudinally collected cryopreserved PBMC from trial NCT04024761 (donor CIML mem-NK infused for MDS/AML relapse after HCT), 3 timepoints x 4 donor-recipient pairs, sorted CD3-/CD56+. Stated motivation is exactly the compartment problem in this claim: "the absence of a robust methodology to track mem-NK cells following their infusion into a genetically identical milieu and in the absence of a donor-specific marker after HCT." Stated result: "the mtDNA-derived clonal repertoire suggested polyclonal NK cell expansion following infusion in all recipients, originating from both the infused mem-NK cells and the reconstituting endogenous stem cell compartment after lymphodepletion," plus day+21 ATAC enrichment for leukocyte activation and type I IFN genes (IFI6, IFITM3) vs screening NK. That is the "are these cells the clonal progeny of the infused preactivated product, or of the recipient's reconstituting HSPC pool?" question, asked and answered with clonal marks.

CAVEAT ON THIS OCCUPANT (important for the parent's decision): I could NOT retrieve the abstract text directly — ashpublications.org and sciencedirect.com both returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch. The methods/results sentences above are reconstructed from two independent search-engine renderings of the same abstract, which agreed. There is no peer-reviewed full paper yet (PubMed search for Shapiro/Birch/Romee + mem-NK + mitochondrial returns nothing beyond the 2022 JCI trial paper). n=4 pairs, 3 timepoints, blood only — no marrow (B4), no tumor (B5), no pre-manufacture donor apheresis baseline described.

WHAT IS STILL UNTRACED: (i) the in vitro arrow A1 -> B1 -> B2 (paired resting vs 16h IL-12/15/18 vs 7/14/21d rested, same donor, IL-15-only control) — no clonal/barcode/mtDNA study found; (ii) whether ML NK are the clonal progeny of the whole resting repertoire vs. selective outgrowth of pre-existing clones — Foltz JA et al. Sci Immunol 2024 (PMID 38941480) asked precisely this precursor->product question (eML-1 from CD56bright, eML-2 from CD56dim) but with SORTED-SUBSET pre-culture + CITE-seq/ATAC readout, i.e. population-level, not clonal; (iii) mouse: Cooper 2009-lineage congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 transfer of IL-12/15/18-preactivated NK establishes donor origin at population level only — no barcode/Polylox/Confetti/CRISPR-recorder study of preactivated NK found; (iv) rhesus: the barcoded macaque NK system has never been run with an IL-12/15/18 preactivation arm.

WHY THE FLAG IS TRUE RATHER THAN FALSE: the field's own leaders have already built and deployed the exact clonal tool against the exact clinical compartment named in this claim (B3 vs A2), reported the answer, and the answer is "polyclonal, mixed origin." Anyone proposing this claim now is entering a room that Romee/Sankaran/Wu are already standing in, roughly one publication cycle ahead.

PMID 36289449. mtscATAC-seq + somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous barcodes on ex vivo human NK from HCMV+/HCMV- donors; demonstrated substantial clonal expansion of adaptive NK, clone-specific accessible chromatin, and stable clonal inheritance of epigenetic state over time (repeat sampling). DIFFERENCE: the memory here is HCMV/NKG2C-driven adaptive NK arising in vivo over years, NOT IL-12/15/18 cytokine-induced ML NK; no cytokine preactivation, no recall assay, no adoptive transfer. It is however the single strongest demonstration that the "is NK memory clonal and is the state clonally heritable?" question is answerable with mtDNA in humans — i.e. the method-plus-question pairing is already published, just on a different inducing stimulus.

3. Allan DSJ, Wu C, Mortlock RD, Chakraborty M, Rezvani K, Davidson-Moncada JK, Dunbar CE, Childs RW. Mol Ther Oncolytics 2023;28:74-87. PMID 36699615 (full text read: /home/user/aaa/refs/P2_PMC9842935.txt). Lentivirally barcoded rhesus HSPC transplant recipients; NK sorted and expanded ex vivo with irradiated LCL or K562-41BBL/mbIL-21 feeders + IL-2; barcode repertoires compared pre/post culture, and "putative memory-like" clones defined operationally as clones already expanded in vivo in CD16+ NK relative to concurrent monocytes (and independently expanded 8-12 months earlier). Result: >50% of starting repertoire retained at d14, Shannon diversity preserved, pre-expanded "memory-like" clones = mean 31% of the product and still proliferative but less so than non-expanded clones. DIFFERENCE: feeder + IL-2 expansion, NOT IL-12/15/18 preactivation; "memory-like" is a proxy label for prior in vivo clonal expansion (CMV/adaptive), never validated by a recall assay; the question asked is "does manufacture distort the repertoire," not "are ML NK the progeny of resting NK."

4. Wu C, ... Bryceson YT, Dunbar CE. Sci Immunol 2018;3:eaat9781. PMID 30389798. Barcoded rhesus; CD56-CD16+ NK are oligoclonal, KIR-segregated, and remain clonally UNCOUPLED from CD56+CD16- NK and from other lineages for >4 years, surviving anti-CD16 depletion/regeneration; only profound sustained IL-15-mediated depletion generated new clones. DIFFERENCE: this is the homeostatic subset-vs-lineage question, not cytokine preactivation. Structurally it is the closest published precedent for using barcodes to decide "is NK phenotype X a state of one lineage or a separate self-renewing compartment" — the same logical move this claim would make.

Blood 2017;129:1940-1946, PMID 27903532 (PIGA-mutant PNH clones used as endogenous marks: adaptive NK maintained long term independent of HSPC input) and Schlums H et al. Blood 2017;129:1927-1939, PMID 28209719 (adaptive NK persist in GATA2 patients depleted of stem/progenitors). DIFFERENCE: population-level genetic marks, not single-cell clonal; adaptive/CMV NK, not CIML.

These two papers are the reason the ReDeeM abstract exists.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
YES — heavily occupied, and in the field this claim borrows from.

MYELOID (the closest structural analogue, and it is now settled): Liu VV, Sandor K, ... Ludwig LS, Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44:1509-1521.e4, PMID 42242233 (preprint bioRxiv 2025.07.16.665245, PMID 40777278). mtscATAC-seq mtDNA clonal tracing of 218,715 cells from MATCHED tumor + adjacent tissue + blood in lung and ovarian cancer patients. They resolved that TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and further identified DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones whose circulating precursors already carry distinct epigenetic profiles — i.e. "intratumoral differentiation fate may be peripherally programmed before infiltration." That is exactly the structural question P2 wants to ask (does a stimulus create the effector state de novo from the general precursor pool, or does it select clones already committed?), asked in the same species, with the same tool, on paired blood/tissue, and answered. The trained-immunity/myeloid field got there first.

T CELL: the "one lineage, many states" version was settled long ago by single-cell fate mapping, and the modern clonal-plus-state version is standard practice — e.g. Pai JA et al. Cancer Cell 2023;41:776-790.e7, PMID 37001526 (TCR lineage tracing of clonal progenitors and long-term persistence of tumor-specific T cells under ICB); Weng C et al. Nature 2024;627:389-398, PMID 38253266 (ReDeeM: mtDNA genealogies coupled to cell state across human hematopoiesis, the platform later pointed at mem-NK). Ludwig 2019 (PMID 30827679), Lareau 2021 (PMID 32788668), Miller 2022 MAESTER (PMID 35210612) are the enabling toolchain, all validated on human lymphocytes.

ILC / INNATE LYMPHOID: Flommersfeld S et al. Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304, PMID 34437840 — single-cell FATE MAPPING of individual NK cells identified a type-1-ILC-like lineage bridging innate and adaptive recognition of MCMV, i.e. the field has already used clonal tools to decide "distinct lineage vs. state" for a memory-associated NK population. Wethington D, ... Grassmann S, Adams NM, Sun JC, Lanier LL, Das J, bioRxiv 2025, PMID 40060511 — single-cell/clonal quantification showing MCMV-response clonal heterogeneity is generated by mature subsets of differing proliferative ability, not by differentiation rate changes; Grassmann S et al. Immunity 2019, PMID 31103380 — Ly49H surface density drives differential clonal expansion. All of these are the "is the memory clone a pre-existing high-responder or a newly instructed cell" question, answered clonally, in NK, in mouse.

NET: for the borrowed mechanism (a stimulus produces a durable "memory/trained" effector state), the myeloid field has the human paired-compartment mtDNA answer (PMID 42242233), the T cell field has the canonical clonal answer, and the NK/MCMV field has the mouse single-cell fate-map answer (PMID 34437840, 40060511). The only genuinely unoccupied slice left for P2 is the IL-12/15/18 in vitro preactivation arrow itself (A1 -> B1/B2 with paired IL-15-only control), and the marrow/tumor compartments (B4/B5) in vivo.
