b.why:
FALSE on four independent grounds, any one of which is sufficient.

(1) WRONG PREDICATE. The claim's predicate is a function — % specific 51Cr release on 721.221/K562, % conjugates with polarized MTOC and perforin at 20 min, CD107a exposure. The primitive returns shared-ancestry and nothing else. This is verbatim the "A becomes functionally B-like" form that prereg 3 fixes as not decidable. Phase A already recorded is_lineage_claim=FALSE: no clone, barcode, congenic marker, transfer, fate map or recorder appears anywhere in Kopcow 2005, Verma 2000, Tokmadzic 2002, El Costa 2008 or Siewiera 2013.

(2) THE ANSWER IS FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, SO IT CANNOT COVARY WITH THE CLAIM. The two things compared are one bead-purified dNK population at t=0 and the same dish at 36 h. They are trivially co-lineal — one prep, one tube. The primitive's output is known before the experiment is run, so it carries zero information about whether the claim is true. A test whose result is determined by the sampling scheme rather than by the hypothesis is not a test.

(3) REVERSIBLE STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE — the decisive point. Cytotoxic competence here is an environmentally-set, reversible functional state, and Kopcow's own Discussion says so verbatim: "the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment." At least three mutually exclusive readings — (a) IL-15 induces the state, (b) leaving the decidua de-represses it, (c) it was never absent (El Costa 2008 PMID 18713971: fresh uncultured dNK lyse after NKp46 crosslinking; Siewiera 2013 PMID 23592985: fresh dNK kill autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts) — all produce the IDENTICAL clonal structure. Every truth-value of the claim maps to the same barcode distribution, so the barcode distribution cannot discriminate among them. That is the definition of not decidable.

(4) OPERATIONAL DEGENERACY. Over the 12-36 h window purified dNK essentially do not divide, so no two cells acquire a shared recent ancestor during the experiment; the primitive collapses to per-cell tagging and returns "no shared ancestor" for every pair whether or not the claim holds. Extending culture until clones do arise substitutes a different experiment, since long culture is itself the confound being adjudicated. Compounding this, barcoding primary human NK requires activating transduction culture (cf. barcoded lentiviral NK delivery, PMID 40621477), which imposes the exact ex vivo perturbation at issue — the instrument creates the artefact it is meant to measure.

The one sub-question lineage could in principle touch — selection of a pre-existing competent minority versus conversion of each cell — is NOT the claim as written, and would additionally require functionally phenotyping the ancestor, which the chromium-release assay consumes.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = the cytotoxic, MTOC/perforin-polarizing dNK present at 36 h carry clonal marks spanning the full t=0 input repertoire, including marks on cells that were non-cytotoxic at input — i.e. conversion within clones, not outgrowth.

Very next experiment: take ONE first-trimester decidual prep and split it three ways — (i) t=0 fresh, (ii) 36 h + 12 ng/ml IL-15, (iii) 36 h medium-only (RPMI-1640 + 10% FCS, no cytokine) — then re-run the identical Kopcow readouts on all three arms: 4 h 51Cr release on 721.221 and K562 across graded E:T, and % conjugates with polarized MTOC (alpha/gamma-tubulin) and perforin granules at 20 min, >=50 conjugates per slide. Add what Kopcow never reported: post-culture viability, absolute recovered cell count, and CTV dilution. Layer on IL-15 dose-response and IL-15Ra blockade. Run >=5 donors with donor-level statistics rather than a representative figure.

Note what this experiment is: the missing no-cytokine arm. No barcode is read anywhere in it. It is the only thing that separates "IL-15 signals a state change" from "36 h out of the decidua plus recovery from collagenase digestion and bead handling."
b.action_if_no:
NO = the 36 h cytotoxic pool derives from a restricted set of clones absent from, or rare in, the non-cytotoxic t=0 input — selection and outgrowth of an already-competent minority rather than conversion.

Very next experiment: take ONE first-trimester decidual prep and split it three ways — (i) t=0 fresh, (ii) 36 h + IL-15, (iii) 36 h medium-only — and re-run 51Cr release, CD107a, and MTOC/perforin polarization on all three, with post-culture viability, absolute recovered count and CTV dilution, to establish whether the competent minority merely survives preferentially or actually expands, and whether it does so without cytokine. Then, as the branch-specific tail, prospectively sort the candidate minority from FRESH tissue (residual CD16-lo cells surviving the CD3/CD16 depletion, NKp46-hi, granzyme-B-hi surrogate) and assay it uncultured against the same targets.
b.both_answers_reason:
FAILS, and fails hard. The very next bench action is word-for-word identical on both branches: split one prep into t=0 / 36 h + IL-15 / 36 h medium-only and re-run lysis plus polarization with viability, absolute counts and CTV dilution. That is the same three-arm culture on both sides. It needs no lineage tool, costs one extra well, and was available in 2005. The lineage answer changes nothing about which experiment is run next — it changes only the sentence written afterwards, which is precisely the vacuity B2 is built to catch.

Three aggravating factors, each independently damning:

(a) THE NO BRANCH IS NEAR-VACUOUS IN THIS SYSTEM. With essentially no division in 12-36 h, "not clonally related" is the default output for every cell pair regardless of the claim's truth. A NO is what a dead-null experiment returns, so it cannot be evidence for selection.

(b) THE ONLY DIVERGENT TAIL DOES NOT NEED LINEAGE. Sorting a prospectively-marked competent minority is reachable directly; CTV dilution plus absolute recovered counts already separate outgrowth from conversion at a fraction of the cost and without transducing the cells. Lineage is not load-bearing on either branch.

(c) THE CLAIM'S PREMISE IS CONTESTED BY CHEAPER ASSAYS ALREADY ON THE RECORD. El Costa 2008 (fresh dNK lyse after NKp46 crosslinking, no culture, no cytokine) and Siewiera 2013 (fresh dNK kill autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts) both say fresh dNK kill when given the right receptor engagement or the right target. The informative next move is therefore a target-and-receptor-choice experiment on fresh cells — again not lineage. And Tokmadzic 2002 (PMID 12516629) reports the claim's own named pair, IL-18 + IL-15, is the one combination that did NOT enhance decidual lymphocyte cytolysis (IL-18 + IL-12 did), so the compound cytokine in the claim is a review-level fusion with a primary source pointing the other way.

R1 is OUT at B2.
b.compartments_needed:
As the claim literally specifies, the two "compartments" are:
  A = fresh, uncultured dNK from first-trimester decidua basalis (~6-12 wk), immunomagnetically depleted of CD3+/CD16+ and CD56-bead purified, assayed at t=0 — the non-cytotoxic state.
  B = the SAME cells after 36 h ex vivo in 12 ng/ml IL-15 — the cytotoxic state.

STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: B is not an anatomical compartment. It is a culture product, a timepoint in a dish. There is no in vivo cytotoxic-dNK compartment anywhere in the body to pair with A. The B3 requirement that compartments A and B be obtainable simultaneously is therefore not merely difficult for R1 — it is undefined, because only one compartment exists and the other is an experimental manipulation of it.

If B is instead read as Kopcow's cytotoxic comparator, the enumerable real compartments become:
  A = first-trimester decidua basalis (surgical, pregnancy-gated)
  B = matched peripheral blood NK from the same woman, same visit
Optional real additional compartments if the question were reframed as an ancestry question: non-pregnant endometrium (pipelle biopsy) and term decidua (caesarean or vaginal delivery).
b.compartments_obtainable:
SPLIT VERDICT. As the claim specifies them: NO — the pairing is undefined, because compartment B is a 36 h culture dish rather than a tissue, so there is nothing to obtain simultaneously with A. For the substitute reading (decidua + matched blood): YES, and routinely so.

Decidua basalis plus a same-visit peripheral blood draw from the same woman is a standard paired collection at elective first-trimester termination, and paired decidua/blood single-cell datasets from the same donor already exist in the maternal-fetal-interface literature, so pairability is demonstrated rather than hypothetical.

GATING, stated explicitly as B3 requires:
  - ONLY AT SURGERY: decidua basalis requires an elective first-trimester termination (or, for term decidua, caesarean/delivery). No non-surgical route to decidua exists.
  - ONLY DURING PREGNANCY: doubly gated — the tissue does not exist outside gestation. Non-pregnant endometrium by pipelle is outpatient and repeatable, but it is a different compartment, not this one.
  - NOT post-mortem-restricted, and NOT mouse-restricted.
  - SINGLE TIMEPOINT PER DONOR: the uterus cannot be resampled, so no within-woman pre-pregnancy baseline and no longitudinal series. Gestational window ~6-12 wk; Kopcow never stated gestational age at all.
  - ASSAY-DESTRUCTIVE ACQUISITION: decidua requires collagenase digestion, which itself perturbs the exact granule-polarization and lysis readouts being scored — the confound is introduced by the act of obtaining compartment A.
b.compartment_notes:
mouse_only = FALSE, for compartment reasons rather than tool reasons. Human first-trimester decidua is genuinely obtainable (surgery- and pregnancy-gated, but routine), every load-bearing source behind R1 is human, and Phase A records no animal work anywhere in them. Nothing about R1 forces a mouse route, and mouse would arguably be the wrong organism: mouse uNK (DBA-lectin+) are a distinct population with trophoblast-invasion biology that does not map cleanly onto human dNK. Note separately that per prereg 4.3 mtDNA barcoding is weak in young inbred mice, so any hypothetical mouse route would need a genetic recorder (Confetti / Polylox / CRISPR) rather than mtDNA — but this is moot, since R1 fails B1 and B2 before compartment logistics matter.

Ordering note for the shortlist: R1 fails B1 (functional predicate; reversible state; clonal answer fixed by construction; no division in the assay window) and then fails B2 independently (both branches converge on the same non-lineage three-arm culture). It also fails prereg 5 criterion 1 at Phase A load_bearing = LOW. The verdict does not depend on B3 or B4, and B3 is recorded above only for completeness.

o.already_traced_evidence:
NOBODY HAS ADJUDICATED R1 WITH A CLONAL/LINEAGE METHOD. Across ~22 distinct queries (PubMed + EuropePMC via lit.py, plus WebSearch/WebFetch), covering every mandated category — mtDNA + (lineage OR clonal) + NK/decidua; mtscATAC-seq; MAESTER; "single-cell mitochondrial" + NK/decidua; barcode + NK cell; lentiviral barcoding + lymphocyte; and for the mouse arm fate mapping / Confetti / lineage tracing / Polylox / CRISPR recorder — I found ZERO studies that apply the clonal-barcoding primitive (do two cells share an ancestor, and how recently) to human decidual NK cells in any form. There is no mtscATAC-seq, no MAESTER, no mtDNA-variant, no somatic-mutation, no X-inactivation, and no barcoding study of decidua or endometrium immune cells at all. There is likewise nothing on the specific IL-15/IL-18 rescue: no study has asked whether the post-culture cytotoxic cells are the clonal progeny of the pre-culture non-cytotoxic cells or an outgrowth of a pre-existing minor clone.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOR THE SHORTLIST (do not read FALSE as "virgin territory"): the ADJACENT ancestry question in the uterus HAS been adjudicated with in vivo lineage-grade tools, just not with barcodes and not in humans. Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025, PMID 39708955: parabiosis + intravascular labeling in mice establishes that uterine trNK cells are derived from peripheral cNK cells, under progesterone control. Also eLife reviewed preprint 109878 (2025): adoptive transfer of CD45.2 splenic cNK into CD45.1 pregnant dams at gd0.5, showing TGF-beta-driven conversion of cNK into uterine trNK. And Sojka et al., J Immunol 2018, PMID 30275046: local proliferation of uterine trNK during decidualization. So "where do uNK come from" is occupied in mouse; "are the cytotoxic and non-cytotoxic dNK states clonally related in human" is not.

Second caveat: the R1 cytotoxic-program axis has been touched in decidua with a fate-mapping (not barcoding) tool — see nearest_occupant.

Also confirmed absent: no Polylox, Confetti, or CRISPR-recorder study of NK or uterine NK cells of any kind surfaced; no barcoded humanized-mouse reconstitution of uterus; no paired blood+decidua single-cell multiome with mtDNA genotyping.

Note the structural point that makes this near-unsearchable in principle: compartment B (IL-15-cultured cytotoxic dNK) has no in vivo existence, so there is no anatomical pair for a clonal method to adjudicate. The only clonal question in the neighbourhood that a method could touch is the reframed one (dNK vs matched pbNK, or endometrial vs decidual uNK), and that reframed question is itself partly occupied (see nearest_occupant and crossfield_occupancy).
o.nearest_occupant:
Two occupants tie for "nearest" along different axes; neither adjudicates R1.

(1) NEAREST ON STRUCTURE — Allan DSJ, Wu C, Mortlock RD, ... Dunbar CE, Childs RW. "Expanded NK cells used for adoptive cell therapy maintain diverse clonality and contain long-lived memory-like NK cell populations." Mol Ther Oncolytics 2023. PMID 36699615, PMCID PMC9842935 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R1_PMC9842935.txt). This is literally the R1 question with real barcodes: rhesus macaques transplanted with lentiviral-barcoded CD34+ HSPCs, then their NK cells put through a clinical-grade cytokine/feeder ex vivo culture (LCL or K562-41BBL/mbIL-21 + IL-2) that MAKES NK CELLS MORE CYTOTOXIC — and the barcodes ask whether the cytotoxic product is the progeny of the input repertoire or a selected minor clone. Answer: clonal continuity, not selection (>50% of starting barcode repertoire retained at day 14; Shannon diversity maintained; long-lived memory-like clones ~31% of output). DIFFERENCES FROM R1: rhesus macaque, not human; peripheral blood NK, not decidual NK; IL-2/feeder expansion over 14-21 days, not 36 h in 12 ng/ml IL-15; NK cytotoxicity is enhanced from an already-cytotoxic baseline rather than "rescued" from a Kopcow-type intrinsic MTOC/granule-polarization block; and pregnancy/decidua is entirely absent. Critically, it already demonstrates that the generic answer to "does a cytokine culture that turns on cytotoxicity select clones?" is NO for NK cells — which is exactly the result R1 would be spending a pregnancy-gated surgical cohort to re-derive.

(2) NEAREST ON SUBJECT — Mohamed MA, Li Y, Wegrzynowicz AK, Lindner PN, Vazquez J, Lopez GE, Stanic AK. "T-bet Fate Mapping Reveals Gestational Stage-Specific Transcriptional Adaptation of Decidual NK Cells." Am J Reprod Immunol 2026;95(3):e70220. PMID 41782473, PMCID PMC12961421 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R1_PMC12961421.txt). Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre fate mapping tracks cells with a HISTORY of T-bet expression through uterus/decidua/placenta across gestation, with bulk RNA-seq of fate-mapped cells and scRNA-seq at mid/late gestation. It directly interrogates the dNK cytotoxic program and asks whether dNK undergo LINEAGE DIVERSION (toward ILC2/ILC3) as they lose it; conclusion is no diversion, transcriptional adaptation plus subset redistribution, with decline of cytotoxic tissue-resident NK by late gestation. DIFFERENCES FROM R1: mouse, not human; Cre-lox transcription-factor-history marking, NOT the clonal primitive (it says "this cell once expressed T-bet", it cannot say "these two cells share a recent ancestor"); it tracks the LOSS of cytotoxicity across gestation, the opposite direction from IL-15 rescue; and IL-15 is mentioned only as an upstream regulator of Tbx21, never as an experimental manipulation.

(3) Closest human-tissue NK clonal work generally — Wu C, Liang JA, Brenchley JM, ... Dunbar CE. "Barcode clonal tracking of tissue-resident immune cells in rhesus macaque highlights distinct clonal distribution pattern of tissue NK cells." Front Immunol 2022. PMID 36605190, PMCID PMC9808525 (already in refs as R1_PMC9808525.txt). Barcoded HSPC transplant tracking clonal overlap of tissue-resident vs blood NK across liver, spleen, lung, GI, longitudinally against PB. UTERUS WAS NOT SAMPLED (zero occurrences of "uter*" in the full text). This is the template a reframed R1 ancestry question would have to follow, already executed for every tissue except the one R1 cares about.

(4) Nearest human NK mtDNA work — Rueckert T, Lareau CA, Mashreghi M-F, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022. PMID 36289449, PMCID PMC9663309. mtscATAC-seq with somatic mtDNA variants as endogenous barcodes in human NK; shows adaptive NK clones expand in HCMV+ donors and are STABLY MAINTAINED IN SPECIFIC EPIGENETIC STATES over time — i.e. the "is a functional/epigenetic state clone-linked or environment-imposed" question answered in human NK. Differences: peripheral blood only, HCMV adaptive NK not dNK, no tissue, no cytokine-rescue manipulation.

(5) Closest work on the actual dNK cytotoxicity axis, but NON-clonal — Greene MM, Asiimwe RR, ... Little SC, Porrett PM. "A developmental program of early residency promotes the differentiation of divergent uterine NK cell subsets in humans." bioRxiv 2025, PMID 40672293, PMCID PMC12265685. Human endometrium; identifies early tissue immigrants, developmental intermediates and mature effector states, with TGF-beta responsiveness determining "either repression or preservation of cytotoxic effector potential." This is R1's exact biological question in human tissue — and it is answered with scRNA-seq trajectory inference, NOT with any clonal method. That is the current state of the art and it is precisely where a lineage tool has not been applied.

(6) Human NK compartment-relationship adjudication without barcodes — Niehrs A, ... Bjorkstrom NK. "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis." Nat Immunol 2025;26(11):2004-2015. PMID 41087727, PMCID PMC12571907 (archived R1_PMC12571907.txt). Uses liver-transplant donor/recipient chimerism (a natural ancestry label), intravascular labeling, humanized mice, macaques and efferent lymph to show human liver CD56bright TR NK are transiently resident and progressively replaced by recruited circulating NK acquiring TR traits via Runx3. Same structural question (is the tissue population continuous with blood?), human, in vivo — but liver, not uterus, and no clonal resolution.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HEAVILY OCCUPIED. R1 invokes a general process — cytokine-driven, reversible acquisition of an effector (cytotoxic) state within one lineage — and every neighbouring field has already answered that structural question with lineage tools, with a consistent verdict.

MYELOID — decisively occupied, and with the exact modern method. Liu V, et al. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 (bioRxiv 2025 version PMID 40777278, PMCID PMC12330704; a copy is already in this repo as refs/42242233.txt); commentary "Attack of the clones," PMID 42276048. They built Mitotrek, profiled 218,715 cells with joint scATAC + mtDNA variants across MATCHED tumor, non-involved tissue and PBMC from the same patients (5 NSCLC, 5 ovarian, 3 with matched blood), and showed that TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally linked to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, with individual clones biased toward DC vs macrophage states plus associated epigenetic signatures. This is the structural template of the reframed R1 ancestry question — paired blood/tissue, mtDNA clonal tracing, asking whether a tissue functional state is clone-intrinsic or niche-imposed — already executed in human. NK cells were included but "rarely detected in most tumors" except one ovarian case with oligoclonal expansion; decidua was not sampled.

ILC — occupied, and it is the field R1's premise was borrowed from. Cytokine-driven, REVERSIBLE inter-state conversion (NKp46+ ILC3 <-> ILC1, ILC2 -> ILC1/ILC3, driven by IL-12/IL-18 and Notch, reversing on cytokine withdrawal) was established with genetic fate mappers (Rorc fate-mapped "ex-ILC3", T-bet fate mapping) precisely because flow phenotype alone could not distinguish "converted" from "recruited." The published lesson is the one B1 encodes: the fate mapper showed both states carry the SAME lineage label, so the lineage tool confirmed common ancestry but could not by itself discriminate a reversible state from a differentiation step — that discrimination came from cytokine-withdrawal reversal experiments, not from lineage. The decidua-specific instance of this same design is PMID 41782473 (above), which explicitly asked whether dNK losing the cytotoxic/T-bet program undergo "lineage diversion" to ILC2/ILC3 and concluded they do not.

NK/ILC BOUNDARY — occupied with actual DNA barcodes. Vo DN, ... Malmberg K-J, Sitnicka E. "A temporal developmental map separates human NK cells from noncytotoxic ILCs through clonal and single-cell analysis." Blood Adv 2024;8(11):2933-2951, PMID 38484189, PMCID PMC11176970 (archived R1_PMC11176970.txt). Lentiviral clonal DNA barcoding of human CB CD34+ cells on OP9 resolves whether the CYTOTOXIC NK state and the NON-CYTOTOXIC CD56+ ILC states are the same or divergent lineages — S3b-NK and S4-NK are clonally close, ILC3 is clonally distant. That is R1's underlying structural question ("is the non-cytotoxic CD56bright-like innate lymphocyte the same lineage as the cytotoxic one, and can one become the other?") answered with barcodes, in humans — in vitro from cord blood rather than in decidua.

T CELL — occupied for the same structure. TCR clonotype is a free endogenous clonal barcode and the field has used it to show that progenitor-exhausted and terminally exhausted, and circulating and tissue-resident, states are routinely occupied by the SAME clone (e.g. PMID 41308653, "Deep profiling of human T cells defines compartmentalized clones and phenotypic trajectories across blood and tonsils," 2025; PMID 34127056, "Maintenance of the human memory T cell repertoire by subset and tissue site," Genome Med 2021). The established conclusion — one clone spans multiple reversible functional states, so clonal identity does not predict effector state — is the direct T-cell analogue of what R1 would find, and it is exactly why lineage was NOT the tool that settled exhaustion reversibility (adoptive transfer of sorted single states was).

NET: the mechanism R1 borrows has had its clonal structure resolved in three adjacent fields, and in all three the clonal answer was "same lineage, different state" — the outcome B1 flags as non-discriminating. R1 would be re-running a settled structural experiment in the one tissue where the compartments cannot be paired.

b.why:
R3 asserts no ancestry relation. There is no compartment A and compartment B whose relatedness is in question — the subject is one population of human blood NK cells in one well, sampled at day 7 (TGF-beta on) and day 17 (10 days after washout). Taking the two halves separately:

(ii) "effector function does not revert" is a pure function claim, read out as granzyme A/B and IFN-gamma expression and (elsewhere in the source) target killing. The primitive returns only whether two cells share an ancestor and how recently. It is silent on whether either cell can degranulate or make IFN-gamma. NOT DECIDABLE, categorically.

(i) "residency phenotype reverts" is the textbook REVERSIBLE STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE. CD103/CD9/CD49a switching on and off leaves no trace in the genealogy: whether the marker reverts or persists, the same clones are present at day 17, descended from the same day-0 founders, with the same coalescent structure. Both answers are consistent with an identical barcode readout, so the barcode cannot discriminate them.

The one genuinely lineage-shaped residue is the selection-vs-conversion alternative: are the day-17 marker-negative cells the PROGENY of the day-7 CD103+ cells (true reversion), or the outgrowth of clones that were never CD103+ (selection)? That is a legitimate "same/different lineage" question and IS decidable in principle. But it is not what the claim asserts, it addresses only the trivial half, and a definitive answer either way leaves the load-bearing assertion — persistence of the functional deficit — completely untouched. Overall verdict FALSE.
b.action_if_yes:
Design that produces a YES: barcode human PB NK cells at day 0 (lentiviral barcoding of human/rhesus NK is established — PMID 40621477, PMID 31649681), expose to TGF-beta, index-sort CD103+ cells at day 7, withdraw, re-read barcodes plus surface phenotype at day 17. YES = the day-17 CD103-negative cells carry the SAME barcodes as the day-7 CD103+ cells, i.e. within-clone reversion, no selective outgrowth.

Very next experiment after YES: nothing lineage-shaped is left to do. You would immediately have to run the non-lineage experiment the claim actually turns on — is the effector deficit a slower RECOVERY TIME CONSTANT or genuine signal-independent fixity? That means (a) withdrawal arms beyond a single 10-day timepoint (20/30/40 d), (b) CellTrace/CFSE division tracking to match proliferative history between arms, since TGF-beta durably suppressed Ki67 and dilution-through-division is exactly the mechanism that resets chromatin and protein load, (c) a TGF-betaR inhibitor arm at withdrawal to prove the signal is truly off, (d) a cytotoxicity readout in the day-17 withdrawal arm (the source has none), and (e) the field-standard test from T cell exhaustion (Philip 2017, PMID 28514453): transfer the withdrawn cells OUT of the inducing environment in vivo and show the state survives multiple rounds of division. None of these requires or uses the barcode.
b.action_if_no:
NO = the day-17 marker-negative population is dominated by barcodes that were CD103-negative at day 7, i.e. apparent "reversion" is selective outgrowth of never-converted clones rather than a cell changing state.

Very next experiment after NO: the identical experiment listed under YES. You would rewrite one sentence about marker kinetics and then still have to run the longer withdrawal timecourse, division tracking, inhibitor arm, killing assay and in vivo removal to learn whether the effector deficit is fixed — because the effector half of the claim is untouched by the selection finding, and a selection result does not predict its direction.

This branch is additionally close to foreclosed and close to vacuous. The source already ran the population-level version of exactly this control (Fig. S3A-C): CD103+ and CD103- NK cells were sorted at day 7 and recultured separately, and BOTH lost CD103 after withdrawal. A barcode experiment returning NO would have to overturn an existing purification control, and if it did, it would revise only a footnote about marker lability that is in any case established better, peer-reviewed and in vivo in humans elsewhere (Niehrs, Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727).
b.both_answers_reason:
Fails B2 on all three strict grounds simultaneously.

1. THE TWO BRANCHES CONVERGE ON ONE IDENTICAL NEXT EXPERIMENT. Under both YES and NO the follow-up is the same package: longer withdrawal arms, division tracking, TGF-betaR inhibitor control, a real cytotoxicity readout, and in vivo removal per the Philip 2017 standard. The barcode result changes no decision, no allocation, and no design parameter of that package.

2. THE YES BRANCH IS VACUOUS. It confirms a control the source itself already ran and reported (Fig. S3C sort-and-reculture). "We would conclude reversion is cell-intrinsic and move on" is precisely the vacuity the filter is written to catch.

3. ANCESTRY IS EMPIRICALLY ORTHOGONAL TO THE READOUT THE CLAIM CARES ABOUT. The decisive line in the archived preprint: "effector function did not differ between CD103+ and CD103- NK cells at day 17, with CD103- cells displaying comparable or even lower IFN-gamma expression." The functional deficit does not segregate with residency-marker history at all. So even the sophisticated framing — "does the dysfunctional state track clone identity?" — is pre-answered in the negative at population level. Knowing who is descended from whom predicts nothing about who is dysfunctional, which is the whole point of the claim.

The genuine weaknesses of R3 (single withdrawal timepoint, unmatched division history, no in vivo arm, in vitro-only referent, unrefereed preprint) are all addressable, but none of them is addressable with a lineage primitive. R3 is OUT — consistent with Phase A's independent finding that is_lineage_claim = FALSE and load_bearing = LOW.
b.compartments_needed:
AS REGISTERED (human, in vitro), there is no compartment pair — A and B are the same culture at two timepoints:
A = day-7 TGF-beta-exposed human PB NK cells (CD103+/CD9+/CD49a+ fraction, FACS-sortable)
B = day-17 NK cells from the same well, 10 days after washout
C = day-17 IL-15-only NK cells from the same donor (required handling-matched control)
All three are splits of one negatively-enriched NK prep from a single venipuncture of one healthy adult.

FOR THE IN VIVO REFERENT (the version that would carry weight), the compartments become:
A' = bona fide tissue-resident NK established in a TGF-beta-rich niche — human liver, decidua, or tumour
B' = the same cells after leaving the niche / after TGF-beta signalling ceases
C' = matched autologous peripheral blood NK
D' = a niche-experienced population whose division history since withdrawal is known (requires photoconversion or a dilution label, not obtainable from a single human biopsy)
b.compartment_notes:
As registered the answer is trivially TRUE and that is itself diagnostic: A, B and C are wells of the same plate from one healthy human blood donor, perfectly paired by construction, obtainable from a routine venipuncture with no surgical, post-mortem, pregnancy or species constraint. Paired availability is unconstrained precisely because the entire claim lives in a dish and has no in vivo referent — B3 is trivially satisfied for a claim that already failed B1 and B2. Lineage tooling is likewise not the binding constraint: lentiviral barcoding of human NK cells is established (PMID 40621477; rhesus NK clonal repertoire PMID 31649681), and endogenous mtDNA approaches (mtscATAC-seq, MAESTER) are mature. The bottleneck is B2, not compartment access.

If the claim were upgraded to its in vivo referent, obtainability degrades sharply and unevenly:
- A' human liver-resident NK: only at surgical resection, transplantation, or post-mortem.
- A' human decidual NK: only during pregnancy, at termination or delivery.
- A' human tumour NK: only at surgery.
- C' matched autologous blood: easy, and pairs with any of the above from one individual.
- B' "cells that have provably left the niche": in humans essentially only two routes, both rare and specialist — donor-derived liver NK recirculating in recipient blood after liver transplantation (Niehrs, Nat Immunol 2025, PMID 41087727), or efferent-lymph / thoracic-duct cannulation. Not obtainable in ordinary human cohorts.
- Sequential sampling of the SAME tissue before and after TGF-beta withdrawal in vivo is NOT obtainable in humans at all: it would need repeat biopsy of the same niche plus systemic TGF-betaR blockade. That arm is MOUSE-ONLY — conditional Tgfbr2 deletion after residency is established, Kaede/KikGR photoconversion to time egress, or transfer of niche-experienced cells.

So mouse_only = FALSE is correct for the claim as written (human, in vitro, paired from one donor), but the only version of R3 with an in vivo referent has a mouse-only withdrawal arm. Either way this does not rescue the claim, because the withdrawal arm is a signal/function manipulation, not a lineage measurement.

o.already_traced_evidence:
NOBODY HAS ADJUDICATED R3 WITH A CLONAL/LINEAGE METHOD. The method-axis searches came back genuinely empty, not merely thin:

(1) MITOCHONDRIAL AXIS — EMPTY. PubMed "MAESTER[tiab] AND (NK[tiab] OR lymphocyte[tiab])" = 0 hits. "mtscATAC[tiab]" = 12 hits, all leukemia/AML/CLL/HSPC/kidney/aging (36792778 Nat Protoc method paper; 41419602 ASCT; 39661948 pAML; 41000852 cryo-mtscATAC; 42193956 liver/spleen MAESTER organ-typing) — NONE on NK cells, none on tissue residency, none on TGF-beta. "(mtDNA OR mitochondrial) AND (clonal OR lineage) AND (natural killer OR NK cell)" returned only metabolism/leukemia papers plus 36289449 (adaptive NK memory, not mtDNA lineage). "innate lymphoid[tiab] AND (mitochondrial OR mtDNA) AND clonal[tiab]" = 0 hits. "single-cell AND clonal AND (tissue-resident NK OR trNK)" = 0 hits. mtDNA lineage tracing in immune cells clearly exists (Penter 34112698, 39236287, 36469010, 35046946) but has never been pointed at NK residency.

(2) BARCODING AXIS — EXISTS FOR NK, NEVER FOR THIS QUESTION. The only real NK clonal-barcoding corpus is the Dunbar lab rhesus HSPC lentiviral-barcode series: 24702997 (Cell Stem Cell 2014, distinct lineage origin for NK), 30389798 (Sci Immunol 2018, clonal expansion/compartmentalized maintenance of CD56+ vs CD16+ subsets), 31649681 (CMV repertoire), 36605190 (Front Immunol 2022, tissue-resident NK across liver/spleen/lung/GI vs blood). I pulled the full methods of 36605190 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/R3_PMC9808525.txt): barcoded CD34+ HSPC autologous transplant, tissue collection by laparoscopy/endoscopy/necropsy, FACS sorting of CD16+/CD56+/DN NK, barcode PCR + Illumina. It measures clonal SHARING between TR NK and PB NK at steady state. There is no TGF-beta arm, no niche-withdrawal arm, no per-clone function readout, and no timepoint structure that could separate "phenotype reverted" from "function persisted". 40621477 and 36699615 are CAR-NK/expansion QC barcoding, not residency.

(3) MOUSE RECORDER AXIS — EMPTY FOR NK. "Polylox[tiab] OR (genetic barcoding AND (NK OR innate lymphoid))" returned only Polylox HSC papers (28813413, 31110297) and the rhesus work — no Polylox/CARLIN/CRISPR-recorder NK paper. "confetti reporter NK cell clonal fate mouse" = nothing on NK. Genetic fate-map tools for NK/ILC1 DO exist and I found them (34437840 single-NK-cell fate mapping; 41966330 Eomes dual fate-label; 21093318 RORgt fate map; Hobit-FM 34880136), but none run a TGF-beta withdrawal/niche-exit design.

(4) CLAIM-CONTENT AXIS — THE CLAIM ITSELF IS OCCUPIED, BUT BY A NON-LINEAGE METHOD. Schmid K, Haimerl C, ... Boettcher JP, Schmid RM, Wiedemann GM, bioRxiv 14 Feb 2026, DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354, "Prolonged TGF-beta locks NK cells in a dysfunctional state through persistent epigenetic remodeling of IRF, T-bet and EOMES binding sites" (TUM/Klinikum rechts der Isar). This runs the registered R3 experiment — short vs prolonged TGF-beta then SIGNAL WITHDRAWAL — with RNA-seq/ATAC-seq/function, and reports the exact dissociation R3 predicts: "In contrast to the lasting repression of effector genes, genes associated with tissue residency exhibit largely reversible transcriptional and epigenetic changes," while prolonged-exposure effector suppression "persists even after signal withdrawal." Confirmed via two independent routes (Europe PMC record + bioRxiv listing). No clonal, barcoding, mtDNA or lineage-tracing method is used anywhere in it (biorxiv.org full text returned 403, so this rests on abstract/results-level text, not the methods section — flagging that limit).

So: already_traced = FALSE strictly on the lineage-method question asked. Phase B should nonetheless see that the registered in-vitro version of R3 has been answered by other means five months before this screen, so the lineage tool would have to be justified by the in vivo referent (A'/B'/C'/D'), not by the washout culture.
o.nearest_occupant:
Two occupants, one on method and one on content — neither is the claim.

NEAREST ON CONTENT (not lineage): bioRxiv DOI 10.64898/2026.02.11.705354 (Schmid/Wiedemann, Feb 2026) — no PMID yet, preprint. Does TGF-beta exposure + withdrawal in NK cells and reports residency-gene reversibility with non-reversible effector suppression. DIFFERENCE FROM R3: identical conclusion, zero clonal content. It is a population-average transcriptomic/epigenomic result, so it cannot exclude the selection alternative — that the day-17 washout well is dominated by descendants of cells that were never durably TGF-beta-imprinted (or that preferentially survived/divided), rather than by the same cells having reverted phenotype while keeping suppressed function. That selection-vs-reversion distinction is precisely and only what clonal barcoding could add, and nobody has added it.

NEAREST ON METHOD (lineage tool, adjacent question): PMID 41966330 (Mucosal Immunol 2026) "Eomes fate-labeling reveals a subset of Eomes-lo NK cells that exhibits an ILC1-like phenotype." Dual-reporter system giving simultaneous LIVE Eomes expression and irreversible Eomes FATE-LABEL, applied in salivary gland and during Toxoplasma gondii infection. This is structurally the closest lineage adjudication that exists: it uses an irreversible label to prove that cells displaying the residency/ILC1-like surface phenotype are fate-labelled ex-Eomes NK cells, i.e. a STATE change inside one lineage rather than a lineage switch — the same "is this a reversible state or a different lineage" question R3 sits on. DIFFERENCES: (a) it is a fate label, not a clonal barcode, so it cannot ask whether two cells share a recent ancestor; (b) it runs the acquisition direction (NK -> ILC1-like), never the withdrawal/reversion direction; (c) it never dissociates phenotype from effector function, which is R3's entire payload; (d) mouse, infection-driven, not TGF-beta withdrawal.

RUNNERS-UP, all clearly outside: PMID 36605190 (rhesus barcode clonal tracking of TR NK vs PB NK across liver/spleen/lung/GI — the closest thing to R3's in vivo A'/B'/C' compartment structure, but steady-state clonal sharing only, no withdrawal, no function). PMID 34437840 (Immunity 2021, Flommersfeld — single-NK-cell fate mapping; finds cNK and ILC1-like NK are DISTINCT lineages after MCMV, i.e. answers the adjacent question in the opposite direction and shows the design R3 would need). PMID 28759002 (Cortez, SMAD4 restrains non-canonical TGF-beta and prevents NK->ILC1-like conversion) and PMID 28759001 (Gao, TGF-beta converts NK to ILC1 in tumours) — TGF-beta-driven acquisition, genetic/adoptive-transfer not clonal, no withdrawal arm. PMID 40610398 (Nat Commun 2025, IL-35 converts human NK to CD9+CD103+CD49a+ ILC1-like via autocrine TGF-beta) and PMID 39692745 (JEM 2025, autocrine TGF-beta1 continuously required to MAINTAIN trNK residency — the closest published statement that residency needs ongoing signal, i.e. is reversible, but shown by conditional deletion, not lineage). PMID 36289449 (Nat Immunol 2022, clonal expansion + epigenetic inheritance of NK memory) — the one paper joining clonality to epigenetic persistence in NK, but HCMV/adaptive NK, not TGF-beta, not residency.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HEAVILY OCCUPIED. G4 applies hard here: R3 invokes residency + plasticity + a "signal removed, phenotype reverts, function does not" structure, and the T cell field has already answered exactly that structural question with lineage tools — including with an endogenous clonal barcode, which is the same primitive barcoding provides.

T CELL / Trm (direct structural match, decided with lineage tools):
- PMID 31278120 (Klicznik, Sci Immunol 2019) "Human CD4+CD103+ cutaneous resident memory T cells are found in the circulation of healthy individuals." Used TCR clonotype sharing — an endogenous per-cell clonal barcode, functionally identical to what mtDNA/lentiviral barcoding would provide — to prove blood CLA+CD103+CD4+ cells are ex-skin-Trm. Result: CD69 is lost on exit while CD103 and the skin-homing program are retained. That is R3's exact shape (residency phenotype partially reverts on niche exit, tissue-imprinted program persists), adjudicated clonally, in humans, seven years ago, in a different cell type.
- Fonseca et al., Nat Immunol 2020, "Developmental plasticity allows outside-in immune responses by resident memory T cells" — Kaede photoconversion: Trm exit tissue, become Tcm-like, retain residency epigenetic imprint and preferentially re-home and re-establish residency. This is the D' compartment R3 says is unobtainable from one human biopsy; the T cell field solved it with photoconversion in mouse.
- PMID 32568362 (JEM 2020, retrograde migration of Trm to draining LN), PMID 32661361 (Nat Immunol 2020, Behr — Trm shape systemic secondary responses), JEM 2021 "Human resident memory T cells exit the skin and mediate systemic Th2-driven inflammation", PMID 38817613 (Front Immunol 2024 ex-TRM review), PMID 41737383 (2026, circulating ex-Trm CD8 in atopic dermatitis), PMID 41950321 (Sci Adv 2026, "CD69 regulates the tissue dynamics of epigenetically imprinted memory CD4+ T cells" — the imprint/phenotype dissociation stated outright), Bromley et al. Immunity 2024 (tissue Treg pool shaped by transient multi-tissue migration + conserved residency program, Kaede).
- PMID 34312547 (Abdel-Hakeem, Nat Immunol 2021) "Epigenetic scars of CD8+ T cell exhaustion persist after cure of chronic infection in humans" — the withdrawal experiment in its purest form: remove the driving signal (HCV antigen, via DAA cure), surface phenotype partially normalizes, epigenetic and functional scar does not, tracked on antigen-specific (clonally defined) cells. R3's "phenotype reverts, function does not" is this result with TGF-beta substituted for antigen and NK substituted for CD8.

ILC / NK (same structural question, lineage tools, adjacent axis):
- PMID 21093318 (Vonarbourg, Immunity 2010) RORgt fate map — irreversible label proves ex-RORgt ILC3 become ILC1-like: the field's canonical demonstration that an ILC phenotype switch is a state change within a labelled lineage.
- PMID 41966330 (2026) Eomes dual live/fate reporter — same logic for NK -> ILC1-like (see nearest_occupant).
- PMID 34437840 (Immunity 2021) single-NK-cell fate mapping — answers the mirror question (cNK vs ILC1-like are distinct lineages, not one plastic state) and demonstrates the exact experimental machinery R3's in vivo referent would need.
- PMID 33214656 (ILC3->ILC1 conversion in Campylobacter), PMID 28698286 (tissue microenvironment dictates ILC3 fate), PMID 34880136 / Hobit-FM (residency TF fate mapping in trNK/ILC1), Immunity 2023 "Circulating NK cells establish tissue residency upon acute infection of skin" (the acquisition direction, fate-mapped).

Bottom line for Phase B: the lineage-tool answer to "does a niche-imposed residency state revert when the niche signal stops, while the functional imprint persists" already exists — it is YES-with-partial-reversion-and-persistent-imprint — it was obtained with TCR clonotypes and Kaede photoconversion in T cells and with fate labels in ILCs, and R3 would be re-running a settled structural result in a new cell type. Combined with the Feb 2026 preprint already reporting the NK-specific answer non-clonally, the residual novelty is narrow.

b.why:
TRUE, but only under one of the two readings the claim conflates, and the row must be re-worded to that reading or it is not decidable at all.

(a) DECIDABLE READING — persistence/identity across time: "the NK cells present in the uterus after delivery are the same clones as (or clonal descendants of) the dNK present during that pregnancy." This is a straight "A and B are the same lineage / the progeny of A are B" proposition. The primitive answers it directly: sample dNK at t1 and uterine NK at t2 in the same woman, ask whether t2 cells fall into clones containing t1 cells and how recently they shared an ancestor. YES = overlapping clones with recent common ancestry; NO = disjoint clones. These are genuinely different clonal structures, so the primitive discriminates.

(b) NOT DECIDABLE READING — the claim's own label: "PTdNK" in the source means Pregnancy-Trained dNK, i.e. dNK acquire an NKG2C-hi/LILRB1-hi epigenetically imprinted state that makes them secrete more IFN-g and VEGFa in a subsequent pregnancy. That is function and phenotype causation, which lineage does not measure. It is also a marker-state claim, and any clone can occupy or vacate a marker state, so both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure. Phase A already flagged this conflation (the lineage half is what R4 asserts and has no evidence; the functional half has evidence and is not what R4 asserts).

NOT the reversible-state failure mode: R4 sits in the registry's "reversal" group but is not a reversibility claim — persistence is about physical presence of cells over time, not about a state occupied and vacated. Phase A flagged the group label as a category error and I concur.

RESOLUTION LIMIT that must be carried forward: shared mtDNA variants between t1 dNK and t2 uterine NK establish common ancestry, not survival of the individual cells. A marrow clone that seeds the uterus twice produces the same signature as a cell that stayed put. Contemporaneous blood at both timepoints is therefore not an optional control — it is the only thing that converts "shared ancestry" into "local persistence." The decidable proposition is strictly "the postpartum uterine NK pool is drawn from the same, uterus-restricted clones as the pregnancy dNK pool," not "the individual cells survived."
b.action_if_yes:
YES = postpartum uterine NK sit in the same clones as that woman's pregnancy dNK, and those clones are absent or rare in her contemporaneous blood, i.e. the replacement-from-circulation model is wrong for the uterus.

Next experiment: add a THIRD timepoint — decidua from that same woman's subsequent pregnancy — and ask whether the clones retained postpartum are the ones that dominate and expand in the next pregnancy, which is the source's actual model.

Why this branch is weaker than it looks: the obvious follow-up ("are the persisting clones the ones carrying the NKG2C-hi / trained chromatin state?") is NOT a next experiment — mtscATAC-seq yields clone identity and chromatin accessibility from the same cells, so that intersection falls out of the very run that produced the YES. It is the adjudicating experiment's second panel. The only genuinely new experiment is the subsequent-pregnancy timepoint: the same assay again, years later, contingent on that woman conceiving and on tissue access at the next termination or delivery (see B3, compartment 4). Payoff is further compressed by Gamliel's own Fig 1G — the NKG2C-hi expansion is present at gravidity>=2 with parity 0, i.e. it tracks having been pregnant, not having delivered — so a YES on post-delivery persistence would not vindicate the source's model either.
b.action_if_no:
NO = the postpartum uterine NK repertoire is clonally disjoint from the pregnancy dNK and is a fresh draw from the contemporaneous blood repertoire.

Next experiment: there is none that the adjudicating experiment has not already performed. The blood arm is mandatory in the design (it is what makes YES interpretable at all), so "they came from the circulation" is already in hand from the same data the moment NO is returned. The NO answer opens nothing new.

The only residual move is to relocate the "memory" from the NK cell to the endometrial niche — ask whether postpartum stroma/epithelium carries the mark and imprints freshly recruited NK (stromal ATAC/methylation, endometrial organoid plus naive NK co-culture). That is (i) a change of subject away from lineage entirely, (ii) an unbounded "go look somewhere else" rather than a determinate next step, and (iii) already the standing model, and it lands in territory this screen holds as T3/T5 (blood NK -> dNK-like in vitro; glycodelin-A). This is the textbook "we would conclude X and move on."
b.both_answers_reason:
FAILS B2 on two independent grounds; R4 is OUT.

1. THE NO BRANCH IS VACUOUS IN THE PROHIBITED SENSE. Its entire content is pre-delivered by the blood control the design already requires. A null falsifies the claim and opens no distinct experiment; the only follow-up is a change of subject to niche imprinting, which is not a lineage question and is already the default model.

2. NO IS THE STRONGLY FAVOURED PRIOR, ALREADY SUPPORTED BY LINEAGE-GRADE EVIDENCE IN THIS EXACT COMPARTMENT, so the probable answer returns almost no information:
- PMID 41811987 (2026), "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation": single-cell SNP/HLA-disparity genotyping of endometrial immune cells in uterus-transplant and HSCT recipients. Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant; HSCT gave near-complete graft-derived endometrial immune reconstitution. The uterine immune pool, uNK included, is replenished from the circulating/marrow compartment. This is donor/recipient genotype used as a lineage primitive in the target tissue.
- PMID 33617461 (Strunz, Sci Immunol 2021), "Continuous human uterine NK cell differentiation in response to endometrial regeneration and pregnancy": by uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins, the uNK niche "could be replenished from circulation" and is under genetic control; differentiation is continuous and coupled to endometrial regeneration.
- PMID 41087727 (2025), "Transient tissue residency and lymphatic egress define human CD56bright NK cell homeostasis": the exact cell type at issue (dNK are CD56bright) is only transiently resident and recirculates via lymphatics; in liver transplantation donor tissue-resident CD56bright NK are progressively replaced by recipient cells.

3. THE YES BRANCH'S ONLY NEW EXPERIMENT IS UNSCHEDULABLE. Its determinate follow-up requires a third sample from the same woman's next pregnancy (B3 compartment 4), i.e. the same assay years later contingent on conception and surgical/obstetric tissue access. Everything else it appears to open (clone x trained-chromatin intersection) is produced by the adjudicating run itself, so the two branches largely collapse into the one experiment.

4. G4 CROSS-FIELD OCCUPANCY. The general structural question R4 borrows — local persistence versus replacement from circulation for a tissue-resident innate lymphocyte — has already been answered with clonal tools in adjacent fields: PMID 42242233 / 40777278 (2026) "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer" used mtDNA variants plus scATAC across 218,715 cells from matched tumour, tissue and blood to show TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally continuous with circulating monocytes; PMID 36289449 (2022) used mtDNA somatic mutations as endogenous barcodes to show clonal expansion and stable epigenetic maintenance of HCMV-adaptive NK in blood. The method is proven in NK cells and the answer pattern in tissue is established.

5. CLAIM-LEVEL SPECIFIC: even a clean lineage answer does not settle R4's actual scientific content, because the load-bearing proposition (trained cells function better in the next pregnancy) is a function claim outside the primitive, and the source's own parity-0/gravidity>=2 result decouples the phenotype from delivery — the thing "persisting after delivery" would be adjudicating.
b.compartments_needed:
Four, of which three must be paired within one woman across two timepoints:

1. dNK from an ONGOING PREGNANCY (t1). Available only during pregnancy and only at a procedure: first-trimester decidua at elective surgical termination (the Gamliel/Hadassah route), or term decidua basalis at Caesarean section / from the basal plate of a delivered placenta. Never obtainable non-invasively.

2. UTERINE LINING AFTER DELIVERY (t2). Four imperfect routes: (i) lochia / shed decidua in the first postpartum days — non-invasive, but it is the EXPELLED material, degraded and blood-admixed, and measures what is being shed rather than what is retained; (ii) Pipelle endometrial biopsy at >=3 months postpartum — feasible, research-only, invasive, requires endometrial regeneration; (iii) menstrual blood by menstrual cup once cycles resume — non-invasive, this is Gamliel's "eNK" compartment, but return of menses is delayed months by lactation and the sample is again shed, not retained, endometrium; (iv) hysterectomy specimen — rare and confounded by the pathology prompting it.

3. CONTEMPORANEOUS PERIPHERAL BLOOD AT BOTH t1 AND t2. Trivially obtainable and strictly mandatory — the only way to separate local persistence from re-seeding by a clone that also lives in blood/marrow (see B1 resolution limit).

4. (Only to test the source's actual model) DECIDUA FROM THE SAME WOMAN'S SUBSEQUENT PREGNANCY (t3). Requires her to conceive again and to have tissue access at that pregnancy.
b.compartments_obtainable:
PARTIALLY YES — compartments 1+2+3 are genuinely obtainable paired from one human; compartment 4 is not, at any usable n.

OBTAINABLE PAIRED (1+2+3): a prospective design works — term decidua plus blood at Caesarean section, then Pipelle biopsy or menstrual-cup collection plus blood at 6-12 months postpartum, from the same woman. Costs are real but survivable: multi-month follow-up, cohort attrition, and IRB approval for a research endometrial biopsy in a postpartum woman. Nothing here is post-mortem-only and nothing is mouse-only.

NOT OBTAINABLE (4): the subsequent-pregnancy sample cannot be scheduled — it needs the woman to conceive again years later AND to have surgical or obstetric tissue access at that pregnancy. It is also self-selecting in a way that breaks the comparison: a woman whose next pregnancy also ends in elective termination is a particular population, and a woman who delivers at term yields term decidua, which is not comparable to first-trimester decidua. This is the compartment the YES branch's only new experiment depends on, and it is the practical reason the YES branch cannot be closed out.

TIMING CONSTRAINTS, explicitly: compartment 1 exists ONLY during pregnancy and only at a procedure. Compartment 2 exists either in the immediate postpartum window (lochia, degraded) or after a months-long delay (biopsy/menses, lactation-dependent). Neither compartment requires post-mortem access; neither is mouse-only.
b.compartment_notes:
Mouse is available but is a poor substitute for this specific claim, so FALSE on mouse_only is not a convenience call. Mouse dNK fate mapping is already being run — PMID 41782473 (2026), Tbx21-Cre x Rosa26-RFP T-bet fate mapping tracking NK across uterus, decidua and placenta through gestation — so the tooling exists. But mice do not menstruate, there is no endometrial-regeneration cycle of the kind the human claim depends on, uNK subset structure differs, and the inter-pregnancy interval that gives "persisting after delivery" its meaning in humans has no mouse counterpart. A mouse result would not transfer.

Two structural notes for the shortlist, both inherited from Phase A and both bearing on how the compartments must be labelled if R4 is ever revived:
1. The word "postpartum" in R4 has no referent in the cited source. Gamliel 2018 sampled first-trimester decidua at termination and menstrual blood from non-pregnant parous women; it sampled no postpartum decidua. "PTdNK" = Pregnancy-Trained dNK, not postpartum dNK. So compartment 2 as R4 names it has never been collected for this question by anyone — Phase A recorded this as searched-and-not-found (G3), not as non-existent.
2. Compartments 2(i), 2(iii) and Gamliel's eNK are all SHED endometrium, not retained tissue. Any design that uses menstrual blood as the "postpartum uterine" compartment is measuring the cells being expelled, which is close to the opposite of the persistence being claimed. Only the Pipelle biopsy (2ii) samples retained lining, and it is the one route that is invasive.

o.already_traced_evidence:
No study has adjudicated "dNK from a pregnancy persist in the uterus after delivery" with any clonal/lineage method. Searched across PubMed + Europe PMC (~30 distinct query formulations) plus 4 web searches, and read the methods of 7 primary sources (archived under /home/user/aaa/refs/R4_*).

Findings by required axis:
(1) mtDNA + clonal/lineage + these cell types: the ONLY mtDNA-barcode NK study is Rueckert et al. Nat Immunol 2022 (PMID 36289449, PMC9663309). Its Methods state explicitly: "Primary NK cells were isolated from freshly drawn peripheral blood of healthy donors ... or from buffy coats." Blood only; no tissue, no uterus/endometrium/decidua, no pregnancy.
(2) mtscATAC / MAESTER / "single-cell mitochondrial" + decidua/endometrium/uterine NK: ZERO hits in PubMed or Europe PMC. An independent web search returned the explicit negative "The search results do not contain specific published studies applying mtscATAC-seq to uterine NK cells in the decidua or endometrium." The only tissue-facing extensions of the method are generic (Cryo-mtscATAC-seq for archived human tissue, bioRxiv 2025.09.17.675534 / PMC12458196; mitochondrial clone tracing in spatially intact tissue, bioRxiv 2025.07.11.664452) and contain no reproductive-tract material.
(3) barcode + NK / lentiviral barcoding + lymphocyte: only the rhesus HSPC-barcoding series (PMID 36605190/PMC9808525; PMID 24702997; PMID 29141868; PMID 40621477). PMC9808525 Methods: "concurrent PB, BAL fluid, and lung, liver, spleen, jejunum, and colon tissue samples from 5 barcoded monkeys" — no uterus, no pregnancy. That paper itself notes NK cells "do not contain endogenous clonal markers," i.e. nobody had a clonal handle on tissue NK before barcoding.
(4) mouse fate mapping / Confetti / Polylox / CRISPR recorder: Polylox/Confetti/Brainbow/CRISPR-recorder crossed with NK or ILC returned nothing relevant in any index. The uterine mouse fate-map literature that does exist stops before delivery or answers a different question — Tbx21-Cre x Rosa26-RFP dNK fate mapping (PMID 41782473, PMC12961421) runs GD6 to GD16-18 only, with no postpartum or second-pregnancy arm; Rorc(gt)-Cre x R26R in Filipovic (PMID 30374017) is used only to label ex-ILC3s; parabiosis + intravascular labelling (PMID 39708955) addresses whether uterine trNK come from circulating cNK in non-pregnant mice; BrdU local proliferation (PMID 30275046) is not clonal.
(5) Corroborating silence: the field's own dedicated review of uterine ILC memory (PMID 35774779, PMC9237338) contains 0 occurrences of "lineage tracing," 0 of "fate map," 0 of "postpartum," and states the position as speculation: "Persisting changes in uterine immune cells (i.e. on their memory properties) may be related to improved pregnancy outcomes in second pregnancies. We speculate that..." Nothing published 2022-2026 in my searches changes that.
(6) The compartment pairing this claim needs has apparently never even been assembled non-clonally: searches for human postpartum uterine/endometrial NK returned no study sampling the human uterine lining after delivery for NK phenotype, let alone paired to that woman's own pregnancy decidua.
(7) The claim's own source lineage is phenotypic throughout: Gamliel 2018 (PMID 29768178) is NKG2C/LILRB1 flow + RNA-seq + ATAC on primigravid vs multigravid decidua, and the follow-up (PMID 38215172, PMC10826933) is functional (F. nucleatum protection). Neither contains a postpartum sample or any clonal marker.
o.nearest_occupant:
Four distinct near-misses; none adjudicates the claim.

1. NEAREST ON METHOD — Rueckert T, Lareau CA, Mashreghi MF, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022. PMID 36289449 (PMC9663309). Exactly the assay R4 would need: mtscATAC-seq/ASAP-seq with somatic mtDNA variants as endogenous barcodes in ex vivo human NK cells, resolving NKG2C+ adaptive clonotypes, plus longitudinal re-sampling of 3 HCMV+ donors at 7, 11 and 19 months showing the same mtDNA clones persist in stable epigenetic states. DIFFERENCES: (a) peripheral blood exclusively — no tissue compartment of any kind, so it cannot separate local tissue persistence from a blood-resident clone; (b) the "training" stimulus is HCMV, not pregnancy; (c) no uterus/endometrium/decidua and no pregnant or postpartum donors; (d) persistence is tested in a compartment that is not shed and regenerated, whereas R4's whole difficulty is that the uterine lining is cyclically shed.

2. NEAREST ON THE ACTUAL BIOLOGICAL QUESTION (human, origin axis) — Strunz B, Ivarsson MA, ... Bjorkstrom NK. "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation." Sci Transl Med 2026;18(840):eadp2583. PMID 41811987. Human endometrium after uterus transplant (UTx) or HSCT, with per-cell donor-vs-recipient assignment by SNP genotype demultiplexing in scRNA-seq and by disparate HLA expression in high-parameter flow. Result: "Recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant, whereas HSCT resulted in near-complete donor-derived immune reconstitution, including formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes"; in one patient male-origin cells reconstituted the endometrium. This is the strongest published evidence bearing on R4's competing hypothesis — that the uterine NK niche is refilled from circulating/marrow-derived precursors rather than by local persistence. DIFFERENCES: (a) donor-vs-recipient genotype is a TWO-WAY label, not clone-level resolution — it cannot tell you whether any individual dNK clone persisted; (b) the subjects are transplanted, tacrolimus-immunosuppressed women, so turnover kinetics are not those of an unmanipulated postpartum uterus; (c) no pregnancy dNK timepoint is tracked across delivery; the design is "how does an emptied/replaced compartment refill," not "does this pregnancy's dNK clone survive parturition."
   Companion: PMID 41811989 (PMC13095030, Sci Transl Med 2026) shows uNK tissue-residency loss after UTx under NFAT inhibition — phenotype/scRNA-seq, no lineage.
   Predecessor: Strunz et al. Sci Immunol 2021, PMID 33617461 — uterus transplantation + monozygotic twins + humanized mice showing "the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation and that it was under genetic control." Same limitation: origin/replenishment, not clonal, no postpartum dNK.

3. NEAREST ON THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM (mouse) — Filipovic I, Chiossone L, ... Colucci F. "Molecular definition of group 1 innate lymphoid cells in the mouse uterus." Nat Commun 2018. PMID 30374017 (PMC6206068). Uniquely, it samples the exact timepoint series R4 cares about — postpartum days 1, 10 and 18 — and reports that ILC1 frequency and absolute number "raise 4-5 fold in second pregnancies," with CXCR6 upregulated. DIFFERENCES: this is a frequency/phenotype argument, not a lineage one. No barcoding, no Confetti/Polylox, no adoptive transfer, no parabiosis, no BrdU; the only fate map (Rorc(gt)-Cre x R26R) is used to identify ex-ILC3s, not to test whether the second-pregnancy ILC1s descend from the first-pregnancy pool. Expansion-in-second-pregnancy is exactly as consistent with de novo re-differentiation from circulating precursors as with persistence.

4. NEAREST MOUSE FATE MAP IN dNK — Mohamed MA, ... Stanic AK. "T-bet Fate Mapping Reveals Gestational Stage-Specific Transcriptional Adaptation of Decidual NK Cells." Am J Reprod Immunol 2026. PMID 41782473 (PMC12961421). Tbx21-Cre x Rosa26-RFP permanently marks cells with a history of T-bet expression, tracked in uterus/decidua/placenta. DIFFERENCES: an expression-history reporter, not a clonal marker (all RFP+ cells are one indistinguishable pool); the timecourse is GD6 through GD16-18 with no postpartum and no second-pregnancy arm; the question asked is state plasticity (T-bet loss, ILC2/ILC3-like drift) not persistence.
