b.why:
The claim has two separable readings and only the weaker one is a lineage question. (a) "dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 are the same or different lineages" would be DECIDABLE (template 3). (b) "a differentiation ORDERING exists among them" — a directed arrow, e.g. dNK3->dNK2->dNK1 — is what the claim actually asserts, and it is NOT decidable from the primitive. Three reasons.

(1) REVERSIBLE, MILIEU-INSTRUCTED STATE WITHIN ONE LINEAGE. The subset labels are graded surface/transcriptional states that the decidual environment sets and that are demonstrably inducible on the timescale of the assay itself: in Guo 2021 (PMID 33390590) CD39 — the marker that defines dNK1 in Guo's own ATAC sorting gate — is acquired within 2 days of culture by cells that lacked it; Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757) CyTOF shows Eomes/T-bet as intermediate/graded across dNK1/2/3, not binary; Cheung 2026 (PMID 41999228) shows TGF-beta instructing dNK2-vs-dNK3 marker composition from a pluripotent source. Under "an ordering exists" and under "no ordering — three interconvertible, signal-instructed states of one decidual NK lineage", the PREDICTED CLONAL STRUCTURE IS IDENTICAL: clones spanning all three subsets. Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is exactly the reversible-state carve-out.

(2) SHARED ANCESTRY CARRIES NO DIRECTION. "Share an ancestor and how recently" yields a tree; painting subset labels on its tips gives a direction ONLY under the added assumption that the label is heritable and transitions are rare or irreversible — precisely the assumption in dispute. With reversible labels, dNK2->dNK1 at rate r and dNK1->dNK2 at rate r' combined with differential proliferation generate the same tree. The topology is not identifiable, and there are three published mutually contradictory topologies to choose among.

(3) SINGLE TERMINAL TIMEPOINT. Decidua is destructively sampled once per pregnancy, so "how recently" cannot be anchored to real time or to a second observation of the same clone, and subset frequencies shift with gestational age through differential proliferation/recruitment/attrition — which changes subclone sizes with zero cells changing identity.

EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF THE LIMIT: the only study to put DNA barcodes on human NK subsets (Vo et al. 2024, PMID 38484189; CellTag lentiviral barcoding of CD34+ progenitors, progeny sorted into ILC3 / S3b-NK / S4-NK) concluded verbatim "clonal bias was only observed between ILC3 and NK cell subsets but not within the NK cell stages." Reading (a) succeeded and reading (b) went flat, in the same experiment, with the same tool.
b.action_if_yes:
DESIGN BEING ADJUDICATED: mtscATAC-seq / MAESTER on hashed, FACS-sorted dNK1 (CD39+CD18-CD103-), dNK2 (CD18+CD39-CD103-) and dNK3 (CD18+CD103+) from a single first-trimester decidua, asking whether somatic mtDNA clones are shared across the three subsets.

YES = clones are shared; the three subsets sit inside common recent clades.

NEXT EXPERIMENT: precisely the one you would run with no lineage data at all — a directional/perturbation experiment to supply the arrow the barcodes do not contain. Concretely: a gestational-age series (6->14 wk) with subset composition tracked, plus decidual explant or endometrial-organoid co-culture with TGF-beta / IL-15 / HLA-C-KIR-ligand manipulation, re-phenotyping on the FULL multi-marker dNK1 identity (KIR, LILRB1, granzyme/perforin, glycolytic programme) rather than CD39 alone. Nothing about the barcode result changes which perturbation you run, which of the three contradictory published topologies you favour, or how you read the outcome.

WHY THIS ARM IS VACUOUS: YES is the near-certain a priori outcome. dNK contain an overt proliferating cluster (dNKp) in both Vento-Tormo 2018 and Guo 2021, and mouse uterine trNK accumulate by LOCAL proliferation with no contribution from migrating NK (Sojka 2018, PMID 30275046). A locally expanded compartment whose states are milieu-set will share clones across states — that is the prediction before any experiment. Confirming it moves nothing.
b.action_if_no:
NO = the three subsets are clonally disjoint; no mtDNA clone spans dNK1/dNK2/dNK3.

NEXT EXPERIMENT: this would refute the ordering outright, and the follow-up is to chase each subset's separate origin using the same mtDNA variants — match dNK1/2/3 clonotypes against paired maternal peripheral-blood NK drawn at the same procedure, and against pre-pregnancy endometrium if any is available, to ask whether each subset is separately seeded from the circulation or separately maintained in situ.

WHY THIS ARM IS WEAK RATHER THAN VACUOUS: (i) it is the same assay extended to one additional compartment, not a different kind of experiment; (ii) the NO result is close to unreachable with this primitive, because absence of shared mtDNA clones is an UNDERPOWERED NULL — it is governed by how many informative heteroplasmies that particular donor carries, capture depth, and cells recovered per subset, and there is no calibration for what clone-sharing "should" look like in a polyclonal, locally expanded decidual NK pool. A null therefore reads "not enough informative variants", whose follow-up is "repeat the assay with more variants/cells", i.e. the same experiment again.
b.both_answers_reason:
The dominant arm is vacuous, which is sufficient to fail B2. YES (clones span the three subsets) is both the a-priori expected outcome AND leaves the next experiment byte-identical to the no-data next experiment, because direction is simply not present in clonal data when the state is reversible. NO is not vacuous in principle — it would kill the ordering and redirect toward separate seeding — but it is not reliably reachable from this primitive (an underpowered null indistinguishable from insufficient mtDNA informativeness), and its follow-up is the same assay on one added compartment. So one arm is a near-certain confirmation that changes nothing, and the other is an ambiguous null whose action is "run it better". They do not fork the research programme. OUT.

Note the asymmetry cleanly: the primitive can FALSIFY an ordering (by showing separate lineages) but cannot ESTABLISH one. A one-sided test whose informative side is the improbable side, and whose probable side is inert, is exactly the failure mode B2 is designed to catch.
b.compartments_needed:
INDEX COMPARTMENTS (all three required simultaneously): dNK1, dNK2 and dNK3 from the SAME first-trimester decidua (6-14 gestational weeks), sorted on the published gates (dNK1 CD39+CD18-CD103-; dNK2 CD18+CD39-CD103-; dNK3 CD18+CD103+), ideally with the proliferating dNKp fraction retained as the within-tissue clonal anchor.

REFERENCE COMPARTMENTS (required only for the NO arm / origin question): paired maternal peripheral-blood NK from the same woman at the same procedure; pre-pregnancy (or non-pregnant) endometrium from the same woman; a bone-marrow / NK-precursor compartment from the same woman.
b.compartments_obtainable:
PARTIAL — the index compartments are trivially co-obtainable; every reference compartment is not.

OBTAINABLE PAIRED FROM ONE HUMAN: dNK1 + dNK2 + dNK3 all live in a single cell suspension from one decidual specimen, so the "compartment A and B simultaneously from the same individual" requirement is met better here than for almost any other claim in this screen. This is S1's one genuine strength. Paired maternal peripheral blood is routinely drawn at the same procedure (Vento-Tormo 2018 used 6 matched blood donors).

ONLY AT SURGERY, AND ONLY DURING PREGNANCY: first-trimester decidua is obtained only at elective surgical termination — or by D&C after embryo demise, which is the disease arm and not a control. The specimen is terminal for that individual: one timepoint per woman, no re-sampling, no follow-up, no before/after within a subject. This is what removes the time axis the ordering claim needs.

NOT OBTAINABLE: pre-pregnancy endometrium from the SAME woman who later supplies the decidua (would require a prospective biopsy in a woman who subsequently conceives and terminates — vanishingly rare); bone marrow or any NK-precursor compartment from the same pregnant woman. Post-mortem access is neither required nor useful here.

NOT AVAILABLE IN MOUSE: dNK1/2/3 is a human-only taxonomy resting on KIR and LILRB1 and on HLA-C/HLA-G engagement. Mice have no KIR and no HLA-G; mouse uterine NK are classified DBA-lectin+/- (PMID 22875907). The most recent mouse decidual fate-mapping study (PMID 41782473, Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre across gestation) itself attributes dNK1/2/3 to human scRNA-seq and never assigns them in mouse. So the one species where a genetic clonal recorder (Confetti, Polylox, CRISPR recorder) could be deployed does not contain the entities the claim is about.
b.compartment_notes:
MOUSE_ONLY = FALSE, but the inverse problem applies and is worth flagging explicitly: this claim is HUMAN-ONLY. The entity does not exist in mouse, so the powerful genetic clonal recorders cannot be brought to bear, and the human-only status is itself part of why B1/B2 fail — you are left with endogenous mtDNA on a one-shot surgical specimen.

TECHNIQUE IS NOT THE BLOCKER. Nothing in B3 fails for methodological reasons. mtDNA clonal tracing is mature in human tissue (mtscATAC-seq, PMID 36792778/36807073; Cryo-mtscATAC for archived tissue, PMID 41000852; MAESTER-style mtDNA enrichment from scRNA-seq, PMID 35210612), has been applied to human uterus (endometrial gland lineage tracing, PMID 32476144 — epithelium, not NK), and has been applied to human tissue NK cells (Liu et al., PMID 40777278 / Cancer Cell 2026: mtscATAC on 124,958 cells from matched NSCLC tumour / non-involved lung / blood plus 93,757 ovarian cells; found expanded tumour-restricted NK clones and high innate-cell clone sharing). The claim fails on inferential structure, not on tissue access or assay maturity.

NK LACKS AN ENDOGENOUS BARCODE. Unlike T and B cells, NK cells have no rearranged germline receptor to serve as a natural clonal marker (stated as the motivating problem in the macaque tissue-NK barcoding study, PMID 36605190). So the T-cell field's cheap adjudication route (TCR clonotype sharing across subsets from one specimen) does not transfer, mtDNA is the only human option, and lentiviral barcoding requires a transplant model (macaque, humanized mouse) — none of which contains a human decidua.

G4 CROSS-FIELD OCCUPANCY. The same structural question has been run with clonal tools in adjacent fields and the pattern is consistent: the tools resolve BETWEEN-lineage separation and myeloid/B differentiation direction, but not ordering within an NK compartment. Liu 2026 (PMID 40777278) resolved directional differentiation for monocyte->macrophage/DC and B->plasma but reported only expansion and clone sharing for NK. Vo 2024 (PMID 38484189) resolved ILC3-vs-NK divergence by barcode but explicitly found no clonal bias WITHIN the NK stages. In mouse decidua, the T-bet fate map (PMID 41782473) found "subset redistribution" across gestation and concluded "rather than undergoing lineage diversion", i.e. composition shift without ordering — the exact confound S1 would have to defeat.

OCCUPANCY SEARCH HONESTY (G3). Targeted searches for mtDNA / mtscATAC / MAESTER / barcode lineage tracing applied to decidua or decidual NK returned no hits (PubMed boolean "(decidua OR maternal-fetal interface) AND (mitochondrial) AND (single-cell) AND (clonal OR lineage)" n=0; "(decidual) AND (natural killer) AND (lineage tracing OR clonal OR barcod*)" returned only off-target reviews; WebSearch surfaced nothing). I would record that as "no hit found" rather than a firm negative — the search was narrow enough that it should not be scored as a confident FALSE for occupancy.

b.why:
DECIDABLE in its pool-level form, with a large and explicitly stated undecidable residue that covers the claim's numbered indices. The claim has to be split, because its two halves fall on opposite sides of the rubric.

(i) DECIDABLE HALF — POOL-LEVEL CARRIAGE. "The decidual uNK pool is the progeny of the pre-conception endometrial uNK pool" is the rubric's "the progeny of A are B" form, and — more decisively — its live rival is itself a PURE CLONAL-STRUCTURE statement, so the fork is exactly what the primitive returns and essentially nothing else in human can settle it. The two rivals are both on the record and both supported by evidence of a stronger class than the claim's own INF_MARKER. Carriage: Sojka 2018 (PMID 30275046), mouse Ncr1 reporter + parabiosis + induced deciduoma — "the accumulated uNK cells were proliferating trNK cells; migrating NK cells made no contribution." Re-recruitment: Greene 2025 (PMID 40672293) — "uNKs derive from circulatory cells in the peripheral blood which immigrate into the endometrium and become resident as they reconstitute the uterine lining after menses"; Strunz 2026 (PMID 41811987), SNP-demultiplexed uterus transplant — "recipient-derived immune cells replaced donor immune cells after uterus transplant"; Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955), parabiosis — uterine trNK "are derived from peripheral cNK cells" under progesterone control. Choosing between these is asking whether a decidual NK cell shares a recent ancestor with a pre-conception endometrium-resident NK cell or only with the contemporaneous circulating pool. Ancestor-sharing plus recency, nothing else.

The "HOW RECENTLY" clause is load-bearing, not decorative. Every NK cell in one woman shares an HSPC ancestor, so bare ancestor-sharing is trivially TRUE under both models. The discriminating readout is whether the decidual repertoire is a low-diversity, bottlenecked subsample of the woman's PRIOR endometrial repertoire (carriage + local expansion) or an unbiased sample of her CONTEMPORANEOUS blood repertoire (recruitment). Note also that the negative is the decisive direction: clonal discordance between prior endometrium and later decidua, against a blood baseline, falsifies carriage outright.

(ii) NOT DECIDABLE — THE NUMBERED 1:1 ARROW uNK1->dNK1, uNK2->dNK2, uNK3->dNK3. This is the rubric's reversible-state case and it fails for the stated reason: both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure. uNK1/2/3 are gated on CD39/CD103/CD49a/KIR/LILRB1 — inducible surface molecules, not heritable marks. Strunz 2021 (PMID 33617461) reports a CONTINUUM with sequential KIR-then-CD39 acquisition driven by IL-15; Greene 2025 attributes the divergent subsets to differential TGF-beta responsiveness of blood-derived precursors AFTER they immigrate; and Cheung 2025 (PMID 41279445 / PMC12637421) derives dNK1/2/3-like subtypes de novo from induced pluripotent stem cells, i.e. the three states are reachable from a starting cell that has never been in a uterus. Consequence: a barcode shared between an endometrial uNK1 and a decidual dNK1 is produced equally by (a) a uNK1 cell carried forward retaining its state, (b) a carried clone of any state re-differentiating into the dNK1 state under local TGF-beta/IL-15, or (c) one clone spanning all three states. Lineage cannot order or attribute a state that is re-inducible from outside the compartment, so the subset indices are not adjudicable by this primitive.

One sub-question inside (ii) IS decidable and should be separated out rather than conflated: "are uNK1/2/3 three separate lineages or three states of one lineage?" — clonal confinement versus clonal sharing across the three gates is the rubric's explicit same/different-lineage case. But answering it does not rescue the arrow; it only reports whether the numbering denotes lineages at all. And Phase A found the gates themselves may not be stable entities to test: Whettlock's own term decidual uNK form ONE cluster when analysed alone and three only after integration with the other datasets, and Guo 2024 recovers a different partition on identical markers.

NET: TRUE, because the load-bearing scientific fork this claim actually turns on (carriage vs re-recruitment) is a clonal-structure question and this primitive is definitionally competent to settle it. The claim should be carried forward only in its rewritten pool-level form; the "1/2/3" indices must be dropped from anything that goes to Phase C, because they are not decidable.

PRACTICAL CAVEAT, recorded here but not allowed to flip B1 (which is about in-principle decidability): the only human-usable mark is endogenous, and NK cells have no rearranged receptor to serve as an endogenous clonal marker — Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) says this explicitly and is why lentiviral barcodes were needed in macaque. So the human readout must be mtDNA variants (mtscATAC/MAESTER) or somatic mutation, whose discriminating power scales with prior clonal expansion. That is a Phase C power question, not a decidability question.
b.action_if_yes:
IF YES — decidual NK clones descend from clones that were resident in the endometrium BEFORE conception, at a sharing rate above the same woman's blood baseline.

TWO CONCRETE NEXT EXPERIMENTS, neither of which is the adjudicating experiment repeated.

(1) MECHANISTIC, AND THE ONE I WOULD DO FIRST — locate the reservoir that survives menstruation. Carriage across a conception is only possible if some uNK clones persist through the shedding of the functionalis, and the immediate unanswered question becomes WHERE. Design: serial clonal census of menstrual effluent from the SAME woman across >=3 consecutive cycles, with a paired peripheral blood draw each cycle. Menstrual effluent is a validated source of uterine NK with a KIR repertoire markedly distinct from blood (PMID 27271316), and it is non-invasive, so serial within-woman sampling is actually possible here in a way it is not for biopsy. Readout: do the same clones reappear cycle after cycle (a persistent reservoir reseeding each regenerated functionalis) or is each cycle's uNK repertoire clonally fresh and blood-derived (in which case carriage across a pregnancy must run through some non-functionalis compartment, and the basalis becomes the target)? Different compartment, different timescale, non-pregnant subjects — and a question that is only worth asking once carriage is established.

(2) TRANSLATIONAL, WITH A DIFFERENT ENDPOINT — power the clinical test whose premise this claim silently is. Pre-conception mid-luteal endometrial uNK assays are already being run and cut-offs already published (PMID 36592442, PMID 25150956, PMID 38164429), and Woon 2022 (PMID 36713400) reasons explicitly from pre-conception endometrial uNK1/2/3 to what will happen to extravillous trophoblast in a later pregnancy. If carriage holds, that inference is legitimate and the next experiment is the prospective cohort that has never been run: recruit in recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics where the biopsy is happening anyway, clone-census it, follow to live birth, and test whether CLONE-LEVEL structure of the pre-conception pool (clonal diversity, size of the clones that get carried, KIR genotype of the carried fraction) predicts outcome better than the current frequency/percentage readout. Endpoint = live birth, measured quantity = clonal, neither of which appears in the adjudicating experiment.
b.action_if_no:
IF NO — decidual NK cells are clonally unrelated to the woman's own pre-conception endometrial pool, and instead nest inside her contemporaneous circulating repertoire.

This branch is NOT "conclude the model is wrong and move on," because a NO answer LOCALIZES the source, and three mutually exclusive candidate sources are already named in this literature and are all sortable at a single surgical event.

CONCRETE NEXT EXPERIMENT — the multi-compartment source-hunt, run cross-sectionally at one termination or caesarean, from one woman: clonal census of decidua basalis, decidua parietalis, adjacent non-decidualized endometrium, decidua-resident CD34+/stage-3 NK precursors (Vacca 2011, PMID 21248224, per the Phase A adversarial pass), and contemporaneous peripheral blood. Ask which compartment's clone set the decidual NK cells sit inside. Three distinguishable outcomes, each with a different follow-on: (a) decidual clones = contemporaneous blood NK clones -> recruitment of circulating NK, and the target for any pre-conception assay moves to blood; (b) decidual clones nest inside the decidual CD34+ precursor clones and NOT inside blood NK clones -> in-situ differentiation from a resident progenitor, and the compartment to profile and to perturb is the progenitor, not the NK cell; (c) decidual clones match neither -> the source is the unsampled basalis, which tells you the sampling scheme, not the biology, was wrong. Note this is a different DESIGN from the adjudicating experiment — single-timepoint, multi-compartment, cross-sectional, no pre-conception arm — not the same experiment rerun.

SECOND, DIRECTLY CONSEQUENTIAL ACTION: a NO answer says the pre-conception endometrial uNK assay currently in clinical use is measuring a compartment that is discarded before the pregnancy it claims to predict. The next experiment is then the head-to-head assay-replacement study — does a blood-based precursor census (whatever compartment (a)/(b) identifies) outperform the mid-luteal endometrial biopsy at predicting live birth in the SAME women? That is a costly, concrete, falsifiable programme, not a shrug.

DISAMBIGUATION BUILT INTO THE NO BRANCH, worth preregistering: a bare NO is confounded by menstruation — the functionalis you biopsied pre-conception is shed by design, so "no clonal continuity" could mean recruitment OR could mean you sampled cells that were destined to be shed while their relatives in the basalis were retained. The contemporaneous blood comparison resolves this asymmetrically: a POSITIVE match of decidual clones to contemporaneous blood establishes recruitment regardless of the shedding confound. So the NO branch must be scored as "decidua matches blood," not merely "decidua fails to match prior endometrium."
b.both_answers_reason:
TRUE, but ONLY for the pool-level reading, and I want the scope condition on the record because the claim as literally written fails this filter.

WHY IT PASSES AT POOL LEVEL. The two branches are not the same experiment and neither is vacuous. YES sends you to serial menstrual-effluent clonal census across cycles in NON-PREGNANT women, asking whether a reservoir persists through shedding — longitudinal, non-invasive, different subjects, different compartment. NO sends you to a single-timepoint multi-compartment sort at termination/caesarean (basalis, parietalis, adjacent endometrium, decidual CD34+ precursors, contemporaneous blood), asking which pre-named source the decidual clones nest inside — cross-sectional, surgical, different compartments. Different tissues, different timescales, different hypotheses, different follow-ons.

THE STRONGEST REASON THIS IS NOT A VACUITY TRAP: both answers are currently live, and each is backed by evidence of a class stronger than the claim's own INF_MARKER, so the field would be moved either way rather than merely confirmed one way. Pro-carriage: Sojka 2018 (PMID 30275046) mouse parabiosis, migrating NK contribute nothing during decidualization. Pro-recruitment: Strunz 2026 (PMID 41811987) SNP-resolved human uterus-transplant chimerism, recipient cells replace donor endometrial immune cells; Greene 2025 (PMID 40672293); Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955). The mouse literature is split against itself and the human transplant evidence is from a non-physiological replacement setting, so neither answer is already banked.

AND BOTH BRANCHES BITE ON THE SAME REAL-WORLD DECISION, in opposite directions: a pre-conception endometrial uNK assay is already being sold with published cut-offs (PMID 36592442, PMID 25150956, PMID 38164429) and Woon 2022 (PMID 36713400) reasons from pre-conception endometrial uNK1/2/3 to later trophoblast interaction. YES -> power that assay prospectively against live birth using clone-level structure. NO -> the assay is sampling a discarded compartment and must be rebuilt on the compartment that actually seeds decidua. Two different, expensive, non-interchangeable programmes.

WHERE IT FAILS, STATED PLAINLY. For the numbered arrow as written (uNK1->dNK1 etc.) B2 fails outright and the claim in that form is OUT: if the answer is YES you cannot separate "uNK1 was carried and kept its state" from "a carried clone re-acquired the CD39+CD103- state under decidual TGF-beta/IL-15," and if the answer is NO you cannot separate "different lineages" from "the same clone changed state." Both answers produce identical clonal structure and neither licenses a different next experiment — the definition of failing this filter. Cheung 2025 (PMID 41279445) makes this concrete by generating dNK1/2/3-like subtypes from iPSC, i.e. the state labels carry no lineage information at all.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE SHORTLIST: carry S2 forward ONLY as "is the decidual uNK pool clonally continuous with the pre-conception endometrial uNK pool, against a same-woman blood baseline?" Drop the 1/2/3 indices. If the preregistration insists the indices are the claim, then S2 is OUT on B2.
b.compartments_needed:
Adjudication needs, from ONE woman, at TWO separated timepoints:

A. PRE-CONCEPTION ENDOMETRIUM (functionalis, mid-luteal / window of implantation) — the putative source pool.
B. PERIPHERAL BLOOD AT THE SAME PRE-CONCEPTION TIMEPOINT — not optional. This is the null against which any A-to-C clone sharing must be scored; without it, shared ancestry is uninterpretable because every NK cell in the woman shares an HSPC ancestor.
C. DECIDUA FROM THE SUBSEQUENT PREGNANCY (first-trimester decidua basalis preferred; term decidua/basal plate as the feasible substitute) — the putative product pool.
D. PERIPHERAL BLOOD CONTEMPORANEOUS WITH C — required to score the recruitment model positively rather than inferring it from a failed match to A (see the shedding confound in action_if_no).

Needed additionally only on the NO branch, all obtainable at the same surgical event as C:
E. DECIDUA PARIETALIS and ADJACENT NON-DECIDUALIZED ENDOMETRIUM.
F. DECIDUA-RESIDENT CD34+/stage-3 NK PRECURSORS (Vacca 2011, PMID 21248224).

Needed to root the clone tree (i.e. to convert "share an ancestor" into "how recently"), and essentially never available:
G. BONE MARROW / HSPC compartment from the same woman.

Needed only if one insists on testing the shedding-reservoir hypothesis directly:
H. BASALIS / deep endometrium — see compartment_notes; this one is structurally unobtainable in the required pairing.
b.compartments_obtainable:
PARTIAL — obtainable in the feasible pairing, low-yield in the fully-specified pairing, and one required compartment is structurally impossible.

A (pre-conception endometrium): YES, easily. Outpatient Pipelle biopsy, no anaesthetic, already routine in recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics where uNK is quantified as standard (PMID 36592442, PMID 25150956, PMID 38164429). Repeatable across cycles. NON-INVASIVE SERIAL ALTERNATIVE EXISTS AND IS VALIDATED: menstrual effluent yields uterine NK whose KIR repertoire is "markedly different from those in peripheral blood NK cells," sampled paired with peripheral blood in the same women (PMID 27271316). This is the single biggest feasibility advantage S2 has over the other pregnancy-gated rows in this screen — it gives serial within-woman pre-conception sampling of the source compartment without a procedure.

B and D (blood at both timepoints): YES, trivially. Venipuncture.

C (decidua from the SAME woman's subsequent pregnancy): THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT, and it is doubly gated — ONLY DURING PREGNANCY and ONLY AT SURGERY. First/second-trimester decidua exists only via elective termination or miscarriage; term decidua only at caesarean or delivery. So the fully-specified design requires a woman who (i) consented to a pre-conception research sample, (ii) then conceived, and (iii) then terminated or miscarried that pregnancy. You cannot plan this, only enrich for it — recruiting in recurrent-miscarriage clinics raises the conversion rate because the subsequent-loss base rate is high and those women are already being biopsied. ASCERTAINMENT BIAS TO PREREGISTER: the first-trimester decidua you can actually obtain in a paired design comes disproportionately from losses, which is precisely the population whose uNK biology is hypothesised to be abnormal. THE FEASIBLE SUBSTITUTE: pre-conception endometrium (or serial menstrual effluent) paired with TERM decidua at elective caesarean is fully obtainable, single-timepoint, and unbiased by loss. Its cost is that at term the three-subset structure collapses anyway (Whettlock's term uNK form ONE cluster analysed alone, three only after integration), so the term design can answer pool-level carriage and nothing about subset structure — which is exactly the scope B1 says is decidable, so this is an acceptable trade.

E and F: YES, same surgical event as C, no extra access cost. F is at the edge of feasibility on cell number (Vacca sorted only hundreds of decidual CD34+ cells per well).

G (bone marrow, to root the tree): NO. Not obtainable from termination or caesarean donors; a marrow aspirate is never taken alongside either. So "how recently" must be estimated from clone-size structure and the blood baseline rather than from a rooted phylogeny.

H (basalis / deep endometrium): STRUCTURALLY UNOBTAINABLE IN THE REQUIRED PAIRING. The basalis requires hysterectomy or a deceased donor — Garcia-Alonso 2021 (PMID 34857954) used 6 deceased-donor whole uteri for exactly this reason. Hysterectomy ends fertility, so NO WOMAN CAN SUPPLY BOTH HER BASALIS AND HER LATER DECIDUA. This is a permanent hole, and it sits under the strongest confound in the design (functionalis shedding), which is why the menstrual-effluent serial census in action_if_yes is the workaround rather than a luxury.

THE ONE HUMAN SETTING WHERE THE PRIMITIVE IS FREE AND THE PAIRING ALREADY EXISTS: uterus-transplant recipients. Donor-vs-recipient SNP and HLA disparity supplies a permanent, cell-intrinsic lineage label with no barcoding and no mtDNA power problem, and these women are serially biopsied before pregnancy and then deliver by caesarean, so A and C come from one woman by construction. Strunz 2026 (PMID 41811987) has already run the SNP demultiplex on non-pregnant endometrium in this cohort; Asiimwe 2026 (PMID 41811989) is the same cohort. THREE CAVEATS: n is very small (uterus transplant is rare, and rarer still with a live birth); recipients are on tacrolimus, which Strunz 2026 itself shows inhibits NFAT and "affected de novo induction of tissue-residency features in vitro," so the residency biology under test is pharmacologically perturbed; and donor/recipient is a TWO-BIN label, not a clone-level one — it answers "was the pool replaced from circulation" but returns no clone-level recency and no subset-resolved structure.
b.compartment_notes:
MOUSE STATUS, both directions. mouse_only = FALSE: the human version is obtainable (see compartments_obtainable), and one human cohort — uterus transplant — even supplies the lineage label for free. But the reverse also holds and matters more for Phase C: MOUSE CANNOT ADDRESS THE CLAIM AS WRITTEN. Mouse uterine ILCs partition as trNK / cNK / ILC1; there is no KIR, no HLA-C, no LILRB1, no EVT invasion at human depth, and no uNK1/2/3 or dNK1/2/3 equivalent. So the subset-indexed claim is human-only by construction. The pool-level claim IS mouse-tractable and every instrument is available paired within one animal (pre-mating uterine horn vs post-implantation decidua, induced deciduoma in one horn, parabiosis, Ncr1 reporters, congenic transfer, Confetti/Polylox/CRISPR recorders) — and it has already been attacked there twice, with conflicting results from the same laboratory: Sojka 2018 (PMID 30275046) found accumulated uNK during decidualization are locally proliferating trNK with no contribution from migrating cells, while Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955) found uterine trNK are derived from peripheral cNK under progesterone control. These are not strictly contradictory (different timescales — establishment of the resident pool at puberty vs expansion during decidualization) but they mean a mouse arm would be re-entering a contested question rather than settling a fresh one.

WHY A HUMAN ARM IS UNAVOIDABLE EVEN THOUGH MOUSE IS EASIER: the entire downstream dependency (pre-conception endometrial uNK subset testing in reproductive-failure clinics, PMID 36713400) is a human clinical inference about KIR/LILRB1 engagement of HLA-C/HLA-G on EVT. None of those molecules exists in mouse. A mouse-only answer cannot touch the thing that makes this claim load-bearing.

MARKING SUBSTRATE. NK cells have no rearranged germline receptor to serve as an endogenous clonal marker — Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190, methods read and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/S2B_PMC9808525.txt) states this explicitly and is why lentiviral HSPC barcoding was required to track tissue-resident NK across liver, spleen, lung and gut in macaque. Prospective labelling is impossible in a human pregnancy, so the human readout must be endogenous: mtDNA variants via mtscATAC-seq/MAESTER, or somatic mutation. Phase A already recorded that mtDNA discriminating power degrades under weak clonal expansion, which is a live risk for a polyclonal uNK pool; that is a Phase C power question and should be preregistered as such, not treated as a decidability failure. The uterus-transplant cohort is the one human route that bypasses the marking substrate entirely, at the cost of n, tacrolimus perturbation, and two-bin resolution.

SEARCH STATUS (informational; B4 not in this schema): I searched mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER clonal tracing crossed with tissue-resident lymphocytes and with decidual/uterine NK, lentiviral barcoding crossed with NK and lymphocyte, Polylox/CRISPR-recorder/ILC fate mapping, paired pre-conception-endometrium-to-decidua designs, menstrual-effluent uNK sampling, and uterus-transplant chimerism. I found the primitive applied to tissue-resident NK in macaque (PMID 36605190) and to the uterine immune compartment via transplant chimerism in human (PMID 41811987), but NO clonal or mtDNA lineage tracing of uterine or decidual NK in any species, and no paired within-woman endometrium-to-decidua design. Phase A's adversarial pass reached the same conclusion independently. I am recording this as suggestive rather than as an established absence — several EPMC queries returned conference-abstract noise rather than clean negatives, so a Phase C occupancy check should re-run this before anyone relies on "nobody has done it."

b.why:
TRUE, but only for the ancestry half of the claim — which is also the load-bearing half.

S3 decomposes into two propositions that the evidence base conflates. (a) ANCESTRY: the dNK of a pregnancy are the progeny of the uterine NK resident in that same uterus before conception. This is the canonical "the progeny of A are B" form and is exactly what the clonal primitive delivers. (b) CONVERSION/FUNCTION: eNK are "special immature cells that await pregnancy" that acquire dNK function under IL-15 (Manaster 2008 PMID 18641324 — the INF_INVITRO source that sets Phase A's strongest class). (b) is the "A becomes functionally B-like" form and is NOT decidable by lineage: barcoding cannot say a cell acquired KIR-mediated licensing, IFN-g/VEGF output, or spiral-artery-remodelling capacity. A positive lineage answer licenses (a) only and must not be read as confirming (b). The row passes B1 because the downstream dependency (pre-conception uNK biopsy testing) rests on (a), not (b).

It escapes the reversible-state trap because the two live rival hypotheses predict DIFFERENT clonal structures, not the same one. Local persistence/expansion predicts dNK clone families enriched for families already resident in that woman's pre-conception endometrium, above what her contemporaneous circulating NK pool would supply. Recruitment/de novo generation (supported by Chantakru 2002 uterine grafts PMID 11751942, Chiossone 2014 PMID 24179150, Strunz 2026 STM chimerism after uterus/HSC transplant PMID 41811987, and by monthly shedding of the functionalis) predicts dNK clones drawn from the contemporaneous circulating spectrum with no uterus-specific enrichment. These differ in "how recently do these two cells share an ancestor", so the primitive discriminates.

Two caveats that are design requirements, not decidability failures. (i) The naive test is degenerate — every hematopoietic cell in one woman shares an ancestor — so the question must be posed as an ENRICHMENT test of pre-conception endometrial clone families in the pregnancy dNK pool against a contemporaneous autologous blood-NK reference, never as a bare shared-ancestor test. (ii) The pre-conception sample must come from the conception cycle, or be explicitly calibrated against measured cycle-to-cycle turnover, because the functionalis and most of its uNK are shed at every menstruation; a NO from a sample taken cycles earlier is uninformative about the cycle-to-pregnancy transition specifically, since those clones would have been lost to menstruation regardless of pregnancy.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = dNK clone families are significantly enriched for clones resident in that woman's pre-conception endometrium, above her contemporaneous blood-NK baseline.

Next experiment: the pre-conception uterine CLONE becomes the unit of prediction, so run a prospective clone-tracked outcome study in the population where the claim is load-bearing — recurrent-miscarriage / recurrent-implantation-failure clinics, which already take luteal-phase endometrial biopsies and already sell CD56+ uNK density as a triage test (PMID 35265977). Bank the conception-cycle pre-conception sample (menstrual-cup MNC and/or Pipelle biopsy), then genotype the ensuing pregnancy's decidua (products of conception at miscarriage, or decidua basalis at delivery) and ask: (1) WHICH pre-conception clones expand — is pregnancy a uniform expansion of the resident pool or a selective sweep of a minority of clones, which are opposite biological pictures both compatible with a bare YES; (2) whether a pre-conception CLONAL parameter (clone-size distribution, oligoclonality, the KIR/education phenotype carried by persisting clones) predicts outcome better than the density number currently sold, i.e. re-base the existing test on the clone rather than the cell count.

Second, distinct experiment enabled only by YES: test the Gamliel 2018 PTdNK "trained memory" claim (PMID 29768178) at clone level — decidua from pregnancy 1 and pregnancy 2 in the same woman, asking whether the NKG2C-hi/LILRB1-hi PTdNK of the second pregnancy are literally surviving clones of the first. That is the only version of the memory claim lineage can adjudicate, and it is incoherent under NO.
b.action_if_no:
NO = dNK clone families are drawn from the contemporaneous circulating spectrum with no enrichment for that woman's pre-conception endometrial clones — the compartment is refilled, not carried over.

Next experiment: the target compartment moves out of the uterus. (1) SOURCE ASSIGNMENT — paired within-pregnancy mtscATAC of decidua plus peripheral blood NK subsets plus circulating CD34+/CD56-bright precursors from the same woman, to assign the dNK founder clones to a specific circulating population rather than merely excluding the endometrium. This is a positive assignment, not a restatement of the negative. (2) TIMING — serial blood sampling across the peri-implantation window and early gestation to date when the founder clones leave the circulation. That defines the intervention window and cannot be recovered from the paired endpoint alone. (3) CLINICAL — a NO removes the lineage premise from pre-conception uNK biopsy testing, because the biopsy would be measuring a population that no longer exists by the time the outcome it predicts occurs. The actionable follow-up is a head-to-head predictive study: does a peri-conception BLOOD NK clonal/subset measure predict pregnancy outcome as well as or better than luteal-phase endometrial CD56+ density? A positive result replaces an invasive commercial test with a blood test; a negative result retires the biomarker rather than relocating it.

Compartment sampled, sampling schedule, and clinical decision all change relative to YES.
b.both_answers_reason:
The branches differ in compartment (uterus vs blood/precursor), in sampling schedule (single pre-conception timepoint vs serial peri-implantation series), and in clinical consequence (clonally re-base an existing test vs relocate or retire it). Neither is "conclude X and move on": the YES branch opens a selective-sweep-vs-uniform-expansion question and a clone-level test of the PTdNK memory claim, both incoherent under NO; the NO branch opens source assignment and recruitment-window dating, both meaningless under YES.

Three risks recorded, since B2 is meant to be strict rather than survivable. (i) The realistic result is quantitative, not binary — partial persistence plus partial recruitment. The design must PRE-SPECIFY the enrichment statistic and its threshold; without that, a mixed answer collapses both branches into "repeat with more donors", which would be vacuous and would flip this row to FALSE. (ii) Part of the NO branch's source assignment falls out of the primary experiment itself, if blood and precursor compartments are sampled at the outset. The genuinely new work under NO is therefore the timing series and the clinical head-to-head, and those two alone are what carry the NO branch — I am counting them, not the free assignment. (iii) The YES branch's follow-on requires the same hard longitudinal pairing again at cohort scale (see B3), so it is actionable but expensive; the NO branch's follow-on is cheap, since within-pregnancy blood+decidua pairing is trivially obtainable. The asymmetry in cost is real but does not make either branch vacuous.
b.compartments_needed:
Three, of which the blood reference is mandatory rather than optional.

A. Uterine/endometrial NK from the NON-PREGNANT cycling uterus of woman W, luteal/secretory phase, ideally of the conception cycle itself. Route: Pipelle/aspiration biopsy, or menstrual-cup mononuclear cells.
B. Decidual NK from the SAME woman W in her subsequent pregnancy: first-trimester decidua (6-15 wk, the canonical dNK compartment), or failing that decidua basalis at delivery.
C. Contemporaneous autologous peripheral blood NK at BOTH timepoints — the reference against which endometrium-specific clonal enrichment is measured. Without C the comparison is degenerate, because all of W's hematopoietic cells share ancestry and the test returns a trivial YES.

Desirable additions: serial menstrual-cup samples across consecutive non-conception cycles in the same woman, to calibrate baseline cycle-to-cycle clonal turnover from menstrual shedding; circulating CD34+/CD56-bright precursors for the NO-branch source assignment. Bone marrow would help but is not routinely obtainable in this population — drop it.
b.compartments_obtainable:
PARTIAL. Same individual: YES, but only longitudinally, prospectively, and with banking. Simultaneously: NO — and that is a logical impossibility rather than a logistics problem, since one uterus cannot be non-pregnant and decidualized at the same instant. A and B are necessarily separated by months to years.

Zero paired human samples exist in the located literature, and not for want of trying. The Phase A primary source says so outright (Feyaerts 2024 PMID 38571943: "we had no access to paired samples, i.e. endometrial and decidual NK cells from the same individual ... this poses inconceivable logistic and ethical barriers"), and I independently confirmed a second 2024 study repeating the identical unpaired architecture (Front Immunol 10.3389/fimmu.2024.1364036, Methods checked: n=4 non-pregnant endometrial biopsies vs n=4 DIFFERENT women's elective-termination first-trimester tissue).

Per compartment: A is easy — outpatient, non-surgical, repeatable, already routine in exactly the RM/RIF population where the claim is load-bearing; the menstrual-cup route is fully non-invasive and reproducible between women and cycles (PMID 24249743), though it remains an unvalidated proxy for biopsy in the same woman. C is trivial at both timepoints. B is the binding constraint: PREGNANCY-ONLY by definition and procedure-tethered — first-trimester decidua only at elective termination or from products of conception after miscarriage; term decidua basalis only at delivery/Caesarean. B is NOT post-mortem-only, NOT mouse-only, and needs no procedure that would not otherwise occur.

Three feasible pairing routes, with their costs. (1) RM/RIF prospective cohort — bank the luteal biopsy already being taken, capture first-trimester decidua from women who conceive and miscarry. Gives the canonical compartment, but the paired cohort is selected for pregnancy failure and may not represent normal pregnancy, which matters because recruitment-vs-persistence could itself differ in failing pregnancies. (2) Unselected cohort followed to delivery — high pairing yield, but the pregnancy compartment is term decidua, by which time uNK have declined and may not be the first-trimester dNK the claim is about. (3) Uterus-transplant recipients, serially biopsied for rejection surveillance and delivering by Caesarean, in whom donor/recipient genotype disparity supplies a lineage marker with no barcode needed — but the graft is immunosuppressed and denervated and its endometrium was itself newly reconstituted, so it does not model physiological cycling endometrium.

Point that revises the Phase A note: the pairing needs prospective BANKING, not prospective assay. mtDNA clonal genotyping now works on archived flash-frozen human tissue (Cryo-mtscATAC-seq, PMID 41000852) and on viably cryopreserved MNC, so pre-conception samples can be banked and genotyped retrospectively for only those women who go on to conceive. That converts "never obtainable from the same individual" into "obtainable at a per-pair yield set by the cohort's conception and miscarriage rates".
b.compartment_notes:
TIMING IS PART OF OBTAINABILITY HERE. The functionalis and most of its uNK are shed at every menstruation and the compartment is rebuilt afterwards, with the field's own reading being at least partial refilling from blood. Sample A must therefore come from the conception cycle, or be calibrated against baseline turnover measured by serial menstrual-cup sampling in the same woman. A sample taken several cycles earlier makes a NO answer uninterpretable, because those clones would have been lost to menstruation with or without pregnancy. This constrains the pairing design; it does not affect B1.

POWER. uNK are the dominant lymphocyte in both compartments (~70% of first-trimester decidual lymphocytes), so per-donor yield clears the pre-registered >=30 NK cells/donor/compartment threshold comfortably — unlike the tumour setting, where the one existing human innate-cell mtDNA tracing study reports NK cells "minimally represented" in most samples (PMC12330704, mtscATAC on matched tumour/normal-lung/blood from the same patients). The binding power limit for S3 is DONORS with both compartments (pre-registered >=3), set entirely by cohort conception/miscarriage rates rather than by cell numbers.

The mandatory blood reference C is what makes this row decidable at all. A design sampling only A and B cannot separate local descent from shared HSC ancestry and would yield an uninterpretable trivial YES.

MOUSE_ONLY RATIONALE. FALSE: all three compartments are obtainable in humans, human somatic mtDNA barcoding is the appropriate tool (per pre-registration section 4.3 it is weak in young inbred mice), and the downstream dependency — pre-conception uNK biopsy testing in women — is human-specific. Mouse fate mapping and parabiosis can address the structural question and largely already have (Sojka 2018 PMID 30275046; Chantakru 2002 PMID 11751942; Tatematsu 2025 PMID 39708955; Mohamed 2026 T-bet fate map), but they cannot substitute for the human pairing.

SCOPE NOTE: this record answers B1-B3 only. already_traced/B4 occupancy is a separate record; searches run here were for decidability and compartment feasibility, and the crossfield hit PMC12330704 (mtscATAC clonal tracing of human innate cells including NK across paired tissue/blood, concluding tissue myeloid cells are replenished from a common circulating bone-marrow-derived reservoir) is flagged for the occupancy pass rather than scored here.

b.why:
DECIDABLE, but only in the same-lineage/different-lineage form, and only with the label applied downstream of the NK progenitor.

WHY TRUE. The falsifiable content Phase A itself names — conversion vs "two independent lineages" — is exactly an MRCA-depth question, which is what the primitive returns. Under two independent lineages, mature blood cNK and liver/skin trNK coalesce only at or above the common progenitor: every cross-compartment cell pair has a deep MRCA, while within-compartment pairs can be shallow. Under conversion, individual clones straddle the two compartments with shallow, post-progenitor MRCAs. That asymmetry in the cross- vs within-compartment coalescent-depth distribution is a direct readout of "do they share an ancestor and how recently," so the claim's load-bearing alternative is adjudicable.

WHAT IS NOT DECIDABLE, AND MUST BE SCOPED OUT.
(1) Direction. A clone found in both compartments is equally consistent with cNK -> trNK, with trNK export back to blood, and with a shared recent precursor that seeded both in parallel. The arrow in "cNK -> trNK" is NOT recovered by clonal structure alone; it needs a timestamp (label the mature cNK pool only, after the trNK pool already exists) so that appearance of label in trNK is directional by construction.
(2) The parenthetical, "acquisition of a residency phenotype," read literally as a phenotype/state statement, is NOT decidable — lineage does not measure whether residency was acquired, only whether the cells are clonally continuous.
(3) The reversible-state trap partially bites. If residency is reversible (an ex-trNK can re-enter circulation, as documented for ex-TRM in the T-cell field), shared clones cannot separate one-way conversion from a single interconverting pool — both give clones spanning both compartments. Crucially, though, the reversibility ambiguity sits INSIDE the "one lineage" branch; it does not collapse the one-lineage vs two-lineage discrimination, which is why this is TRUE rather than FALSE.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT FALLS OUT OF THE PRIMITIVE. HSC/HSPC-level barcoding cannot decide this claim: both hypotheses predict shared HSPC barcodes across compartments, because both candidate lineages descend from the same HSCs. This is exactly the ceiling on Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus, blood vs liver/spleen/lung/GI NK) — they observe both PB-shared and tissue-private NK clones, but at HSPC-clone resolution "shared" does not separate "a cNK converted" from "one HSPC clone independently fed two lineages." The decidable design needs either an inducible label at or below the mature cNK stage (Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode/Confetti, induced after the resident pool is established) or enough sub-clonal resolution (mtDNA sub-clone structure via mtscATAC-seq/MAESTER, rooted on same-donor HSPCs) to measure coalescent DEPTH rather than mere set overlap.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = clones straddle mature circulating cNK and tissue trNK with shallow (post-progenitor) MRCA; the trNK pool is clonally continuous with the mature circulating pool.

Very next experiment: the conversion flux is now a measurable quantity, so perturb the source and re-read the SAME clonal output. Concretely — Ncr1-CreERT2 driving both the inducible barcode/Confetti and Tgfbr2-flox (TGF-betaRII is the named requirement in the sibling uterine claim, Barahona/Yokoyama), tamoxifen after the resident pool is established, then score whether cNK-derived barcodes still enter the liver/skin trNK compartment and at what rate. Paired arm: naive vs locally infected tissue (VACV/HSV ear skin, per the Gasteiger-lab design, PMID 38157853) to test whether entry is a steady-state trickle or inflammation-gated — which is the specific thing Sojka parabiosis could not see, since parabiosis tests pool replenishment at steady state, not inducible entry.

This is a new mouse, a new perturbation, and a new statistic (barcode entry rate under a genetic block). It is motivated ONLY by YES: with NO there is no source to knock out.
b.action_if_no:
NO = cross-compartment MRCAs are uniformly deep; trNK clones are tissue-private and coalesce with blood cNK only at or above the progenitor.

Very next experiment: the question flips from "how much flux" to "which progenitor, and when," which is a different sampling program, not a conclusion. Concretely — move the labeling window earlier and swap in the candidate source compartments: pulse-label in the fetal/perinatal window, and compare an ILC-progenitor-restricted CreER (Il7r/Rag1/PLZF-class) against Ncr1-CreER, asking which progenitor compartment shares a SHALLOW MRCA with adult liver trNK. In parallel, use the within-tissue clone-size distribution to test whether the resident pool is self-maintained by local proliferation rather than fed from outside at all. In the human arm this means dropping blood cNK as the comparator and adding fetal liver / BM ILC progenitors / adult BM CD34+ to the panel.

Precedent that this branch is productive rather than terminal: the tissue-macrophage field's NO answer (tissue macrophages are not monocyte-derived) is what launched the fetal-origin program. Same structural shape here.
b.both_answers_reason:
TRUE, and I tried to break it.

The two branches do not collapse. YES points at a KNOWN source and asks a mechanism/requirement question — build Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode x Tgfbr2-flox, measure blocked entry rate. NO points at an UNKNOWN source and asks an ontogeny question — shift the labeling window to the fetal/perinatal period, swap the comparator compartments to progenitors, and test in-situ self-renewal via clone-size distribution. Different mouse, different compartments sampled, different summary statistic. Neither is "we would conclude X and move on."

Honest deductions, recorded rather than hidden:
(1) SHARED CONTROL, NOT SHARED EXPERIMENT. Both branches need same-individual HSPCs to root the tree and set the baseline coalescent depth. Under YES that sample is a control; under NO it becomes the primary search space and gets extended backward in developmental time. The overlap is a control, not the experiment, so it does not trip the "same thing" rule.
(2) THE LIKELY REAL ANSWER IS MIXED, NOT BINARY. Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) already sees both PB-shared and tissue-private NK clones in macaque; mouse skin shows infection-driven conversion (PMID 38157853) while liver parabiosis (Sojka 2014) shows no steady-state exchange. So the expected result is "some fraction, under some condition." This is the main thing that could make the experiment descriptive rather than decisive. It does NOT flip the verdict, because a mixture makes the FRACTION the object of study and both branch experiments then apply to their respective fractions — but it does mean the claim should be preregistered with a quantitative threshold (what cNK-derived fraction of the trNK pool counts as YES) rather than as a binary, or it will resolve to an uninformative "both."
(3) The directional version of this experiment carries the actionability. If only the non-directional human mtDNA version is run, YES degrades toward "they are one lineage" — still not vacuous, since it kills the two-independent-lineage alternative Phase A flags, but the YES-branch follow-up above requires the mouse timestamp to be well-posed.
b.compartments_needed:
THREE compartments, needed simultaneously from one individual:

A. Circulating conventional NK — peripheral blood (human venipuncture; mouse blood + spleen). Trivial.

B. Tissue-resident NK from ONE defined tissue. The claim must name the tissue, because feasibility differs sharply:
   - LIVER (the compartment Sojka 2014 parabiosis actually addresses): human via deceased-donor liver perfusate, or via surgical resection (hepatectomy/metastasectomy), both with paired blood from the same individual.
   - SKIN: punch biopsy + paired blood, outpatient and repeatable — but trNK are rare in normal human skin, so cell-number limiting.
   - UTERUS/ENDOMETRIUM: pipelle biopsy + paired blood, outpatient, repeatable, non-pregnant; uNK are abundant, which is the best cell-number profile of the options. Decidua proper is pregnancy-only (termination/delivery).
   - LUNG/GUT: resection or endoscopic biopsy + paired blood.

C. A ROOTING compartment: HSPC/progenitors (BM aspirate or mobilised CD34+) from the SAME individual. This is not optional. Without it you cannot convert "clone shared vs private" into "MRCA shallow vs deep," and the whole discrimination in B1 collapses — you cannot distinguish a shared HSPC clone from a genuine peripheral conversion.
b.compartments_obtainable:
TRUE, with a cell-number caveat that is the real bottleneck.

Paired A+B from one living human is routine: blood + endometrial pipelle (outpatient), blood + skin punch, blood + liver resection at surgery. None of the required compartments is post-mortem-only, pregnancy-only, or mouse-only. Adding C from a living donor costs one extra invasive procedure (BM aspirate). All three come paired and unforced from a single deceased organ donor (vertebral-body BM + blood + multiple solid organs), which is the standard organ-donor tissue pipeline.

Verified precedent that in-life paired sampling works in a primate: Wu 2022 (PMID 36605190) took liver and spleen by laparoscopy, gut by endoscopic pinch biopsy, and LN by surgical excision, serially, from LIVING barcoded macaques alongside blood.

THE CAVEAT, from the same paper: subset-resolved sorting of tissue NK (CD56/CD16 subsets out of each organ) was only possible in the ONE animal that came to autopsy — the serial in-life biopsies gave paired tissue+blood but not enough cells to sort resident NK subsets. So paired sampling is obtainable; paired sampling at the DEPTH needed for clonal statistics on a rare resident subset pushes you toward organ-donor, autopsy, or surgical-resection-scale material rather than needle biopsy. This is the practical constraint that should be preregistered, and it argues for endometrium (abundant uNK, repeatable outpatient sampling) or resection-scale liver over skin.
b.compartment_notes:
SPLIT FEASIBILITY — the two versions of this experiment have different species ceilings, and this should be recorded explicitly:

- The NON-DIRECTIONAL version (are cNK and trNK one lineage or two?) is HUMAN-DOABLE. Endogenous mtDNA clonal readouts (mtscATAC-seq, MAESTER) need no genetic engineering, so paired blood + tissue + BM from one human is sufficient. This is the version that kills Phase A's "two independent lineages" alternative.
- The DIRECTIONAL version (does a mature cNK become a trNK) is MOUSE-ONLY, because it requires an inducible label restricted to the mature cNK pool (Ncr1-CreERT2 x barcode/Confetti, induced after the resident pool exists). No human equivalent.

So mouse_only = FALSE overall, but the arrow in the claim as written is mouse-only.

Other notes:
- Known mtDNA-clonality limitation worth pre-checking on power: informative mtDNA variants are recovered best from expanded clones (see PMID 40134031, "Clonal expansion dictates the efficacy of mitochondrial lineage tracing in single cells"). A small, non-expanded resident pool may simply not carry resolvable variants — this is a power question for Phase C, not a decidability question, but it can silently convert a real YES into an apparent NO.
- G4 note: the structurally identical question (are tissue-resident cells clonally continuous with the circulating pool, or a separate lineage?) has already been worked over in the T-cell field via TCR-based clonal overlap between TRM and circulating memory, and in the myeloid field via fetal-origin fate mapping, where the NO answer was the productive one. Occupancy in those fields should be checked before this is shortlisted.
- B4 (already_traced) was not requested in this claim's output schema and is not asserted here. Searches did surface direct partial occupancy — PMID 36605190 (macaque HSPC barcode, blood vs tissue NK clones), PMID 38157853 (mouse, circulating NK establish skin residency after infection), PMID 34437840 (single-NK-cell fate mapping, ILC1-like progeny) — but none applies a timestamped label downstream of the NK progenitor, which is the design B1 identifies as necessary. I am not recording a FALSE on prior art.

o.already_traced_evidence: TRUE at three independent levels. (1) MOUSE, directly and recently: Torcellan et al., Immunity 2024, PMID 38157853 (Romagnani lab) used inducible genetic fate mapping — Sell-CreERT2 x Rosa26-LSL-tdTomato and Eomes-CreERT2 x Rosa26-LSL-tdTomato, tamoxifen-pulsed BEFORE infection — plus percutaneous Dendra2 photoconversion (histone-Dendra2 mice) and i.v. anti-CD45 vascular labeling, to show that circulating CD62L+Eomes+ cNK are recruited into VACV/S. aureus-infected skin and become long-lived CD69hi Tcf1hi trNK that retain the photoconverted label at d5 and d10 (CD49b-hi NK lost it by d5). Verified in the archived full text (/home/user/aaa/refs/T1_PMC10783803.txt): "a significant fraction of CD69hi NK cells in the skin fate-mapped for Sell and Eomes expression, suggesting that circulating cNK cells can become trNK cells during infection." This IS the claim, answered directionally. (2) MOUSE, uterus — the compartment the task flags as the best cell-number option: Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025, PMID 39708955, parabiosis + intravascular labeling: "Our parabiosis studies confirmed that the progesterone-responsive trNK cells are derived from peripheral cNK cells." Note this is the same lab whose eLife 2014 parabiosis study (Sojka et al., eLife 3:e01659) concluded liver CD49a+DX5- trNK are a lineage DISTINCT from cNK — so the field has already answered the claim in both directions, tissue by tissue, with lineage tools. The dispute is live and public: Schuster/Degli-Esposti Immunity 2025 PMID 40073839 vs the Romagnani reply PMID 40073840. (3) ACTUAL CLONAL BARCODING, NHP, with the rooting compartment built in: Wu, Liang, Brenchley, ... Dunbar, Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525. High-diversity lentiviral barcode library into autologous rhesus CD34+ HSPCs, TBI conditioning, then serial paired sampling of PB alongside liver + spleen (laparoscopy), gut (endoscopic pinch biopsy), lung/BAL (bronchoscopy), and necropsy tissue in one animal. Barcodes are installed at the HSPC, so compartment C is present by construction. Result: a set of highly expanded PB CD16-CD56- (DN) NK clones also contributed to TR NK in ALL tissues examined (both TR CD56-CD16+ and TR DN), but were ABSENT from TR CD56+CD16- NK; plus tissue-private clone sets (lung-only, GI-only) and a liver+spleen-shared set. Prior work from the same lab: PMID 24702997 (Cell Stem Cell 2014, NK have a clonally distinct lineage origin from myeloid/B/T) and PMID 30389798 (2018, clonally compartmentalized maintenance of macaque CD56+16- vs CD56-16+ NK subsets). (4) HUMAN, clonal, mtDNA, paired blood+tissue: Liu VV, Sandor K, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT, "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer," Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 (preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704). mtscATAC-seq, 218,715 cells, matched tumor + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + PBMC from the SAME patients (5 NSCLC, 5 ovarian), with 4 NK/ILC clusters in lung and 3 in ovarian. Verified in the archived text: expanded NK clones were found in NILT and peripheral blood; of 14 blood-enriched clones, 2 were NK-dominated (donor SU-L-005) with 66.0% of cells in PBMC but 25.3% in tumor and 8.8% in NILT — i.e. blood NK clones demonstrably present in tissue; NK were grouped with the innate cells that "consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing... originated from recent hematopoietic output"; and one ovarian tumor showed oligoclonal NK expansion ABSENT from matched blood (tumor-restricted). (5) HUMAN NK mtDNA method proof, blood-only: Rückert et al., Nat Immunol 2022, PMID 36289449 / PMC9663309 — mtscATAC clonal tracking of adaptive NK in HCMV+ donors. I grepped the archived full text: liver=0, biopsy=0, bone marrow=0, "resident"=0 hits. So this establishes that mtDNA barcoding resolves human NK clones but does NOT touch residency. NEGATIVE result worth recording: my Polylox, Confetti, Sleeping Beauty and CRISPR-recorder searches returned NO NK-specific or trNK-specific study — those recorder classes have not been pointed at this question. That gap does not rescue the claim, because parabiosis, inducible Cre fate maps, HSPC barcoding and mtDNA have already occupied it.
o.nearest_occupant: Two co-nearest occupants, one per axis. NEAREST ON THE CLONAL PRIMITIVE: Wu et al. 2022, PMID 36605190 (Front Immunol, PMC9808525). It uses exactly the primitive in question (shared-ancestor barcodes), in a large outbred primate, with paired blood + liver + spleen + lung + GI from the same animal, AND with the HSPC rooting compartment supplied by construction. HOW IT DIFFERS: (a) not human, and requires myeloablative TBI + autologous transplant, so every clonal structure it reports is post-transplant reconstitution, not steady-state adult homeostasis; (b) it stratifies NK by CD56/CD16 only — it never gates on the canonical residency markers (CD69, CD49a, CD103, CXCR6) that define the "residency phenotype" the claim is about, so its "TR NK" is operationally "NK recovered from a tissue," which is a weaker definition than the claim uses; (c) because the barcode is installed in the HSPC, a shared barcode between blood NK and tissue NK proves a shared HSPC ancestor, NOT that a mature circulating cNK converted in the periphery — it therefore cannot by itself separate "parallel HSPC output to two sites" from "peripheral conversion," which is the exact discrimination B1 needs; (d) n is small (a handful of animals) and the paper itself reports the trNK clonal pattern was "more heterogeneous between individual animals." NEAREST IN HUMAN: Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 (preprint 40777278). Human, mtDNA clonal, matched blood + non-involved tissue + tumor in one individual, NK included, and it already reports the two possible answers coexisting (blood NK clones found in tissue; tumor NK clones absent from blood). HOW IT DIFFERS: (a) NK are a side observation, not the paper's object — the analysis and the headline are monocyte-to-macrophage/DC3; (b) cell types are annotated from chromatin accessibility (NCR1, GNLY, KLRD1) into a merged "NK/ILC" cluster, with NO residency-marker stratification, so it never separates cNK from trNK — it separates blood-NK from tissue-NK by sampling site, which is the confound, not the answer; (c) tissue is lung (NILT and tumor) and ovarian tumor — not liver, not endometrium, not normal skin; every donor is a cancer patient, several treatment-exposed; (d) no BM/HSPC rooting compartment at all, so MRCA depth is inferred only from mtDNA variant sharing depth; (e) NK numbers are thin — they state NK are depleted in tumor relative to NILT and "rarely detected in most tumors," with the oligoclonal NK finding resting on a single donor (SU-O-005) and the blood-enriched NK clones on a single donor (SU-L-005). RESIDUAL UNOCCUPIED SLICE, stated precisely so it is not overclaimed: human, non-malignant tissue, NK explicitly stratified by CD69/CD49a/CXCR6 residency phenotype, with a paired BM/HSPC rooting compartment. That is narrow, and both flanking papers would likely be read by reviewers as having already settled the direction.
o.crossfield_occupancy: G4 applies squarely — "acquisition of tissue residency" is a borrowed mechanism, and the field it was borrowed from has already answered the identical structural question with clonal tools, in humans, at larger n. T CELLS (fully occupied, and the borrowing source): the TCR is a free natural clonal barcode, so human TRM has had this exact adjudication for years. Klicznik et al. 2019, PMID 31278120 — human CD4+CD103+ cutaneous resident-memory T cells are found in the circulation of healthy individuals, i.e. paired skin+blood TCR clonal sharing showed the residency phenotype is not clonally sealed and traffics in BOTH directions. Snyder/Farber, PMID 38422982 (2024) — dynamic establishment of the RECIPIENT TRM repertoire after human intestinal transplantation, which is the cleanest possible human answer to "do circulating cells become resident," because donor/recipient HLA chimerism roots the clone unambiguously; this is the design NK lacks and could copy. Also PMID 34127056 (maintenance of the human memory T cell repertoire by subset and tissue site, paired multi-tissue organ donors), PMID 41615802 (Cell Rep 2026, intra-donor cross-tissue T cell clonal expansion across the gut-liver-blood axis — the exact liver+blood paired design T1 wants, already executed for T cells), and PMID 41308653 (2025, compartmentalized clones and phenotypic trajectories across blood and tonsils). MYELOID (fully occupied, and by the very same mtDNA primitive T1 would use): Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233 established with mtscATAC in paired human blood/tissue/tumor that TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and went further than a yes/no by identifying DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones whose blood precursors are epigenetically pre-programmed. That is the structural template — "circulating precursor acquires a tissue-restricted state" — already answered, published, and commentaried (PMID 42276048). ILC (partially occupied, mouse): PMID 39242588 (2024) showed recipient tissue microenvironment determines the developmental path of intestinal ILC progenitors; PMID 38871999 / 38872000 (2024) map Eomes+ BM precursors to classical NK and show distinct developmental pathways generate functionally distinct NK populations; PMID 41172988 (2025) NFIL3-driven ILC specification. NET EFFECT: the T cell field answered this with a natural clonal barcode, the myeloid field answered it with mtDNA in humans, and the mouse NK field answered it with parabiosis and inducible fate maps in skin, uterus and liver. A clonal-barcoding NK version would be the fourth pass at a question whose answer is already published as "yes in skin and uterus, no in liver, tissue-dependent" — which is also why the both-answers-actionable test (B2) is where this claim is most at risk: "yes" reproduces Torcellan 2024 and Tatematsu 2025, "no" reproduces Sojka 2014, and neither outcome forces a different next experiment.
