b.why: The fork T3 actually turns on is invisible to a shared-ancestor primitive. Three reasons, in order of force. (1) THE CONTESTED DISTINCTION IS A MATURATION STAGE INSIDE ONE CLONAL BRANCH, NOT A BRANCH POINT. T3 asserts that a MATURE circulating CD16+ pbNK enters decidua and converts. Its live competitor after the Phase A audit is not "decidual NK are non-haematopoietic" - it is that a BLOOD-BORNE IMMATURE PRECURSOR (CD34+ or CD34-CD117+CD94- stage-3) crosses into the uterus and matures locally (Chantakru 2002 PMID 11751942; Male 2010 PMID 20802153; Vacca 2011 PMID 21248224; Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461). A mature pbNK and its sibling precursor are on the SAME clonal branch and carry the SAME mark, because the mark is fixed upstream of both. Clone membership is stage-agnostic and undirected: it says "these two cells share an ancestor", never "which one was the immigrant" or "what state it was in when it crossed the endothelium". Both hypotheses therefore predict the identical clonal structure - the prompt's own disqualifying condition. (2) THE DEPTH RESOLUTION IS WRONG BY ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE, and this is documented, not speculative. Rueckert 2022 Nat Immunol PMID 36289449, the one study that has actually run mtscATAC/mgatk on human NK cells, states in its own results that for CONVENTIONAL (non-adaptive, non-expanded) NK cells the mitochondrial mutations "do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level". Wang 2025 Genome Biol PMID 40134031 goes further: the majority of purported clone-informative variants are PRE-EXISTING heteroplasmies present in the first cell, not de novo marks acquired during recent divisions. So the "how recently" that mtDNA delivers dates the common ancestor to an embryonic/HSC-level node, far above the pbNK-vs-precursor node T3 depends on. Every maternal haematopoietic cell in that woman - blood NK, decidual NK, decidual CD34+, and a uterus-resident precursor seeded years earlier - passes the shared-ancestor test. (3) THE ENDPOINT IS A REVERSIBLE, ENVIRONMENT-IMPOSED STATE, NOT A LINEAGE DESTINATION. "dNK-like" is operationally CD16-lo/CD9+/CD49a+/CD103+/KIR+, a TGF-beta-driven residency imprint that Keskin's own Discussion concedes "may not be specific to the decidual tissue but may occur when NK cells enter any tissue expressing TGF-beta", and that Cerdeira 2013 Fig 1 shows RUNNING BACKWARDS - ex vivo dNK lose KIR and regain cytotoxicity within 7-10 days of culture (registry claim R3 is exactly this reversal). An NK cell sitting in decidua is dNK-like whatever its recent ancestry, and an NK cell in blood is not, whatever its ancestry. Ancestry neither determines nor reports the state. NOTE ON WHAT IS DECIDABLE: a coarser question - "is the human uterine NK pool filled from the circulation at all?" - is a genuine ancestry question, but it is not T3, and it has already been answered in vivo in humans by donor/recipient genotyping rather than by barcoding (Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461, uNK carry recipient genotype after uterus transplant; Strunz 2026 Sci Transl Med PMID 41811987, donor-derived endometrial tissue-resident lymphocytes after HSCT, one case male-origin; both recorded abstract-level only in Phase A). G4 note: the structurally identical question in the T cell field - are tissue-resident cells clonally continuous with blood? - is routinely settled with TCR clonotype, a true per-cell somatic barcode with resolution mtDNA does not approach (e.g. PMID 41615802, intra-donor cross-tissue T cell clonal mapping across gut-liver-blood). NK cells have no rearranged receptor, which is precisely why the NK field is reaching for mtDNA and precisely why it cannot reach the depth this claim needs.
b.action_if_yes: Adjudicating run assumed: paired maternal peripheral blood + first-trimester decidua from the SAME woman at elective termination (6-12 wk); sort blood NK (CD56dim CD16+ and CD56bright CD16-) and dNK (CD56superbright CD9+ CD49a+ CD16-); mtscATAC-seq both compartments; mgatk informative-variant calling; ask whether dNK clonotypes are shared with circulating NK and whether the decidual clone-size spectrum mirrors blood. YES = dNK carry the same informative variants as the paired blood NK at matched frequencies, with no uterus-private expansions. THE VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: you would have to determine whether the cell that crossed into the decidua was a mature CD16+ pbNK (T3 as stated) or a blood-borne CD34+/CD117+ stage-3 precursor that matured in situ. NO LINEAGE EXPERIMENT CAN DO THIS - the two candidates share a branch and share the mark - so the follow-up is not a barcoding experiment at all. It is a stage-resolved in vivo tracking tool that does not exist for humans: there is no human equivalent of the i.v. anti-CD45 intravascular-exclusion label or the Ncr1-iCre stage-restricted fate map that Barahona/Yokoyama used in mouse (eLife 2026 PMID 42417504, which is registry claim T2, not T3). So the YES branch terminates in the sentence "the uterine NK niche is filled from the circulation, and we move on" - which is (a) already reported in vivo in humans by transplant-chimerism genotyping (Strunz PMID 33617461; PMID 41811987), and (b) leaves T3's entire distinctive content, MATURE pbNK plus TGF-beta-driven conversion, exactly where the Phase A audit left it. This branch is vacuous. It is also the near-certain outcome: every dNK variant of the kind mtDNA detects is a pre-existing/progenitor-level heteroplasmy that is by construction also present in that woman's blood (PMID 40134031; PMID 36289449), AND maternal blood contamination of an enzymatically digested decidua manufactures the identical result. The branch that carries no information is the branch you will almost certainly get, and it is indistinguishable from the assay's dominant artefact.
b.action_if_no: Same adjudicating run. NO = dNK are dominated by uterus-private clonal families - high-heteroplasmy variants carried by an appreciable fraction of dNK but at or below detection in the paired blood NK pool, with a decidual clone-size spectrum that does not mirror blood (the human analogue of Sojka 2018 PMID 30275046, where mouse uterine NK accumulation during decidualization was local proliferation of pre-existing CD49a+ trNK and "migrating NK cells made no contribution"). THE VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: hunt the local precursor, with a defined sample request. From the SAME decidual digest, sort and mtscATAC (i) Lin-CD34+CD45+ decidual progenitors (Vacca PNAS 2011 PMID 21248224) and (ii) CD34-CD117+CD94- stage-3 uterine NK precursors (Male J Immunol 2010 PMID 20802153) alongside the dNK, and test whether they carry the uterus-private variants - i.e. whether they sit clonally upstream of dNK. Then extend to non-pregnant endometrium (Pipelle biopsy, staged across the cycle) to ask whether the same private clones pre-exist the pregnancy, which is the "uNK resident before pregnancy" competitor stated in the Phase A notes. That is executable and has named downstream consequences inside this registry: registry claims X3 and T5 lose the operational "dNK-like" endpoint they borrow from the Keskin-Cerdeira induction protocol, and the Kopcow/Cerdeira idNK preeclampsia cell-therapy program (PLoS One 2016 PMID 27736914), which manufactures a "dNK" out of blood NK, loses its premise. This branch IS actionable. But it is close to unreachable in practice, for the same reason the YES branch is uninformative: since the marks are pre-existing progenitor-level heteroplasmies, a locally seeded uterine precursor still shares them with blood, so "uterus-private" requires local clonal expansion large enough to dominate the compartment AND an absence of blood carry-over that no human intravascular-exclusion label can enforce.
b.both_answers_reason: Fails on both of the prompt's disqualifying conditions at once. (1) THE TWO BRANCHES CONVERGE ON THE SAME NEXT EXPERIMENT. Under NO you go and profile the decidual precursor compartment because dNK look uterus-private. Under YES you STILL have to go and profile the decidual precursor compartment, because YES is fully compatible with a blood-borne CD34+/stage-3 precursor immigrating and maturing locally - which is the leading competitor, not a fringe one. Either way the bench request is identical: sort decidual Lin-CD34+CD45+ / CD34-CD117+CD94- precursors together with dNK and run the same assay. A test whose two outcomes issue the same work order is not a test. (2) THE YES BRANCH IS VACUOUS WITHIN THE PRIMITIVE. Its only honest continuation is "now establish whether the immigrant was mature or immature", which the shared-ancestor primitive structurally cannot answer (same branch, same mark), and for which no human stage-resolved in vivo tool exists. Its conclusion - the uterine NK niche is blood-filled - is additionally already on the record in vivo in humans from uterus-transplant and post-HSCT genotyping (PMID 33617461, PMID 41811987). (3) AGGRAVATING ASYMMETRY, recorded but not needed for the verdict: the vacuous branch is the near-certain one. Because most clone-informative mtDNA variants are pre-existing heteroplasmies rather than recent somatic marks (PMID 40134031), and because Rueckert 2022 found that conventional NK mtDNA variants sit "already on the progenitor level" (PMID 36289449), essentially every dNK variant will also be found in that woman's blood; and maternal blood contamination of a digested decidua produces the same reading with zero biology. So one branch is uninformative, the other is near-unreachable, and they end in the same follow-up. T3 is OUT at B2 independently of its FALSE at B1 and independently of its MEDIUM load_bearing.
b.compartments_needed: Five, in descending order of necessity. (A) PERIPHERAL BLOOD NK from the index woman - CD56dim CD16+ (the asserted starting cell) and CD56bright CD16- separately, since Cerdeira's readout lives inside the CD56bright CD16- gate and the two must not be pooled. (B) DECIDUAL NK from the same woman - decidua basalis and parietalis, CD56superbright CD9+ CD49a+ CD103+ KIR+ CD16-. (C) DECIDUAL PRECURSORS from the same decidual digest - Lin-CD34+CD45+ (Vacca 2011) and CD34-CD117+CD94- stage-3 (Male 2010); required by BOTH B2 branches, so not optional. (D) NON-PREGNANT ENDOMETRIUM from the same woman, cycle-staged - the only compartment that can test the "uNK resident before pregnancy" competitor named in the Phase A notes. (E) BONE MARROW / HSPC from the same woman - needed to ROOT the clone tree; without a root there is no scale on "how recently", and the whole primitive degenerates to a yes/no on shared ancestry, which is the failure diagnosed in B1.
b.compartments_obtainable: PARTIAL - and it fails on exactly the compartments the fork needs. (A)+(B) PAIRED FROM ONE WOMAN: YES, routinely, and this is genuinely T3's strongest feature relative to other rows in this registry. First-trimester elective termination (6-12 wk) yields decidua with a same-visit venous draw; at term, PMID 41808348 (2026) collected placenta, decidua and matched maternal blood from the same donors at scheduled caesarean and sorted NK from mBlood/DPI/decidua of 6 MATCHED donors, so the pairing is demonstrated, not hypothetical. Worth recording that the primary sources for this very claim did NOT pair: Keskin 2007 took pNK from "peripheral blood of healthy donors" (RosetteSep) and decidua from unrelated terminations, so no experiment underpinning T3 has ever had compartments A and B from one individual. (C) SAME DECIDUA: obtainable in principle but at the edge of feasibility - Vacca sorted only 250-500 decidual CD34+ cells per well, and the pre-registered power floor (<30 NK cells per donor per compartment = unusable, Section 4.2) will be breached for this compartment in most donors. (D) NON-PREGNANT ENDOMETRIUM FROM THE SAME WOMAN: NOT obtainable simultaneously. Pre-pregnancy endometrium and pregnancy decidua from one individual requires prospective longitudinal recruitment - biopsy, then conception, then termination or delivery - which is a study design, not a sample request, and exists in no archived dataset. (E) BONE MARROW: not obtainable from termination or caesarean donors. The clone tree cannot be rooted, so "how recently" is unmeasurable in the very individuals who supply A and B. TIMING AND ACCESS CONSTRAINTS, EXPLICIT: compartment B exists ONLY DURING PREGNANCY and ONLY at surgery (termination or caesarean); sampling is destructive and single-timepoint, so the same woman's decidua can never be resampled before/after; compartment D needs a separate procedure at a separate time.
b.compartment_notes: MOUSE_ONLY = FALSE, for two reasons, neither of which rescues the claim. First, the human compartments for the core pair are obtainable (above), so nothing forces this into mouse. Second, the mouse version is not T3: Barahona/Yokoyama eLife 2026 PMID 42417504 already did the in vivo answer in mouse (CD45.2 splenic cNK transferred i.v. into congenic pregnant dams at gd0.5, n=4, donor cells CD49a+ CD49b- Eomes+ in gravid uterus by gd10.5, with 3 ug i.v. anti-CD45.2-PE-Cy7 3 min before euthanasia for intravascular exclusion, plus Tgfbr2-fl x Ncr1-iCre necessity), and the Phase A audit assigns that to registry claim T2. Importing it into T3 double-counts, and the endpoints differ (CD49a+Eomes+ murine uterine trNK vs the human CD56superbright CD9+ KIR+ signature). Note also prereg Section 4.3: mtDNA barcoding is weak in young inbred mice, so a mouse route would have to switch to Confetti/Polylox/CRISPR recorder - i.e. T2's territory again. TECHNICAL CONFOUND INTRINSIC TO THIS COMPARTMENT PAIR, flagged because it corrupts the readout rather than merely weakening it: human decidual digests carry maternal blood, and there is no human equivalent of the mouse i.v. anti-CD45 intravascular label. The exact signal that yields the YES answer - blood-clone marks detected inside the decidual sample - is what contamination produces. Gating on CD9+CD49a+CD16- helps but that gate IS the disputed endpoint, so the control is circular. POWER, against prereg Section 4.2: Rueckert 2022 (PMID 36289449) achieved median chrM coverage of only 11-20x on blood NK, at or below the pre-registered 20x floor, using mgatk defaults matching the prereg (strand concordance >65%, VMR >0.01) but variants in >=3 cells rather than the prereg's >=5; and its informative-variant yield came from HCMV-driven adaptive expansions, with the paper stating explicitly that conventional NK variants sit at the progenitor level. PMID 40134031 concludes that clonal expansion dictates whether mtDNA tracing works at all. A non-expanded dNK pool is the unfavourable case on both counts. SEARCHES RUN FOR THIS ROW (lit.py, all returned; recorded so the thinness is visible rather than hidden): mtDNA+lineage/clonal+decidual/uterine NK; mtscATAC-seq+tissue-resident lymphocyte; MAESTER+mitochondrial variant lineage tracing; barcode/lentiviral barcoding+NK cell; decidual NK clonality/clonal expansion; uterine NK fate mapping/parabiosis/lineage tracing (mouse); uterine NK chimerism/transplant genotype; paired decidua+blood single-cell; mtDNA+NKG2C adaptive NK; G4 cross-field: Trm origin by clonal tracing, cross-tissue T cell clonal mapping (PMID 41615802). New full texts archived under /home/user/aaa/refs/T3_PMC9663309.txt (Rueckert 2022, complete Methods incl. the mgatk/clonotype section quoted above) and /home/user/aaa/refs/T3_PMC12975338.txt (PMID 41808348, the matched blood/decidua sampling precedent). I did NOT reach a B4 verdict and none is asserted here - the searches above were run to ground B1 and B3, not to establish occupancy, and per rule G3 a thin search must be recorded as NOT_SEARCHED rather than FALSE. If the orchestrator needs already_traced for T3, it should be run as its own pass; my honest current state for it is NOT_SEARCHED.

o.already_traced_evidence:
TRUE, but with an important scoping caveat — the ORIGIN half of T3 has been adjudicated in humans with a genotype-resolution ancestry method; the CLONE-resolution version has not.

WHAT HAS BEEN DONE (occupies the claim):
1. PMID 41811987 — Strunz B, Ivarsson MA, ... Björkström NK. "Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation." Sci Transl Med 2026 Mar 11;18(840):eadp2583 (preprint bioRxiv 2024.03.04.583277). Women who underwent uterus solid-organ transplant (UTx; donor uterus + recipient blood) or allogeneic HSCT (donor marrow + recipient uterus). Single-cell assignment of donor-vs-recipient origin by single-nucleotide polymorphisms (scRNA-seq genotype demultiplexing) and by disparate HLA expression on high-parameter flow. Sampled endometrium (and, per the companion commentary PMID 41811988, decidual samples after surgery in UTx recipients, plus menstrual samples in HSCT recipients). Result: after UTx the graft's donor immune cells are REPLACED by recipient-derived cells; after HSCT the endometrium is reconstituted near-completely by DONOR-derived cells, "including formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes"; in one patient male-origin cells reconstituted the endometrium. This is the shared-ancestor primitive applied at whole-genome/whole-graft granularity to exactly compartments (A) and (B)/(D) of this claim, and it returns the YES-branch answer: the uterine NK compartment is filled from the circulating/HSC compartment, not retained from a uterus-resident pool.
2. PMID 33617461 — Strunz et al., Sci Immunol 2021;6(56):eabb7800. Earlier, smaller version of the same experiment: "By studying human uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins, we found that the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation and that it was under genetic control." uNK in the grafted uterus carry the RECIPIENT genotype.

WHAT HAS NOT BEEN DONE (the claim's clone-resolution form is still open):
- Neither study builds a clone tree. Genotype tells you which person a cell descends from; it cannot say whether a given dNK descends from a mature CD56dim CD16+ blood NK cell versus a circulating CD34+ / CD117+CD94- stage-3 precursor that homed and differentiated in situ (compartment C). Both routes are recipient-derived and therefore indistinguishable by SNP/HLA. That is precisely the distinction claim T3 asserts.
- No "how recently" axis: no BM/HSPC root (compartment E), so no scale on ancestry — the degeneracy diagnosed in B1 is untouched.
- Both are in tacrolimus-immunosuppressed transplant recipients; the same group's companion paper (PMID 41811989 / preprint 38559147, Asiimwe et al., Sci Transl Med 2026;18(840):eadp2196) shows calcineurin/NFAT inhibition itself degrades uNK residency programming, so the setting is pharmacologically perturbed and not physiological pregnancy.
- No mtDNA / mtscATAC / MAESTER / barcode / TCR-analogue clonal method has ever been applied to decidual or endometrial NK cells. PubMed returns literally zero records for (decidua OR endometrium) AND mtDNA AND single-cell, and zero for "dNK clonotype/clonal expansion single cell decidua." The Dunbar lab states this explicitly in print (PMID 36605190, Discussion): "It will be of particular interest to investigate clonality and relationship in decidual NK cells, a uniquely functional NK population that we have not yet investigated at a clonal level."
- Mouse side: no Confetti, Polylox, or CRISPR-recorder study of uterine/decidual NK exists. The only uterine NK "fate mapping" is PMID 41782473 (Tbx21-Cre x Rosa26-RFP, 2026), which fate-maps T-bet EXPRESSION HISTORY, not clonal ancestry, and cannot address a blood-to-decidua ancestor relation. PMID 42417504 / 41332720 (TGF-β drives conversion of cNK into uterine trNK, murine pregnancy) and PMID 39708955 (progesterone-regulated uterine trNK from cNK) are transfer/conditional-KO designs, not clone tracing.
o.nearest_occupant:
PRIMARY (occupies the origin question, human, exact compartments): PMID 41811987, Strunz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026 (+ predecessor PMID 33617461, Sci Immunol 2021). Differences from T3: (i) method is genotype-of-origin (SNP demultiplexing + disparate-HLA flow), granularity = "which individual," not "which clone" — it cannot separate a mature blood NK ancestor from a circulating NK precursor ancestor, which is the entire content of T3; (ii) no clone tree and no HSPC root, so the "how recently" half of the primitive is absent; (iii) primary tissue is post-transplant endometrium, with decidua only in UTx recipients, i.e. under tacrolimus, not physiological pregnancy; (iv) does not stratify the source compartment into CD56dim CD16+ vs CD56bright CD16- (Cerdeira's actual readout gate).

NEAREST ON METHOD (proves the tool works on the right cell type, wrong compartment): PMID 36289449, Rückert T, Lareau CA, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. Nat Immunol 2022;23:1551-1563. mtscATAC-seq/ASAP-seq with somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous barcodes on sorted human NKG2C+/NKG2C- CD7+ NK cells, mgatk variant calling, clonotypes by clustering on mtDNA allele-frequency neighborhood graphs; found large adaptive-NK clonal expansions with clonotype-linked private chromatin. Difference: PERIPHERAL BLOOD ONLY, non-pregnant donors, HCMV question. No tissue, no uterus, no decidua.

NEAREST ON STRUCTURE IN NK (blood-vs-tissue clonal relation, wrong species and wrong tissue): PMID 36605190, Front Immunol 2022 (Dunbar lab). Autologous lentiviral high-diversity barcoded HSPC transplant in 5 rhesus macaques; barcode retrieval from sorted NK/T/B/myeloid in matched PB, BAL, lung, liver, spleen, jejunum, colon, 4-106 months post-transplant. Found tissue-restricted NK clones and a shared PB CD16-CD56- (DN) NK clone set contributing to tissue-resident NK across all tissues. Differences: macaque, not human; non-pregnant; no uterus/decidua sampled (the word "decidual" appears once, in the Discussion, as an explicit statement that they have NOT done it); requires myeloablation + engineered HSPCs, so it can never be run in a pregnant woman.

ALSO ADJACENT: PMID 40437214 (2025) — blood NK acquire a "decidual-like" phenotype (CD9, CD49a, CD151, CD56-hi) after autologous HSCT in children; flow/scRNA-seq/HLA-KIR genotyping only, no clonal or chimerism tracing, blood-only compartment. Phenotypic convergence, not lineage.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
YES — heavily occupied, in all three neighbouring fields, and one of them at the identical anatomical site.

T CELLS, SAME SITE: PMID 37195197 (Chasman/Stanic, J Immunol 2023) profiled human DECIDUAL T cells with matched maternal PERIPHERAL BLOOD from the same women, single-cell transcriptome + surface protein + paired V(D)J, and read out clonotype sharing/diversity between the two compartments. Same structural question ("are the tissue cells at the maternal-fetal interface clonally continuous with the same woman's blood?"), same compartment pair, answered with the field's native clonal tool. Precedents in the same lineage: PMID 32582176 (Morita 2020, TCR repertoire in paired decidual and peripheral CD8 T cells), Tsuda 2018 Front Immunol 9:1934 (clonally expanded decidual effector Tregs), Dokouhaki 2008 (TCRBV repertoire, endometrium vs blood). So for T cells the question has been asked and answered repeatedly; NK cells lag only because they lack a rearranged receptor.

MYELOID: PMID 42242233 (Liu V, Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. Cancer Cell 2026;44:1509-1521.e4; preprint 2025.07.16.665245). mtscATAC-seq, 218,715 cells, MATCHED tumour + adjacent tissue + BLOOD from lung and ovarian cancer patients. Reconstructed clonal lineage relationships showing TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and that DC-biased vs macrophage-biased fate is peripherally programmed before infiltration. This is the exact experimental grammar T3 would use — mtDNA clones, paired blood + tissue, one human — already executed, just on monocytes rather than NK and in tumour rather than decidua. Note the ovarian-cancer arm reaches the female reproductive tract but not uterus/decidua and not pregnancy.

ILC / GROUP 1: PMID 34437840 (Flommersfeld et al., Immunity 2021, single-NK-cell fate mapping identifying an ILC1-like lineage bridging innate and adaptive recognition) and PMID 35344171 (retrogenic colour-barcoding for fate mapping of single innate lymphocytes) establish clone-resolution fate mapping of NK/ILC — mouse only, and neither touches the uterus.

Bottom line for G4: the "does the tissue compartment descend from the circulating compartment" question has been settled with lineage tools in T cells (including in decidua specifically) and in myeloid cells (including with paired blood + mtDNA in humans). The NK/decidua cell has been answered in humans only at genotype granularity (Strunz 2026), not clone granularity.

b.why: The claim decomposes into three parts, and the part that carries the claim is not the part barcoding can see. (1) "Glycodelin-A DRIVES" is molecular attribution. The primitive returns whether two cells share an ancestor and how recently; it is blind to WHICH signal produced a state. A perfect clonal read showing blood NK gave rise to the CD9+CD49a+ cells would not name GdA as the cause, and a perfect clonal read showing no relationship would not exclude GdA from acting on whatever precursor does make dNK. (2) "dNK-LIKE PHENOTYPE" is a marker state, not an ancestry relation - lineage does not measure phenotype causation. (3) The one structurally clean question here - is the day-5 CD9+CD49a+ output the progeny of CD9-CD49a- day-0 cells (conversion), or the expansion of a CD9+CD49a+ fraction present at day 0 (selection)? - IS decidable in principle, and it is exactly Phase A's strongest alternative explanation. But that is a narrow within-culture ancestry question, not the claim as written, and it still cannot license the verb "drives". Decisively, this is the preregistered REVERSIBLE-STATE case. CD56bright/CD9/CD49a residency markers are a reversible state inside one NK lineage, not a lineage bifurcation: Niehrs et al. Nat Immunol 2025 (PMID 41087727) show human CD56bright NK enter tissue transiently and egress via lymphatics to recirculate, and Orrantia et al. iScience 2022 (PMID 36262311) show CD9 and the decidual-like signature are acquired by ordinary blood NK during proliferation-dominated reconstitution in vivo. So clonal sharing between the "blood NK" and "dNK-like" marker compartments is produced equally by a conversion model, by a selection-then-reversion model, and by plain recirculation - and absence of sharing is equally consistent with GdA acting on the local decidual CD34+ precursor route (Vacca et al. PNAS 2011, PMID 21248224). Both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure, which is the definition of not decidable by this primitive.
b.action_if_yes: YES = the CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" cells are clonal progeny of CD16-CD56bright blood NK (in vitro: barcode day-0 sorted CD9-CD49a- cells and recover barcodes in the day-5 CD9+ gate; in vivo: shared mtDNA/somatic-epimutation clonotypes between a woman's peripheral blood NK and her decidual NK). Very next experiment: a GdA specificity-and-necessity perturbation with the readout unchanged - GdA vs de-sialylated GdA vs an irrelevant sialylated glycoprotein at matched 5 ug/mL protein load (the load control Lee 2019 lacks), plus L-selectin blockade and PAEP knockdown in endometrial epithelial organoid conditioned medium, run head-to-head against the TGF-beta arm (Keskin 2007, PMID 17360654) and the hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine arm (Cerdeira 2013, PMID 23487420) that already yield the same CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ output, scoring CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a/VEGF.
b.action_if_no: NO = no clonal relationship; the CD9+CD49a+ cells are a selected/expanded pre-existing fraction, or decidual NK are not recent progeny of circulating NK at all. Very next experiment: run the identical GdA perturbation on the compartment that does give rise to dNK - decidual CD34+ precursors differentiating on decidual stroma (Vacca 2011) - adding and withholding GdA with the same de-sialylated-GdA, load, and anti-L-selectin controls and the same CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a/VEGF panel. Same reagent, same controls, same readout, same success criterion; only the cell placed in the well changes.
b.both_answers_reason: The two branches converge on one experiment: give or withhold glycodelin-A with the missing specificity/load controls and score the dNK marker panel. That experiment is mandatory under YES and under NO, its design is identical, and what would count as a positive is identical - the lineage answer changes only which starting cell goes into the well, never whether the experiment is run or how it is read. The causal clause is therefore ungated by the lineage result, which is the failure mode this filter exists to catch. Three further strikes. (a) The NO branch is the vacuous one named in the preregistration: no recent clonal relationship between decidual and peripheral NK is already the field's working model (Vacca 2011 local CD34+ precursors; Sojka 2014 eLife PMC3975579 tissue-resident uterine NK as a distinct lineage from conventional cNK), so NO confirms the prior and the next move is exactly what it is today. (b) Barcoding is not even the deciding instrument for the one decidable sub-question: conversion vs selection at day 5 is discriminated by CFSE/CTV dilution, absolute cell counts, and a day-0 CD9+/CD49a+ frequency within the CD56bright gate - all cheap, all omitted from the source study - so clonal tracing would be adjudicating something a proliferation control settles first. (c) Because the marker state is reversible and traffic-dependent (Niehrs 2025), the assay has no stable target: YES in one sampling window and NO in another are both true readings of the same biology, so neither answer can be converted into a committed next step.
b.compartments_needed: Minimum pair for adjudication: (A) peripheral blood NK, both CD16-CD56bright and CD56dim gates, from a pregnant woman; (B) decidual NK (CD9+CD49a+CD56superbright) from the SAME woman's decidua basalis/parietalis. Because the GdA exposure window is progesterone-driven and first-trimester-weighted, compartment B must be GdA-high first-trimester decidua, not term tissue, for the claim's own premise to hold. Strongly desirable additions: (C) pre-pregnancy secretory-phase endometrial uNK from the same woman in a prior cycle, to catch the endometrial-to-decidual step rather than only its endpoint; (D) the decidual CD34+ precursor compartment (Vacca 2011), which travels with B and is the competing origin that any clonal result must be scored against; (E) bone marrow, only if the question is pushed back to the HSC-level ancestor. For an in-vitro-only version, the "compartments" collapse to day-0 sorted CD9-CD49a- CD56bright NK and the day-5 CD9+CD49a+ population from one culture, which is trivially paired but answers only the narrow selection-vs-conversion sub-question.
b.compartments_obtainable: Partly, and only under a hard surgical-and-pregnancy constraint. A+B paired from one human: YES in principle and routinely done for phenotyping - it is exactly the sourcing Lee 2019 used - but first-trimester decidua is obtainable ONLY at surgery, specifically surgical termination of pregnancy, and ONLY during pregnancy; term decidua parietalis requires Caesarean section or delivery. That makes A+B a single terminal timepoint per woman with no repeat sampling and no before/after GdA-exposure comparison in the same individual, which is fatal for a claim about a factor driving a transition over time. Not post-mortem-restricted. C is separately obtainable as an outpatient Pipelle endometrial biopsy in a prior cycle, so a preconception cohort could in principle assemble blood + endometrium longitudinally (cohorts of this scale exist - PMID 40561039 biopsied 924 women pre-pregnancy), but the terminal decidual sample still requires a pregnancy ending in surgery, so the full A+B+C set is only completable in women whose pregnancies are terminated or delivered surgically. D comes with B at no extra access cost. E (bone marrow) requires a separate aspirate essentially never taken alongside a termination, so an HSC-anchored version is not obtainable paired. Tooling constraint on the human arm: prospective label-based barcoding is impossible in a human pregnancy, so the only usable primitive is endogenous - mtDNA variants via mtscATAC-seq or MAESTER (PMID 35210612), or somatic epimutations (PMID 40399669) - and their clonal resolution depends on prior clonal expansion (PMID 40134031), which is precisely what is in dispute for a polyclonal blood NK pool.
b.compartment_notes: The decisive access asymmetry is species, not tissue, and it splits the claim in two so that no single organism can test it whole. PAEP/glycodelin has NO mouse or rat ortholog - the gene is lost in mouse, rat, rabbit, tarsier, megabat and dolphin and is functional only in higher primates (confirmed in Phase A). So the entire mouse lineage toolkit that could address the structural clause - T-bet fate mapping of decidual NK (PMID 41782473, 2026), circulating-NK-to-tissue-resident conversion demonstrated in skin (PMID 38157853), autocrine TGF-beta1 driving resident NK differentiation (PMID 39692745), Confetti/Polylox/CRISPR recorders - can never address the "glycodelin-A drives" clause without first humanizing PAEP. Conversely the human arm is the only place GdA exists, and there prospective barcoding is unavailable, leaving only endogenous mtDNA/epimutation readouts on surgically-constrained single-timepoint tissue. Note also that the structural question underneath this claim - do circulating cells convert to a tissue-resident state, or is the resident pool locally derived - has already been attacked with lineage tools in the adjacent fields the mechanism is borrowed from: skin NK residency (PMID 38157853), rhesus macaque NK clonal compartmentalization by lentiviral barcoding (PMID 30389798, PMID 31649681), and blood-versus-tonsil compartmentalized human T cell clones (PMID 41308653). None of these were run on decidua, and none of them could attribute the transition to a named ligand, which is the same wall this claim hits.

o.already_traced_evidence:
TRUE for the lineage-decidable CORE of T5 ("blood/circulating NK are the precursors of uterine/decidual tissue-resident NK"), FALSE for the GdA-specific attribution. Split explicitly:

(1) MOUSE, ANSWERED WITH A LINEAGE-RELATIONSHIP TOOL, AND ANSWERED WITH THE SAME HORMONE AXIS. Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025, PMID 39708955. Parabiosis + intravascular fluorescent antibody labeling + flow. They asked precisely "what is the origin of uterine trNK cells" and showed trNK are DERIVED FROM peripheral conventional NK cells; ovariectomy at 3 wk abolished uterine trNK unless progesterone was given; MPA expanded the cNK-derived trNK compartment and a progesterone-receptor antagonist abolished it. T5's structural core is "a progesterone-driven decidual signal converts circulating NK into decidual-type tissue NK." That precursor-product relationship, under progesterone control, is already adjudicated affirmatively. Caveat: parabiosis is a circulating-origin/chimerism tool, not a per-cell clonal barcode (it shows the compartment is fed from blood, not that cell x and cell y share a recent ancestor), and GdA/PAEP is never tested.

(2) HUMAN, ANSWERED WITH GENETIC-ORIGIN LINEAGE ASSIGNMENT. Strunz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 41811987 ("Reconstitution of the uterine immune milieu after uterus or hematopoietic stem cell transplantation"). Single-cell donor-vs-recipient assignment by SNP demultiplexing and disparate HLA (scRNA-seq + high-parameter flow) in women after uterus transplant (UTx) and after HSCT. After UTx, recipient-derived immune cells REPLACED donor immune cells in the endometrium; after HSCT, near-complete DONOR-derived reconstitution INCLUDING formation of tissue-resident lymphocytes; one patient had male-origin cells reconstituting the endometrium. This is the human version of "uterine tissue-resident NK are progeny of the circulating/BM-derived pool," answered YES. Caveat: non-pregnant endometrium, not GdA-high first-trimester decidua; genetic origin, not clonal barcode; NK not isolated as the sole question.

(3) MOUSE FATE MAP APPLIED TO dNK DIRECTLY. Mohamed et al., Am J Reprod Immunol 2026, PMID 41782473. Tbx21-Cre x Rosa26-RFP T-bet fate mapping across virgin uterus, decidua, placenta at GD6-18, plus bulk and scRNA-seq of fate-mapped cells. Records expression history (did this cell ever express T-bet), so it adjudicates a differentiation-history question in the decidua, and concludes dNK adapt transcriptionally rather than undergo lineage diversion. Not clonal, not GdA, mouse only.

(4) THE ANALOGOUS NK SUBSET-CONVERSION CLAIM, ADJUDICATED BY TRUE CLONAL BARCODING, AND ANSWERED NO. Wu et al., Sci Immunol 2018, PMID 30389798. Lentiviral high-diversity barcoding of autologous rhesus HSPCs, >4 yr follow-up: CD56-CD16+ NK clones stayed long-term clonally UNCOUPLED from CD56+CD16- NK; "linear NK cell production from multipotent hematopoietic progenitors or less mature CD56+CD16- cells is negligible during homeostasis and moderate proliferative stress." T5's compartment A is exactly the CD56bright/CD56+CD16- gate. The same lab's Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190, extended barcoding to blood-vs-tissue NK (liver, spleen, lung, GI, LN, BAL) and found tissue-resident NK clones distinct from blood, with expanded PB DN clones feeding tissue CD16+ and DN NK but ABSENT from tissue CD56+CD16- NK. Uterus/decidua were not sampled and the animals were not pregnant.

(5) THE GdA-SPECIFIC CLAIM ITSELF: NOT TRACED BY ANY LINEAGE METHOD. The source paper, Lee et al., Hum Reprod 2019, PMID 30597092, is bulk flow cytometry on immunomagnetically/FACS-sorted blood CD16-CD56bright NK treated with 5 ug/mL amniotic-fluid-purified GdA, scoring CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a, VEGF/IGFBP-1 secretion, L-selectin binding, ERK blots, HUVEC tube formation and trophoblast invasion. No clonal marker, no single-cell readout, no proliferation/division control, so it does not even separate selective outgrowth of a pre-existing CD9+CD49a+ subset from conversion of CD9-CD49a- cells. Search "glycodelin clonal lineage tracing barcode" returns ZERO records in PubMed and EPMC. No mtDNA / mtscATAC / MAESTER / barcode study has ever been applied to GdA-exposed NK, and none to paired human blood + first-trimester decidual NK.

Also found and checked, adjacent but not occupying: Vacca-type in-situ origin work "In vivo generation of decidual natural killer cells from resident hematopoietic progenitors" PMID 24179150 (differentiation potential of decidual CD34+ precursors, no clonal marker); Sojka et al. J Immunol 2018 PMID 30275046 (local proliferation of uterine trNK during decidualization, BrdU-type, not clonal); Strunz et al. Sci Immunol 2021 PMID 33617461 (continuous human uNK differentiation, trajectory inference, no lineage tool); "Deciphering decidual leukocyte traffic with serial intravascular staining" PMID 38268922 (mouse trafficking, not clonal); Orrantia et al. iScience 2022 PMID 36262311 (blood NK acquire a CD9+ decidual-LIKE phenotype in vivo after autologous HSCT, bulk RNA-seq + flow only, no clonal marker, and notably with no decidua and no GdA present, which is a phenotype-without-tissue counterexample worth knowing); Greene et al. bioRxiv 2025 doi 10.1101/2025.07.05.663267 (human uNK residency program, scRNA-seq, cited by PMID 41811989, not lineage-tooled).

For the in-vitro-only sub-question (selection vs conversion in a dish), the nearest tooled precedent is Vo et al., Blood Adv 2024, PMID 38484189: DNA-barcode clonal tracing across in vitro NK/ILC differentiation stages from cord-blood CD34+ on OP9, which resolved S3b-NK vs S4-NK vs ILC3 relatedness. Same instrument, different input cells, no GdA, no dNK markers.
o.nearest_occupant:
Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, Mucosal Immunology 2025, PMID 39708955, "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus."

What it did: parabiosed mice plus intravascular antibody labeling to separate truly tissue-resident from blood-borne cells, combined with ovariectomy at 3 weeks and hormone add-back (progesterone, medroxyprogesterone 17-acetate) and a progesterone-receptor antagonist.

What it established: uterine trNK cells are derived from peripheral conventional NK cells, and that derivation is progesterone-dependent and progesterone-expandable.

How it differs from T5, precisely, on four axes:
1. SPECIES/COMPARTMENT. Mouse uterus and estrous-cycle uterus, not human first-trimester decidua basalis/parietalis. T5's compartment B (CD9+CD49a+CD56superbright first-trimester dNK) has no mouse equivalent with matching markers, and the mouse work is largely non-pregnant/peri-implantation.
2. LIGAND. Progesterone as a systemic hormone, not glycodelin-A. GdA is the downstream progesterone-driven decidual glycoprotein in humans; mice have no GdA acting in the way the claim requires. So the mouse result establishes THAT the conversion route exists under progesterone, while leaving entirely open WHICH progesterone-induced decidual factor executes it. That "which factor" question is a mechanism question, not a clonal-structure question, so the residual unoccupied part of T5 is the part clonal barcoding cannot decide anyway.
3. TOOL CLASS. Parabiosis + intravascular staining is a compartment-origin/chimerism assay: it says the tissue pool is fed from the circulating pool. It is not the barcoding primitive (do these two cells share an ancestor and how recently). A barcode could in principle still add clone-level resolution (e.g., whether one blood clone seeds many dNK, or dNK are polyclonally seeded), but the yes/no origin answer is already in hand.
4. STARTING GATE. Mouse cNK is the DX5+/CD49b+ circulating pool, closest to human CD56dim; T5 nominates human CD16-CD56bright specifically. Note that the one true clonal-barcode result bearing on that gate, Wu et al. Sci Immunol 2018 PMID 30389798, found CD56+CD16- NK do NOT feed the mature CD16+ pool in macaque blood, i.e., the barcoding field's answer for the CD56bright-as-precursor premise in the periphery has already been NO in the one place it was tested.

Two co-nearest occupants that matter as much:
- Strunz et al., Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 41811987: human UTx and HSCT with SNP/HLA-based single-cell donor-vs-recipient origin assignment; recipient cells replace donor immune cells in transplanted endometrium, and HSCT gives near-complete donor-derived endometrial reconstitution including tissue-resident lymphocytes. This is the human answer to "are uterine tissue-resident lymphocytes progeny of the circulating/BM pool" and it is YES. Differs from T5 by being non-pregnant endometrium (not GdA-high decidua), by not being NK-specific, and by using genetic origin rather than clonal barcodes.
- Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190: lentiviral barcoded autologous HSPC transplant in rhesus, clonal comparison of blood vs tissue-resident T, B, myeloid and NK across liver, spleen, lung, GI, LN. This is the exact instrument T5 would need, already built and validated for NK. It has simply never been pointed at uterus/decidua, and the animals were not pregnant.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
Yes, heavily occupied across all three fields, and in two of them the same structural question is considered settled.

T CELL FIELD (uses TCR as a free endogenous barcode, so it has been ahead of NK on this question for a decade):
- Poon et al., Nat Immunol 2023, PMID 36658238, "Tissue adaptation and clonal segregation of human memory T cells in barrier sites": paired blood + multiple tissues from the same organ donors, TCR clonotype sharing used to ask exactly "is the tissue compartment the progeny of the blood compartment." Answer: partial sharing with substantial clonal segregation, i.e., the tissue pool is not simply a converted blood pool.
- PMID 38422982 (2024), "Dynamic establishment of recipient resident memory T cell repertoire after human intestinal transplantation": donor/recipient chimerism plus TCR repertoire tracking over time in human transplanted gut. This is the exact design that the human uterine field is now copying via UTx/HSCT (PMID 41811987), and it answers the recruitment-vs-residency origin question directly.
- Snyder/Zuber-type solid-organ transplant TRM work generally: the "circulating precursor converts to tissue-resident phenotype" claim has been adjudicated with genetic origin markers, not phenotype, since the mid-2010s.
Implication for T5: the T cell field's verdict is that the honest answer is usually "partially, with clonal segregation," not a clean yes/no. A dNK result is likely to land in the same ambiguous middle, which is exactly the zone where a lineage answer is least actionable.

ILC FIELD:
- ILC1/ILC2/ILC3 plasticity has been fate-mapped in mouse for years (Rorc-fate map, Bcl11b, T-bet driving ILC3-to-ILC1 conversion in gut/liver/inflamed mucosa; see review PMID 38563448 and the mechanistic literature cited inside PMID 41782473).
- Critically, T-bet fate mapping has ALREADY been run on decidual NK specifically: PMID 41782473 (2026). Its conclusion is that dNK do NOT undergo lineage diversion despite losing T-bet, they adapt transcriptionally. That is the ILC field's tool answering the decidual version of the plasticity question already.
- Flommersfeld et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 34437840: single-cell fate mapping/barcoding of mouse NK identified an ILC1-like lineage bridging innate and adaptive recognition, i.e., single-NK-cell clonal fate has been resolved in vivo.
- Vo et al., Blood Adv 2024, PMID 38484189: human DNA-barcode clonal tracing separating NK from noncytotoxic ILC developmental routes in vitro.

MYELOID FIELD:
- Liu et al., Cell 2019, PMID 31491389, Ms4a3-Cre fate mapping: cleanly separated monocyte-derived from embryonically-seeded tissue macrophages and effectively closed the "does the circulating cell become the tissue cell" question for macrophages. This is the canonical demonstration that this structural question is answerable and, once answered with a proper lineage tool, stops being a research program.

NK-INTERNAL CROSSFIELD:
- The macaque barcoding program (PMIDs 24702997, 29141868, 30389798, 36605190) has already applied the exact primitive to NK ontogeny, NK subset interconversion, and blood-vs-tissue NK clonal relationships. Human adaptive NK clonality has been read out with natural somatic markers (Corat et al., Blood 2017, PMID 27903532, PIGA-mutant clones in PNH; Rueckert et al., PMID 36289449, clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of NK memory).

Bottom line on borrowed occupancy: T5 borrows "differentiation/plasticity of a circulating cell into a tissue-adapted cell." Every field it borrows that from has already answered it with a lineage tool, and the reproductive-immunology field itself has now answered it twice (mouse parabiosis PMID 39708955; human transplant chimerism PMID 41811987). What remains unoccupied is only the GdA-as-the-driver part, which is a mechanism/causation question that the clonal barcoding primitive explicitly cannot decide.

b.why:
FALSE — this is the reversible-state carve-out, and it fails on three independent grounds.

(1) THE PREDICATE IS A STATE, NOT AN ANCESTRY RELATION. The claim is "IL-35 drives NK TOWARD a CD9+CD103+CD49a+ ILC1-like PHENOTYPE." Both operative terms are non-lineage: "toward ... phenotype" is directional state language, and "ILC1-like" is a functional/phenotypic predicate. The primitive (do two cells share an ancestor, how recently) returns nothing about whether a cell is ILC1-like. This is the rubric's "A becomes functionally B-like" case.

(2) BOTH READINGS PRODUCE THE SAME CLONAL TOPOLOGY — the decisive point. The two live interpretations are (a) genuine differentiation of cNK into an ILC1-like cell, and (b) a reversible, cytokine-maintained surface program (three integrins/tetraspanin) layered on unchanged cNK. Under BOTH, barcodes straddle the CD49a-/CD49a+ boundary: clones appear in both marker fractions at intermediate timepoints and the whole day-0 repertoire is represented by day 8. There is no barcode topology that separates "converted" from "transiently up-regulated ITGA1/ITGAE/CD9," because no lineage branch is created in either case. Clonal structure is degenerate with respect to the question actually being asked. The 48 h washout non-reversal reported by the source does not rescue this — 48 h of marker persistence is not a heritable branch, and the cross-field literature says the program is generic and reversible over longer horizons (Fonseca ex-TRM, PMID 32066954; Zitti Immunity 2023, PMID 37269830, showing IL-15+TGF-b induces CD49a and a TRM program on CIRCULATING human CD8 T cells, RUNX2/RUNX3-dependent — i.e. the same integrin program is cross-lineage and therefore not lineage-diagnostic).

(3) THE CAUSAL CLAUSE IS OUTSIDE THE PRIMITIVE. "IL-35 drives" is a perturbation-attribution claim. Lineage supplies no causal attribution; and the proximal cause in the source's own data is autocrine TGF-b (fully abrogated by anti-TGF-b1/2/3 and Galunisertib, reproduced by TGF-b alone), so the clause is one step upstream of the measured mechanism regardless of any clonal readout.

WHAT IS DECIDABLE, AND WHY IT DOES NOT SAVE THE ROW: there is a narrow lineage-shaped residue the claim does not assert — "is the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ population the clonal progeny of marker-negative cNK, or the outgrowth of a pre-existing, clonally distinct subset?" That is a legitimate same/different-lineage question and is decidable in principle (mtDNA-variant tracking or lentiviral barcoding on day-0 blood NK, indexed on the marker triad). This is why T6 is a near-miss rather than a trivial FALSE. But it is not the claim, it fails B2 below, and it is gated on a marker definition the field itself calls unresolved: Wu et al. (PMID 36605190, PMC9808525), the only primate barcode study of blood-vs-tissue NK clonality, states outright that "definitive markers to distinguish NK from ILCs in tissues remain unresolved" and that they "are not able to exclude the presence of ILCs." A clonal answer inherits the gate it is asked to adjudicate; if "ILC1-like" is defined by the very markers in dispute, the barcode result is only as meaningful as the sort.

(Decidability here does not depend on the Phase A dispute over the primary source's verification status — the claim's structure fails the primitive either way.)
b.action_if_yes:
ANSWER = YES (clones straddle the boundary; barcodes/mtDNA clones found in BOTH the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ and marker-negative fractions of the same day-4 well, converted cells drawn from across the day-0 repertoire with no clonal restriction) => reading: "conversion, not selection."

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: nothing lineage-shaped. Concretely, all three next moves are non-clonal:
(a) REAGENT QC — assay PeproTech 200-37 single-chain IL-35 (HEK293, 406-aa IL12A-EBI3 fusion, used at 100 ng/mL) against vehicle on a Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rb1-IL-12Rb2 reporter with pSTAT1/pSTAT4 readout, i.e. the Aparicio-Siegmund assay (PMID 25259790), because if the recombinant is inactive or carries a TGF-b-inducing contaminant the clonal result is about a different molecule entirely.
(b) IS THE STATE A SET-POINT OR AN ENDPOINT — extend washout well past 48 h (7-14 d) and add Galunisertib AFTER conversion is established, asking whether CD9/CD103/CD49a revert. A revertible marker set is a state, not a fate.
(c) IS "ILC1-LIKE" ANYTHING BEYOND GENERIC TGF-b RESIDENCY — score the same cells against a CD8 TRM program (ITGA1, ITGAE, RUNX2, CD9) alongside the paper's ILC1 UCell signature; PMID 37269830 predicts they are the same program, which would void the ILC1 interpretation without touching lineage.

None of (a)-(c) requires or uses the barcodes. The YES answer changes nothing about what you do next.
b.action_if_no:
ANSWER = NO (clones partition; the CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells trace to a restricted set of pre-existing day-0 clones essentially absent from the marker-negative fraction) => reading: "selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing subset."

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: first, disbelieve the assay, then run the same three experiments as the YES branch.
(a) ASSAY CONTROL FIRST — re-run the culture starting from a FACS-purified CD9-CD103-CD49a- day-0 fraction. This is the single control Phase A already flags as missing (t=0 was never gated marker-negative), it is a one-day flow experiment, and it settles selection-vs-conversion completely WITHOUT any barcodes. A NO result would also be immediately suspect on technical grounds: lentiviral barcoding requires activation/transduction that itself induces CD103/CD49a through the same TGF-b axis being studied, and an <=8-day culture in which IL-35 SUPPRESSES proliferation gives mtDNA-based tracking almost no dividing generations, so apparent clonal partition is confounded by near-zero clonal resolution. The first response to NO is therefore to re-test the instrument, not to act on the biology.
(b) then the identical REAGENT QC (PMID 25259790 assay), and
(c) then the identical TGF-b-dependence / TRM-vs-ILC1 signature-specificity tests.

So even the "interesting" branch routes through a cheap flow control that makes the lineage assay redundant, and then converges on the YES branch's experiments.
b.both_answers_reason:
FALSE — fails on all three of the strict tests: convergence, vacuity, and wrong-instrument.

CONVERGENCE. After stripping the assay-control step, the YES and NO branches terminate in the SAME two experiments: (i) validate the single-chain IL-35 reagent on an IL-35R reporter, and (ii) determine whether the CD9/CD103/CD49a program is a TGF-b-maintained reversible set-point and whether it is distinguishable from the generic CD8 TRM program. The load-bearing uncertainties in this claim — reagent validity, mechanistic displacement onto TGF-b, and whether "ILC1-like" is a real identity or a generic integrin signature — are all non-lineage, so the clonal answer does not gate any of them. Whichever way the barcodes fall, the next bench day is identical.

VACUITY OF THE YES BRANCH. YES is not a discriminating outcome, it is the answer already forced by data in hand: IL-35 suppresses proliferation, survival is unchanged out to day 9, "nearly all cells" are marker-positive by day 8 (arithmetically unreachable by selecting a near-absent blood precursor in the absence of division), and both >98%-pure sorted NKG2C+ and >98%-pure sorted NKG2C- subsets converted independently. A prospective clonal assay whose result is pre-determined by existing controls returns "conversion confirmed, proceed to the experiments we already needed" — the textbook vacuous branch.

WRONG INSTRUMENT FOR THE ONLY DECIDABLE RESIDUE. The one sub-question lineage could answer (pre-existing subset vs conversion) is answered more cheaply, more directly, and without the transduction/proliferation confounds by a single FACS step: purify CD9-CD103-CD49a- NK at t=0 and re-run. Since that control is a mandatory prerequisite in BOTH branches anyway, the clonal experiment is dominated by a control that must be run regardless. Spending a barcoding assay to reach a conclusion that a one-day sort already delivers is not an actionable fork.

RESIDUAL ASYMMETRY, AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH. A strict steelman: NO would overturn the source's central claim and its downstream pan-cancer/TCGA inference, and would prompt prospective isolation of a distinct CD9+CD103+CD49a+ blood precursor — nominally a different experiment from the YES branch. But (1) NO is close to excluded a priori by the proliferation/survival/sorted-subset data above, (2) the first and correct response to NO is to suspect the assay's own artifacts rather than the biology, and (3) prospective isolation of that precursor is again the same t=0 sort. The asymmetry is nominal, not operational. OUT.
b.compartments_needed:
Two distinct compartment sets, depending on which version of the claim is adjudicated.

VERSION 1 — the in vitro claim as actually evidenced (population-frequency shift in culture):
  A. Day-0 human peripheral blood CD56+CD3- NK, prospectively gated CD9-CD103-CD49a- (the marker-negative starting compartment).
  B. Day-4 and day-8 CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells from the IL-35 arm of the SAME well.
  B'. Day-4/day-8 marker-NEGATIVE cells from that same well (the within-well comparator that makes the straddle-vs-partition read possible; without it there is no boundary to test).
  C. The paired IL-2-alone well from the SAME donor.
All four come from one buffy coat or leukapheresis from one healthy donor, split across wells. Same individual by construction.

VERSION 2 — the in vivo claim the result is deployed to support (tumour NK are IL-35-converted ILC1-like cells):
  A. Autologous peripheral blood cNK from the patient.
  B. Tumour-infiltrating CD9+CD103+CD49a+ group-1 ILC from the resected lesion.
  C. Adjacent non-malignant tissue from the same organ (to separate tumour-driven from tissue-intrinsic residency).
  D. A compartment defined by prior IL-35 EXPOSURE — required for the "IL-35 drives" clause, and it does not exist as a sortable population.

OPTIONAL PHYSIOLOGICAL COMPARATOR (if one wants the natural human CD9+CD49a+ compartment rather than tumour): decidual NK, for which CD9+CD49a+ is the canonical hallmark; or liver-resident CD49a+ NK.
b.compartments_obtainable:
MIXED — TRUE and trivially so for Version 1; TRUE-but-surgical for the tissue arm of Version 2; STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for the compartment that carries the claim's causal clause.

VERSION 1: FULLY OBTAINABLE, PAIRED, FROM ONE HUMAN, WITH NO ANATOMICAL OR ETHICAL CONSTRAINT. A single healthy-donor buffy coat split across wells yields A, B, B' and C simultaneously from the same individual. Not post-mortem, not surgical, not pregnancy-limited, not mouse-only. This is one of the rare rows where compartment access is a complete non-issue — which is precisely why T6 must be killed on B1/B2 rather than on B3. Compartment availability is not the binding constraint here.

VERSION 2: A is a routine blood draw (obtainable paired at induction of anaesthesia). B and C are SURGERY-ONLY — they require a resection specimen or biopsy; there is no non-surgical route to tumour-infiltrating or adjacent-normal lymphocytes. Paired blood+tumour+adjacent-normal from one patient is nonetheless standard practice in tumour immunology and is exactly the sampling underlying the public cohorts (lung, oesophagus, colon, breast) that the source re-analysed in silico rather than sampling itself. So B/C are obtainable, at surgery, paired, from one human.

COMPARTMENT D IS NOT OBTAINABLE IN ANY SPECIES-APPROPRIATE FORM. Prior IL-35 exposure is not a sortable cell property, there is no fate-mark for having seen IL-35, and no human in vivo IL-35 perturbation exists. A tumour cell that converted in vivo carries no feature distinguishing it from a tissue ILC1 of separate ontogeny. This — not tissue access — is the real compartment failure, and no amount of specimen collection fixes it.

OPTIONAL COMPARATORS, flagged explicitly as the brief requires: decidual NK (the canonical human CD9+CD49a+ compartment) is PREGNANCY-ONLY, obtainable solely at elective termination or delivery, and can never be paired with the same individual's pre-conversion state under a controlled perturbation. Liver-resident CD49a+ NK are TRANSPLANT/PERFUSATE- or POST-MORTEM-ONLY in humans.
b.compartment_notes:
SPECIES SCISSORS — the structurally important note. The compartments are obtainable in the species where the perturbation cannot be performed (human: blood and tumour are easy, but no in vivo IL-35 challenge and no fate-mark), while the perturbation-plus-fate-map version is only executable in the species where the claim was never made (mouse: Ebi3/Il12a conditional deletion, Ncr1/Eomes fate maps, parabiosis, Polylox/confetti). Human IL-35 reagent biology and the human CD9/CD103/CD49a triad do not transfer cleanly to mouse, and the mouse literature already routes this phenotype through TGF-b rather than IL-35. So the two halves of a decisive experiment sit in different organisms and cannot be joined.

NEAREST EXISTING OCCUPANCY FOUND (informational, for the shortlist's benefit; not a formal B4 verdict): Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525, archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC9808525.txt — autologous barcoded-HSPC transplant in rhesus macaque tracking clonal relationships of NK across peripheral blood, liver, spleen, lung and GI tract. This is the closest thing to the structural question ("are marker-defined tissue NK clonally the same population as blood NK?") actually executed with a clonal primitive in a primate, and it reports tissue-restricted NK clone sets alongside shared blood/tissue clones. It also supplies the caveat that guts the marker gate: "definitive markers to distinguish NK from ILCs in tissues remain unresolved," authors "not able to exclude the presence of ILCs." Also found: PMID 40621477 (lentiviral barcode delivery into human and rhesus NK — establishes the barcoding is technically feasible in NK, which is why B2 rather than feasibility is the binding failure).

SEARCH HONESTY (rule G3): my targeted searches for mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER applied specifically to NK or ILC1, and for Polylox/CRISPR-recorder/confetti applied to NK-to-ILC1 conversion, returned reviews and off-target hits only — thin and ambiguous. I am NOT recording those as "nobody has done it." Treat the already_traced status for the mtDNA-in-NK and recorder-in-ILC1 arms as NOT_SEARCHED, not FALSE. The Phase A adversarial pass separately documents the relevant in vivo primary sources (Flommersfeld PMID 34437840 single-cell colour-barcoding + parabiosis; Gao PMID 28759001; Cortez PMID 27156386; Sojka PMID 24714492; Gasteiger PMID 26472762), and per G4 the T cell/TRM field has already answered the same structural question by TCR clonal-repertoire overlap between paired blood and skin (Zitti, PMID 37269830) — the clonal step NK cells cannot borrow, having no rearranged receptor.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE SHORTLIST: T6 is OUT, failing B1 (cytokine-induced reversible within-lineage state; both readings share one clonal topology) and failing B2 decisively (convergent branches, vacuous YES, and a one-day FACS control that dominates the lineage assay). B3 is the row's only strong leg and it cannot carry it.

o.already_traced_evidence:
NOBODY HAS ADJUDICATED THIS CLAIM WITH A CLONAL/LINEAGE METHOD — neither Version 1 (in vitro) nor Version 2 (in vivo tumour).

HARD NEGATIVE ON THE IL-35 AXIS. PubMed field query `IL-35 AND (lineage tracing OR clonal OR barcode)` returns count=0. Query `IL-35 NK cell` (8 recent hits reviewed) contains no lineage/clonal paper — only the primary source (PMID 40610398), an EGFR-NSCLC IL-35 immunosurveillance paper (PMID 41357575), and unrelated pharmacology. There is no IL-35 fate-mapping or IL-35 barcoding literature at all, in any cell type.

THE PRIMARY SOURCE ITSELF IS NOT A LINEAGE STUDY. Confirmed from the archived Phase A audit and abstract: Picant et al. (PMID 40610398) used 10x CellPlex CMO hashing, which is SAMPLE/CONDITION hashing, not lineage barcoding. No cell was tracked. The claim rests entirely on per-well population-frequency shifts (n=3-5 donors).

METHOD-CLASS SEARCHES ALL CAME BACK EMPTY ON THIS TARGET:
- mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER + NK/ILC + clonal/lineage: PubMed count=8, of which exactly one is on-topic (PMID 36289449, blood NKG2C+ adaptive NK, no CD49a/CD103/ILC1 anywhere in the text — grep for "CD49a" and "ILC1" in the archived full text returns 0 hits each).
- `("tissue-resident" OR "tissue resident") AND (NK OR "natural killer") AND (barcod* OR "clonal track*" OR "lineage tracing")`: PubMed count=2 total (PMID 36605190, PMID 29141868). The entire world literature clonally tracking tissue-resident NK is two papers, both macaque HSPC-barcoding, neither involving IL-35, tumour, CD103 or CD9.
- `Confetti AND (ILC OR "innate lymphoid" OR "NK cell")`: count=0.
- `ILC1 AND ("fate map*" OR "lineage tracing")`: count=13, fully reviewed; none touches IL-35, CD9, or human in vitro conversion.
- Polylox/PolyloxExpress + ILC, and CRISPR-recorder + ILC: no on-target hits (only generic method reviews, e.g. PMID 39587306).
- `("natural killer"[ti] OR "NK cell"[ti]) AND (lineage tracing OR fate mapping OR barcod* OR clonal*[ti])`: count=63, screened; the only clonal-primitive NK papers are the macaque barcoding series, Rückert 2022, Vo 2024, and the Buchholz single-cell fate-mapping series.

WHAT THE MARKER TRIAD SEARCH SHOWS. `CD9 AND CD103 AND CD49a` in tiab returns only 6 PubMed records ever. Two matter: the primary source (PMID 40610398) and PMID 32332109 (J Immunol 2020, "TGF-β and IL-15 Synergize through MAPK Pathways to Drive the Conversion of Human NK Cells to an Innate Lymphoid Cell 1-like Phenotype") — the same human phenotype, same three markers, produced five years earlier by a different cytokine, also with zero lineage adjudication. So the phenotype has been generated twice in vitro and traced zero times.

CAVEAT (G3-honest): my negative is strong for PubMed/EPMC-indexed work through the search date. I did not exhaustively sweep bioRxiv/medRxiv preprints; a 2025-2026 preprint applying mtDNA tracing to human tumour NK/ILC1 could exist unindexed. I checked the obvious candidate (PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704, the Liu et al. preprint) and confirmed it does not cover the residency markers. Two of my cross-field citations (PMID 25962122, PMID 31278120) were confirmed at title/PMID level only, not read to methods.
o.nearest_occupant:
There is no single occupant; the claim sits in an unoccupied gap between four adjacent published studies, each of which fails to cover it on a different axis.

1. NEAREST ON METHOD + SPECIES + CELL TYPE — Rückert T, Lareau CA, Mashreghi MF, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022;23:1551-1563. PMID 36289449 / PMC9663309. This is the proof that the exact primitive works in exactly this cell type: mtscATAC-seq/ASAP-seq on ex vivo human NK cells from 4 HCMV+ and 3 HCMV- donors, using somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous barcodes to reconstruct clonal relationships and link them to chromatin and surface phenotype. HOW IT DIFFERS: it resolves the ADAPTIVE axis (NKG2C+ HCMV-driven clonal expansion), not the RESIDENCY axis. Grepping the full text for "CD49a" returns 0 and "ILC1" returns 0. Peripheral blood only — no tissue, no tumour, no cytokine perturbation, no IL-35. It answers "are adaptive NK clonally expanded?", not "are CD9+CD103+CD49a+ cells the progeny of marker-negative cNK?"

2. NEAREST ON THE STRUCTURAL QUESTION — Flommersfeld S, Böttcher JP, ... Buchholz VR, Grassmann S. "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection." Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304. PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403. This asks T6's exact structural question with a true clonal primitive: retrogenic fluorescent-protein colour barcoding of HSCs, then sorting and adoptively transferring 15-20 SINGLE colour-barcoded CD27+Ly49H+ NK cells into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients, MCMV infection, and reading single-cell-derived progeny. ANSWER OBTAINED: cNK and "ILC1-like NK" are TWO DISTINCT LINEAGES that maintain their phenotype through memory and reinfection — explicitly, "even without MCMV infection, no evidence for maturation of ILC1-like NK cells into the CD62L+ subsets was found." Parabiosis confirmed the ILC1-like subset is spleen-resident while cNK equilibrate. HOW IT DIFFERS: mouse, not human; MCMV, not IL-35; and critically the marker definition is orthogonal — their ILC1-like NK cells are CD27+CD62L-CD160+ and the paper states they LACKED CD49a. So the answer that exists ("separate lineage, not conversion") was obtained for a differently-defined ILC1-like population in a different species under a different stimulus.

3. NEAREST ON VERSION-2 COMPARTMENTS — Liu V, Sandor K, Yan PK, et al. (Satpathy lab). "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44(7), 13 Jul 2026. PMID 42242233 (preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704). mtscATAC-seq + Mitotrek on 218,715 cells from MATCHED tumour, non-involved lung tissue, and PBMC from 5 NSCLC and 5 ovarian cancer patients — i.e. precisely the paired autologous blood + tumour + adjacent-normal compartment set that Version 2 of T6 requires, in humans, with mtDNA clonal resolution. It includes NK/ILC clusters (3-4 NCR1+ clusters). NK finding: expanded NK clones present in NILT and blood; one ovarian tumour (SU-O-005) had substantial NK infiltration with oligoclonal architecture whose expanded clones were ABSENT from matched blood, i.e. a tumour-restricted NK response. HOW IT DIFFERS: verified by grep of the full text — "CD49a" appears 0 times and "CD103" appears 0 times. Residency phenotype was never a variable; NK-to-ILC1 conversion was never asked; the NK analysis is one patient, incidental, and framed as adaptive-like expansion. The infrastructure to answer T6 Version 2 has been built and pointed at myeloid cells, and the NK/ILC1-residency question was simply not asked.

4. NEAREST ON PAIRED BLOOD-VS-TISSUE NK WITH REAL BARCODES — Cai S, et al. "Barcode clonal tracking of tissue-resident immune cells in rhesus macaque highlights distinct clonal distribution pattern of tissue NK cells." Front Immunol 2022. PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525. Autologous transplant of high-diversity barcoded macaque HSPCs; clonal distribution of T, B, myeloid and NK across liver, spleen, lung, jejunum, colon, lymph node vs longitudinal blood, in 5 animals. Found a mixed picture: some large blood clones also expanded in liver/spleen, plus sets of tissue-restricted NK clones unique to lung or GI. Notably they DID stain CD49a and report it on CD56+ and DN NK subsets in all tissues. HOW IT DIFFERS: macaque, not human; steady-state tissues, not tumour; CD49a was a descriptive flow marker, never the sorting axis for clone-sharing analysis; no CD9, no CD103, no IL-35, and no test of whether CD49a+ tissue NK share clones with CD49a- blood NK.

5. NEAREST ON HUMAN NK-vs-ILC LINEAGE WITH LENTIVIRAL BARCODES — Vo DN, ... Malmberg KJ, Sitnicka E. "A temporal developmental map separates human NK cells from noncytotoxic ILCs through clonal and single-cell analysis." Blood Adv 2024;8:2933-2951. PMID 38484189 / PMC11176970. CellTag lentiviral barcode library, low-MOI transduction of human cord-blood Lin-CD34+ cells, ~570 barcoded founders on OP9, 4-week differentiation, then FACS-purified lineage outputs read for barcode sharing. Concluded S3b-NK and S4-NK are closely clonally related while ILC3 is distant. HOW IT DIFFERS: this is DEVELOPMENTAL (progenitor to NK/ILC), not mature-NK-to-ILC1 conversion; the comparator ILC is ILC3, not ILC1; grep confirms "CD49a" 0 hits and "CD103" 0 hits; no cytokine perturbation arm.

ALSO CHECKED AND EXCLUDED AS OCCUPANTS: Frey HC, ... Laouar Y, iScience 2025 (PMID 40104068; preprint PMID 38659946) uses Asialo-GM1 as a "site-agnostic marker for fate mapping NK-to-ILC1 plasticity" across TGF-β and T. gondii models — but this is a phenotypic stability marker, NOT a clonal primitive; no cell is tracked, no ancestry is measured. Park E, ... Sibley LD/Colonna M, eLife 2019 (PMID 31393266 / PMC6703900) sorted congenically distinct Eomes-GFP NK vs ILC1-like cells and adoptively transferred them into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- hosts — population-level transfer, not clonal; it did find some transferred Eomes- ILC1-like cells re-expressing Eomes. Cortez et al. Nat Immunol 2017 (PMID 28759002, SMAD4) and Gao et al. Nat Immunol 2017 (PMID 28759001, TGF-β-driven NK-to-ILC1 tumour immunoevasion; Author Correction PMID 38514890) are the canonical mechanistic parents of this claim and use genetic knockouts plus transfers, never a clonal barcode.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HEAVILY OCCUPIED — G4 fires strongly. T6's structural question, stripped of IL-35, is: "are cells bearing tissue-residency markers the clonal progeny of circulating marker-negative cells of the same type, or a separate lineage?" That question has been asked and answered with lineage tools in all three neighbouring fields, and in two of them the answer is already known.

T CELL FIELD — ANSWERED, and answered first, because T cells carry a free endogenous barcode (the TCR) that NK cells lack. The residency marker in question is literally the same molecule, CD103/ITGAE, induced by the same cytokine, TGF-β. Gaide O et al., "Common clonal origin of central and resident memory T cells following skin immunization," Nat Med 2015, PMID 25962122 — TCR-clonotype adjudication showing skin-resident and circulating memory compartments descend from common clones. Klicznik MM et al., "Human CD4+CD103+ cutaneous resident memory T cells are found in the circulation of healthy individuals," Sci Immunol 2019, PMID 31278120 — the CD103+ tissue-resident phenotype is clonally continuous with blood, i.e. CD103 positivity is a STATE, not a lineage boundary. (Both confirmed at PMID/title level, not read to methods.) This is the single most important cross-field result for T6: the field that borrowed T6 its marker and its cytokine already determined that the TGF-β/CD103 residency phenotype does not partition the clonal tree. Any lineage adjudication of T6 would be re-running, on NK cells, an experiment whose answer in the neighbouring lineage is on the books.

ILC FIELD — ANSWERED for the adjacent conversion. Muraoka WT, ... Tumanov AV, "Campylobacter infection promotes IFNγ-dependent intestinal pathology via ILC3 to ILC1 conversion," Mucosal Immunol 2021, PMID 33214656 / PMC8084871 — RORγt-Cre × ROSA26-YFP cell-fate mapping (methods confirm the Rorc-Cre and ROSA26-YFP alleles) established that the pathogenic IFNγ+T-bet+ NK1.1- ILC1-profile population develops FROM RORγt+ progenitors, i.e. genuine ex-ILC3 conversion. Bielecki P et al., "Skin-resident innate lymphoid cells converge on a pathogenic effector state," Nature 2021, PMID 33536623 — fate-mapping of skin ILC convergence. And within group-1 ILC specifically, Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) is the clonal answer described above: separate lineages, not conversion. So the ILC field has established BOTH outcomes are obtainable and has resolved them case by case with Cre-lox fate maps and single-cell barcoding — meaning T6's question is technically tractable but no longer structurally novel.

MYELOID FIELD — ANSWERED, in the exact human compartment set T6 Version 2 needs. Liu V et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233: mtDNA clonal tracing across matched tumour/adjacent-normal/blood demonstrated that TME-resident myeloid subsets — macrophages and DC3 — are clonally linked to both circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, while also resolving distinct DC-biased versus macrophage-biased clones enriched in tumour versus NILT respectively. That is precisely the "does a tissue-associated state map onto clonal structure?" question, run to completion in human cancer patients. Their quantitative myeloid result (mean 58.5% same-type fraction in myeloid clones vs 78-79% for T/B clones) is the template answer T6 would be reproducing on the NK/ILC1 axis.

NET: the IL-35 wrapper is unoccupied and the NK/CD9-CD103-CD49a version is unoccupied, but the underlying structural question is occupied in T cells (answered: residency marker = state, clones shared), in ILC (answered both ways, case-dependent), and in myeloid (answered: tissue subsets clonally linked to circulating precursors, with clone-level state bias). The borrowed mechanism's occupancy lives in the T cell field it was borrowed from.
