b.why:
DECIDABLE, but only in a specific reading, and two of the claim's three clauses have to be handled separately.

The claim bundles (a) a PROVENANCE assertion — intratumoural NK descend from the NK pool that was in that organ, not from the circulating pool; (b) a TEMPORAL assertion — that ancestral pool was in the organ before the tumour; (c) a FUNCTIONAL rider — "functional" intratumoural NK.

(a) is squarely the primitive's form ("the progeny of A are B" / "A and B are same-or-different lineage") and is DECIDABLE. The two competing hypotheses predict genuinely different clonal structures, not the same one: under X1, tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-same-organ NK and only deeply (at the HSPC root) with blood NK; under the recruitment alternative (Torcellan 2024 PMID 38157853; Horowitz 2026 PMID 42090477) the reverse. The primitive's "how recently" term is what does the work — it separates "kin because both were seeded from the same marrow clone" from "kin because one locally divided into the other." This requires three compartments, not two; with only tumour+organ the answer is symmetric (organ->tumour, tumour->organ, blood->both are all consistent with the same sharing) and would fail.

(c) is NOT lineage-decidable and must be discharged by construction, not by inference: "functional" has to become a sort gate on compartment B (GzmB+/degranulating/IFN-g+ intratumoural NK) so that lineage is asked about an already-functionally-defined bucket. Lineage must never be used to argue the cells are functional.

(b) is decidable ONLY if the mark is applied before the tumour exists (photoconversion/inducible fate map/parabiosis at t0), which makes it a true lineage question — "do these tumour cells descend from the cells I marked in the organ." Read from a single post-tumour timepoint it is not a lineage property at all and must be imported as an assumption.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE REVERSIBLE-STATE TRAP, and the condition under which it becomes one. Tissue residency IS a reversible/inducible state — Torcellan 2024 shows circulating NK acquire it, Horowitz 2026 shows TGF-beta is sufficient ex vivo, Blood 2025 (PMID 40857665) shows chronic activation installs a residency-like state via KLF2 loss. If X1 were phrased as "NK acquire residency inside tumours," both answers would be consistent with one clonal structure and it would be NOT DECIDABLE. But X1 is phrased as an origin claim: which pool did these cells come from. Provenance of a cell from compartment A versus compartment B is pedigree, not state. The state is the confound here, not the claim. CONDITION: this only holds if compartments A and B are defined SPATIALLY (cells physically in the uninvolved organ vs physically in the tumour, with i.v. anti-CD45 labelling to exclude vascular contamination). If compartment A is instead defined phenotypically as CD49a+CD103+CD69+ "trNK", the compartment is a reversible state, cells enter and leave it with no lineage event, and the claim collapses back into the undecidable form. The registry must fix the spatial definition or this row is not decidable.

SECOND CONDITION, from the registry's own ontology. Because this registry treats ILC1 as distinct from NK (T4, P3), a positive result is only about X1 if the marked cells are NK-lineage — otherwise it is Dadi 2016 (PMID 26806130) again, whose resident population is Nfil3-independent and transcriptionally "distinct from conventional NK cells," and whose cNK showed HIGH non-host chimerism. Usefully, that fork is itself a lineage question the same primitive answers (do the tissue cells coalesce with blood cNK, or with an ILC-progenitor-derived clade — cf. Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, "did not interconvert with NK cells"), so it can be settled inside the same experiment rather than assumed.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = tumour NK coalesce recently with uninvolved-organ NK and only at HSPC depth with blood NK; the pre-tumour organ label is recovered inside the established tumour.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: convert the pre-tumour lineage label into a functional handle and selectively ablate ONLY the resident-derived pool, before tumour induction, in the autochthonous model. Concretely: pre-tumour photoconversion or inducible Ncr1/Hobit-driven marking of the uninvolved organ in an animal carrying an inducible DTR restricted to the marked cells; deplete the marked resident pool at t0; read tumour incidence and growth against (i) unlabelled controls and (ii) a recruitment-blocked arm (S1PR/chemokine-axis blockade) that leaves the resident pool intact. This is the experiment the field currently states it cannot do — "the current lack of experimental tools to block recruitment of circulating NK cells or to specifically target the newly identified resident cells currently precludes testing this possibility" — and a YES is exactly what licenses building the tool.

WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a YES makes the resident pool the causally load-bearing compartment and selects a specific therapeutic lever — preserve/expand the resident pool, i.e. the IL-15 axis chosen on residency grounds (Nixon 2022 PMID 35394814, with a filed MSKCC patent on targeting ILC1 IL-15 signalling; supported by Dadi's Il15-/- acceleration versus Nfil3-/- no-effect). It also re-reads the CD49a+ NK prognostic literature in HCC (PMID 31311791) as a genuine residency pedigree rather than a TME-exposure readout. Second, cheaper follow-on available immediately from the same clonal data: test at clone resolution whether the intratumoural clones are the same clones that were locally proliferating pre-tumour — i.e. put Dadi's EdU inference (local proliferation, not immigration) on a clonal footing.
b.action_if_no:
NO = tumour NK coalesce with blood NK and are no more related to uninvolved-organ NK than the HSPC-root baseline; the pre-tumour organ label is absent or negligible inside the tumour.

VERY NEXT EXPERIMENT: a different design on a different compartment — label the CIRCULATING pool at defined times relative to tumour onset (serial photoconversion of blood/spleen, or HSPC barcoding with staggered induction) and measure (i) entry timing and dwell time of intratumoural NK, and (ii) whether a SINGLE recruited clone gives rise to both CD49a+CD103+ "trNK-like" and conventional intratumoural progeny. Point (ii) is the decisive one and is not asked at all on the YES branch: it distinguishes in-situ diversification from one entrant versus separate entrants with pre-set fates, which is precisely the Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) selection-versus-conversion fork that those authors named for tumours themselves. The macrophage field has already run this exact design with photoconversion (PMID 40523200: dwell-time-dependent divergence of monocyte-derived TAM fates), so the protocol is off the shelf.

WHY IT IS NOT VACUOUS: a NO flips the therapeutic lever from preserve-the-resident-pool to promote-recruitment-then-impose-residency, which is the Horowitz ex-vivo TGF-beta ctrNK manufacturing route (PMID 42090477) — and a NO would establish that the manufactured product recapitulates a real in vivo route rather than a flask artefact, which is currently unknown. It also inverts the causal reading of the CD49a+ HCC prognostic signal (pedigree -> TME-exposure biomarker), and it demotes the IL-15/resident axis as a mis-chosen lever. Within this registry it hands the phenomenon to T1 (cNK -> trNK) with a specific, differently designed test rather than terminating inquiry.
b.both_answers_reason:
TRUE, but bound to the mouse pre-tumour-label design; the human-only version FAILS this filter and I record that separately below.

The branches are not the same experiment. YES -> ablate/preserve a resident pool that is now known to exist and to be the source (perturbation applied pre-tumour, to the organ). NO -> time-resolved recruitment and single-entrant diversification (perturbation applied to the circulation, at staggered times). Different compartment perturbed, different labelling schedule, different readout, and opposite therapeutic levers (IL-15 support of a resident pool versus promote-recruitment-and-impose-residency).

STEELMAN FOR FALSE, which I ran and rejected. (i) The flagship downstream programme is origin-agnostic by construction: Horowitz 2026 makes ctrNK by TGF-beta-differentiating PERIPHERAL NK ex vivo, so that ACT platform is unaffected whether the cells were resident, recruited, or made in a flask. Phase A downgraded load-bearing to MEDIUM for exactly this reason. If that were the only dependency, both branches would collapse to "characterise the residency programme" and the row would be OUT. It survives because the OTHER named dependency does flip: the IL-15/resident axis was chosen BECAUSE of the residency model (Dadi: Il15-/- accelerates tumour growth, Nfil3-/- does not), so YES validates the lever and NO shows it mis-chosen. (ii) The realistic outcome is MIXED, not binary — the home field where this structural question is settled (myeloid: Loyher 2018 PMID 30201786, Casanova-Acebes 2021 PMID 34135508) returns "both origins contribute, resident-derived dominate early and are progressively displaced, site-dependent." A ratio rather than a dichotomy is a real weakness, but the ratio's kinetics dictate a different intervention WINDOW, which is still a decision, and the YES-branch ablation is exactly what tests whether the resident-derived fraction is the functionally load-bearing one. The branches bend but do not merge.

WHERE IT FAILS, stated so the shortlist is not corrupted: in the HUMAN three-compartment mtDNA design (Liu 2026 architecture), the NO branch is actionable (redirect to recruitment/T1; re-read the prognostic literature) but the YES branch is close to vacuous — there is no available perturbation of a human resident NK pool, so a YES yields "we conclude resident-derived" and stops. Actionability therefore lives in the mouse instantiation. If the registry intends to prosecute X1 in human surgical material only, this filter should be scored FALSE.

I note that X1 is USER-DESIGNATED HIGHEST PRIORITY and I have not let that carry the pass: the TRUE rests on the branch asymmetry above, and I have named the exact design under which the same claim fails.
b.compartments_needed:
FIVE compartments, needed simultaneously and ideally from one individual. The first three are mandatory; C is the one most often omitted and its absence is fatal.

A. NK resident in the UNINVOLVED SAME ORGAN — defined spatially (in the organ, i.v. anti-CD45-negative), not by CD49a/CD103/CD69, and critically resident there BEFORE the tumour existed.
B. NK INSIDE THE ESTABLISHED TUMOUR, gated functionally at sort (GzmB+/degranulating/IFN-g+) so the "functional" clause is a sorting criterion rather than a lineage inference.
C. CIRCULATING NK (blood, and spleen in mouse). MANDATORY DISCRIMINATOR — without it, shared clones between A and B cannot be separated from common marrow ancestry and neither answer is reachable.
D. BONE MARROW / HSPC compartment, to set the deep-coalescence null: how related are any two NK from this individual by marrow output alone. Without D there is no baseline for "how recently" and the primitive's discriminating term is unusable.
E. An ILC1 / ILC-progenitor-derived comparator from the same tissue, required by this registry's own ontology (T4, P3 treat ILC1 as distinct from NK). Without E a positive result may be an ILC1 result mislabelled as trNK — precisely the fork that made Dadi 2016 unusable for this row.
b.compartments_obtainable:
PARTIAL. Obtainable in full from one mouse; NOT obtainable in full from any human, and the compartment that fails in humans (A with its pre-tumour timepoint) is the one carrying the claim's temporal clause.

HUMAN. A+B+C paired from one person: YES, but AT SURGERY ONLY, and only in organs where tumour-free same-organ tissue is resected alongside the tumour. NSCLC lobectomy is the good case and has actually been done — Liu 2026 (PMID 42242233, GSE302113) obtained tumour + non-involved non-adjacent lung + PBMC from 5 patients. HCC/liver-met resection and nephrectomy are the other good cases. A "BEFORE THE TUMOUR": NOT OBTAINABLE IN HUMANS AT ALL, not post-mortem, not at surgery — no human sample exists of an organ from before its own tumour arose. Contemporaneous uninvolved organ is a proxy that assumes the uninvolved region was not remodelled by the tumour-bearing state, an assumption Liu's own data strain. D (marrow) paired with a solid-tumour resection: only opportunistic (staging biopsy), practically NOT paired. E: sortable from the same sample, but the human NK/ILC1 boundary is contested (PMID 38956380), so the gate is imperfect.

MOUSE. A (pre-tumour labelled) + B + C + D + E all obtainable in ONE animal, and every instrument that resolves the temporal clause is MOUSE-ONLY: congenic CD45.1/CD45.2 parabiosis (done in tumour-bearing MMTV-PyMT by Dadi 2016), Kaede/photoconvertible photoconversion of the uninvolved organ before tumour induction, inducible Ncr1- or Hobit-driven fate mapping, i.v. anti-CD45 intravascular labelling as vascular-contamination control, and retrogenic/lentiviral clonal barcoding (Flommersfeld 2021 PMID 34437840, single-NK colour barcoding). REQUIRES AN AUTOCHTHONOUS MODEL (MMTV-PyMT, TRAMP, KP lung) — a transplanted flank tumour has no "organ before the tumour" in any meaningful sense.

NHP. Rhesus HSPC barcoding already tracks tissue-versus-blood NK clonally (Wu 2022, PMID 36605190) — correct tool, correct cell type, no tumour; a tumour-bearing macaque is not a practical model.
b.compartment_notes:
THE COMPARTMENT PAIRING AND THE NK ABUNDANCE ARE ANTI-CORRELATED ACROSS HUMAN TUMOUR TYPES, and this is the practical obstacle that sinks the human design. In Liu 2026 the tumours WITH matched uninvolved organ were NSCLC, where NK are explicitly DEPLETED in tumour relative to non-involved lung; the one tumour with real NK infiltration was ovarian (SU-O-005), for which no matched normal ovary was collected because ovarian debulking does not reliably yield tumour-free ipsilateral ovary. So where compartment A exists, compartment B is thin; where B is rich, A is missing. On top of this sits a power problem: mtDNA clone-assignment is only 15-26% in solid tissue versus 20-32% in PBMC, so per-patient NK clone counts are small and a null result at n=5 would not be informative. A re-analysis of GSE302113 is therefore the cheap move but not the decisive one.

MOUSE-ONLY = TRUE IS A JUDGEMENT ON THE CLAIM AS WORDED. The relatedness half (do tumour NK coalesce with organ NK or with blood NK) IS answerable in human surgical material with the architecture that already exists. Only the "present in the organ before the tumour" half is mouse-only. If the registry is willing to reword X1 to drop the temporal clause and ask purely about provenance at one timepoint, mouse_only becomes FALSE and a human design is available — but that reworded claim then overlaps T1 and needs re-scoping against it.

STANDING RISK ON THE MOUSE DESIGN: Dadi's parabiosis window was only 2 weeks (4-8+ weeks is the TRM-field standard) with no i.v.-labelling vascular control, and the lesions were precancerous/early rather than established tumours. Any new X1 experiment must fix all three or it will reproduce the same ambiguity.

o.already_traced_evidence:
NO study in any species has adjudicated X1 with a clonal method. The primitive required is "do these two cells share an ancestor, and how recently" applied to compartment A (NK resident in the uninvolved same organ, pre-tumour) vs compartment B (NK inside the established tumour), with compartment C (blood) as the mandatory discriminator. That test does not exist in the literature.

What DOES exist, and why none of it closes the row:

(1) HUMAN, RIGHT METHOD + RIGHT COMPARTMENTS, NK TEST NEVER RUN. Liu VV et al., Cancer Cell 2026;44(7):1509-1521.e4, PMID 42242233 (preprint doi 10.1101/2025.07.16.665245, PMC12330704; GEO GSE302113). mtscATAC-seq, 218,715 cells, 23 samples, 5 NSCLC patients with matched tumour + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + PBMC, 5 ovarian. This is A + B + C simultaneously from one human with a real clonal barcode - the only such dataset. But the NK-specific adjudication is absent: (a) NK are DEPLETED in tumour vs NILT, verbatim "enrichment of B and plasma cells and depletion of NK cells in the tumor relative to NILT"; (b) the ONLY tumour with substantial NK infiltration is one OVARIAN tumour (SU-O-005) - and the ovarian arm has NO matched uninvolved organ, so compartment A does not exist for the single NK-informative tumour; (c) compartment E is not merely missing but actively collapsed - the paper annotates "4 NK cell/ILC clusters (NCR1)" and its own methods say "GNLY, NCR1 (NK/ILC)", i.e. NK and ILC1 are one label, exactly the fork this registry forbids (T4, P3); (d) no functional sort gate (no GzmB+/IFN-g+ gating), so the "functional" clause is never a sorting criterion; (e) single post-resection timepoint - the organ was never observed before the tumour, so "how recently" cannot be anchored to the pre-tumour state.

CRITICALLY, where Liu 2026 does touch NK it points AGAINST X1, not toward it: in NSCLC donor SU-L-005, 2 of the 14 blood-enriched clones are NK-dominated with cells distributed 66.0% PBMC / 25.3% tumour / 8.8% NILT - blood-to-tissue, the opposite direction; and the cell-type-pair clone-sharing analysis places NK with monocytes/macrophages/DCs in the group whose pattern "suggest[s] that they originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration". Separately, the expanded NK clones in SU-O-005 were "absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response" - a tumour-restricted result with no organ comparator, which is compartment B alone.

(2) TRUE EXOGENOUS BARCODE, NK-SPECIFIC BY DESIGN, NO TUMOUR. Wu C/Dunbar lab, Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525. Autologous rhesus macaque HSPC transplant with high-diversity lentiviral barcodes; tissue NK from liver, spleen, lung, GI vs PB, longitudinal. Explicitly motivated by NK: "we focused on NK cells which do not contain endogenous clonal markers and have not been previously studied in this context." This supplies A-analogue + C + D (the HSPC barcode set IS the deep-coalescence null). Findings: a set of highly expanded PB CD16-CD56- clones also contributing to tissue-resident NK in all tissues, plus tissue-restricted TR NK clones (lung, GI) and liver/spleen-shared sets. This is the healthy-state baseline X1 needs, measured with the exact primitive - but compartment B is absent entirely (no tumour anywhere in the study), so it cannot adjudicate X1.

(3) ORIGIN QUESTION IN A TUMOUR, WRONG INSTRUMENT AND WRONG LINEAGE. Dadi S et al., Cell 2016;164(3):365-377, PMID 26806130 / PMC4733424. CD45.1/CD45.2 congenic parabiosis in MMTV-PyMT mice with pre-transformation enumeration of the same organ. Two disqualifiers for B4: parabiosis is a compartment-exchange assay, NOT a clonal method - it cannot state whether any two cells share an ancestor or how recently, which is the entire primitive; and its resident subject is explicitly non-cNK (the same parabiosis shows non-host chimerism "much lower for ILC1ls... when compared to cNK", and Nfil3-/- leaves ILC1l unperturbed while cNK are "greatly reduced"). Under this registry's ontology that is compartment E contaminating compartment A - the ILC1 fork.

(4) TRUE SINGLE-CELL NK FATE MAPPING, NO TUMOUR. Flommersfeld S et al., Immunity 2021;54(10):2288-2304.e7, PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403; method paper Methods Mol Biol 2022, PMID 35344171. Retrogenic colour barcoding of SINGLE Ly49H+CD27+ NK cells into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- recipients, MCMV. Resolves two pre-existing NK lineages including an ILC1-like splenic-resident one. Setting is infection, not tumour; the authors name the tumour extension as open.

(5) NEAREST BY TOPIC, NO CLONAL METHOD AT ALL. Sci Immunol 2026, PMID 42247486 (snRNA+snATAC of NSCLC intratumoural NK; ITGAE+/ITGA1+ taNK subsets; "trajectory and regulon analyses revealed an inflammation-driven transition") - trajectory inference, no barcode, no organ comparator, no blood discriminator. Sci Transl Med 2026, PMID 42090477 (CD39+CD49a+CD103+ ctrNK) - differentiates ctrNK ex vivo FROM PERIPHERAL NK, i.e. origin-agnostic in vitro.

MOUSE TOOL CAVEAT (stated for honesty): "Ncr1 CreERT2" and "Ncr1-Cre fate mapping" both returned ZERO PubMed hits, and "photoconversion Kaede lymphocyte migration tumor" returned zero. Such mice do exist, so these are degenerate zeros reflecting poor title/abstract indexing of genetic-tool names rather than informative negatives. A mouse inducible NK fate map applied to this question could in principle sit inside a paper titled about something else. I could not surface one through five independent formulations, but this is the one place a hit could hide.
o.nearest_occupant:
TWO occupants, neither of which reaches the claim; they are nearest along different axes.

NEAREST BY ARCHITECTURE (has A+B+C in one human, with a real clonal barcode): Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44(7):1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233. GEO GSE302113.
HOW IT DIFFERS, precisely:
- The NK arm was never run as a lineage test. NK are depleted in tumour vs NILT, so compartment B is near-empty in the arm (NSCLC) that HAS compartment A.
- The one tumour with real NK infiltration (ovarian SU-O-005) has NO matched uninvolved organ. So for the single NK-informative tumour, compartment A does not exist. A and B are never both populated in the same patient for NK.
- Compartment E is collapsed, not merely absent: NK and ILC share one annotation ("4 NK cell/ILC clusters", markers "GNLY, NCR1 (NK/ILC)"). A positive here could not be distinguished from an ILC1 result.
- No functional gating at sort; "functional intratumoural NK" is never a sorting criterion.
- Single post-resection timepoint; no pre-tumour observation of the organ, so the "before the tumour existed" clause of compartment A is unmeasured.
- Its NK-touching results run counter to the claim's direction: blood-enriched NK-dominated clones (SU-L-005) distribute 66.0% PBMC / 25.3% tumour / 8.8% NILT, and NK group with innate cells "originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration".
- Power: clone assignment in tissue is deliberately traded down for fidelity (Mitotrek), n=5 per arm.

NEAREST BY PRIMITIVE (true exogenous clonal barcode, NK-specific by design, has C and D): Wu C et al. "Barcode clonal tracking of tissue-resident immune cells in rhesus macaque highlights distinct clonal distribution pattern of tissue NK cells." Front Immunol 2022. PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525.
HOW IT DIFFERS: compartment B is absent entirely - there is no tumour in the study. It measures tissue NK (liver, spleen, lung, GI) vs blood NK clonal relationships in the HEALTHY transplanted animal. It is therefore the null model X1 requires (it is, to my knowledge, the only dataset that supplies compartment D as a built-in HSPC barcode baseline for NK), not an adjudication of X1. Species is macaque post-transplant, so tissue NK there are marrow-reconstituted by construction - which is itself a confound for reading it as a "pre-existing resident" baseline.

ALSO ADJACENT: Dadi 2016 (PMID 26806130) - parabiosis + pre-tumour enumeration in tumour-bearing mice, but parabiosis is not a clonal method and the subject population is explicitly not cNK. Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) - genuine single-cell NK fate mapping, but infection not tumour.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
G4 APPLIES (the claim invokes residency + differentiation). BOTH neighbouring fields have answered the SAME structural question - "is the functional intratumoural population the pre-existing resident one, or is it replenished from circulation?" - with lineage-grade tools, and NEITHER returns the clean answer X1 asserts. The NK field is the only one of the three that has not run it.

MYELOID - the field where this exact structural question is settled, and settled with fate maps. Loyher PL et al., "Macrophages of distinct origins contribute to tumor development in the lung," J Exp Med 2018;215(10):2536-2553, PMID 30201786 / PMC6170177. Transgenic fluorescent reporters (MacBlue x Cx3cr1-EGFP/+), Ccr2-/-, and parabiosis in mouse lung tumours. Verbatim: "In pulmonary nodules of WT mice, the ratio of ECFP+/EGFP+ cells was 0.57 +/- 0.10, whereas the corresponding ratio was 0.14 +/- 0.08 in Ccr2-/- mice and 0.96 +/- 0.07 in host parabiont mice"; conclusion "the TAM compartment is intermingled by both yolk sac-derived interstitial and monocyte-derived recruited macrophages, differentially represented in the TME depending on the anatomical site of tumor development in the lung." Also Casanova-Acebes M et al., Nature 2021;595:578-584, PMID 34135508 (resident macrophages sit next to tumour cells early, TME later dominated by monocyte-derived cells); Zhu Y et al., Immunity 2017, PMID 28813661. Macaque analogue with true barcodes: PMID 38048388 / PMC10835270, ongoing HSPC production of tissue-resident macrophages. ANSWER THE FIELD RETURNED: never "resident becomes intratumoural" - always BOTH origins contribute, resident-derived dominate early and are progressively displaced by recruited cells, and the split is site-dependent.

T CELL - the field with a somatic clonal barcode (TCR), and it has run the blood-discriminator version of exactly this design. Yost KE et al., "Clonal replacement of tumor-specific T cells following PD-1 blockade," Nat Med 2019, PMID 31359002: the clones that expand in the tumour are largely NOT the pre-existing intratumoural ones but novel clones entering from outside. Wu TD et al., "Peripheral T cell expansion predicts tumour infiltration and clinical response," Nature 2020, PMID 32103181: the intratumoural effector pool is clonally continuous with, and replenished from, the periphery - this is the direct structural analogue of the C-as-discriminator design X1 needs, already executed. Counterweight showing pre-existing tissue populations CAN matter: Malik BT et al., Sci Immunol 2017, PMID 28738020; Enamorado M et al., Nat Commun 2017, PMID 28714465 (resident AND circulating both required); Molodtsov A et al., Immunity 2021, PMID 34525340; Sci Immunol 2023, PMID 37683037 (pre-existing tumour-resident T cells associate with neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 response); Nat Immunol 2026, PMID 42399697 (pregnancy-induced TRM-like cells contribute to breast tumour control). Also relevant to the "functional" clause: bystander TIL (Nature 2018, PMID 29769722) show that being intratumoural and being functional are separable.

ILC - the field that pre-empts compartment E and constrains what a positive X1 could even mean. Nixon BG et al., Sci Immunol 2022;7(70):eabi8642, PMID 35394814: "Cell fate-mapping and transfer studies revealed that granzyme C-expressing innate lymphocytes could be derived from ILC progenitors and did not interconvert with NK cells, ILC2s, or ILC3s" - OBS_GENETIC evidence for two independent origins for the CD49a+ intratumoural type-1 population. Flommersfeld 2021 (PMID 34437840) names the selection-vs-conversion alternative for tumours explicitly and demonstrates it with single-cell fate mapping. Blood Adv 2024, PMID 38484189, separates human NK from noncytotoxic ILCs by clonal analysis. Hepatic ILC1 wave/fate-mapping work: PMID 36054340, 35348580, 37352115.

NET: the instrument exists, the design is standard, and two adjacent fields have executed it. The NK version is unoccupied - and in both fields that did run it, the pre-existing-resident-becomes-the-functional-intratumoural-cell reading was the one that failed or had to be qualified.

b.why:
Three independent reasons, any one of which is sufficient.

(1) THE TERMINAL NODE IS A FUNCTION, NOT A POPULATION. "Tumour NK -> pro-angiogenic phenotype" is the canonical "A becomes functionally B-like" form. The load-bearing content is VEGF secretion / angiogenesis promotion. Clonal barcoding reports shared ancestry and its recency and nothing else; it cannot report whether a cell secretes VEGF or remodels vessels. The functional half of the claim is outside the primitive's range entirely.

(2) "DECIDUAL-LIKE" IS AN ANALOGY, NOT AN ANCESTRY ASSERTION, AND THE TWO NAMED COMPARTMENTS CANNOT BE CLONALLY COMPARED EVEN IN PRINCIPLE. dNK and tumour NK reside in different tissues and, in essentially every realisable case, different individuals. Clonal relatedness between cells from two different humans is not merely unmeasured, it is undefined: somatic mtDNA variants sit on individual-private germline haplotypes, and lentiviral barcodes are per-recipient. Asking "do these share a recent ancestor" across donors has no answer the primitive can return. The claim's headline comparison therefore poses no lineage question at all — Phase A's INF_MARKER grading is exactly right about the epistemic move being made (CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ resemblance), and marker resemblance is not an ancestry relation.

(3) THE ONLY WELL-FORMED RESIDUAL QUESTION IS A REVERSIBLE-STATE QUESTION. Reformulated intra-patient — "are intratumoural CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ NK the progeny of the same recent ancestors as that patient's circulating CD56dim NK, or a clonally distinct compartment?" — this has the decidable same/different-lineage shape. But CD56bright/CD16-/VEGF+ is an inducible, non-heritable cell state, so both answers are consistent with the same clonal structure:
  - SHARED CLONES is consistent with (a) in-situ conversion of infiltrating cNK, and equally with (b) recruitment of a pre-existing CD56bright subset that of course shares ancestry with CD56dim, since all NK in one person converge on a common HSC/NK-progenitor pool and the "how recently" cut-off is set by the analyst, not by the biology.
  - NO SHARED CLONES is consistent with (a) a genuinely separate tissue-resident/ILC-like origin, and equally with (b) sparse clone capture — the expected null when clone sizes are small (see Wang et al., Genome Biol 2025, PMID 40134031: clonal expansion dictates the efficacy of mtDNA lineage tracing).
Because the state is reversible and not transmitted through the clonal record, the barcode partition is invariant to which hypothesis is true. Empirically this is already visible: PMID 42242233 (Cancer Cell 2026) recovered BOTH patterns for NK in the same study — expanded NK clones shared with blood/non-involved tissue in some patients, and tumour-restricted NK clones absent from matched blood in another — without that bit resolving any state-transition question.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = intratumoural pro-angiogenic NK share recent clones with matched peripheral blood NK (blood-derived infiltrators).

Very next experiment: an induction/perturbation assay. Take autologous peripheral blood NK, expose to tumour-conditioned medium and to candidate TME drivers individually (TGF-beta, hypoxia/HIF, adenosine, PGE2, IL-15 withdrawal), read out acquisition of CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ and angiogenic output (HUVEC tube formation / aortic ring). Then block the winning driver in vivo and ask whether intratumoural VEGF+ NK frequency and microvessel density fall.

Note this is precisely the experiment already performed without any lineage input: PMID 32655841 (renal cell tumours convert NK to a pro-angiogenic phenotype) and PMID 30597092 (glycodelin-A converts blood CD16- CD56bright NK to a dNK-like phenotype) both ran the conversion assay directly.
b.action_if_no:
NO = no shared clones between intratumoural pro-angiogenic NK and matched blood NK.

Very next experiment: first, a methods response, not a biological one — sequence more cells, more timepoints, and deeper mtDNA coverage to exclude the sampling-failure explanation, because a negative is the expected artefact under sparse clone capture. Only after that survives do you go looking for the alternative source (adjacent normal tissue NK, bone marrow NK progenitors, tissue-resident ILC1) — and having found a candidate source, the next step is again an induction/perturbation assay: expose that source population to TME signals and ask what drives the VEGF+ CD56bright state, then block it.

The biologically informative move in this branch is therefore the same assay as the YES branch, reached one step later and after a round of "sample deeper".
b.both_answers_reason:
FAILS, and this is the decisive filter for X3. Both branches converge on the identical next experiment: a TME-signal induction/blockade assay asking which soluble driver produces the CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ state and whether blocking it reduces tumour angiogenesis. The lineage answer changes neither the reagents, the readout, nor the therapeutic hypothesis.

Branch-by-branch:
- YES is vacuous-confirmatory. It tells you tumour NK came from the blood, which is the field's default assumption and which nobody's next experiment is waiting on. You then run the conversion assay — the assay already run in PMID 32655841 and PMID 30597092 with no lineage data at all.
- NO is not merely non-actionable but under-determined. Its immediate consequence is "sequence more cells", a methods action, because absence of shared barcodes is the expected null under sparse sampling. It cannot distinguish a real separate origin from a detection failure without an orthogonal argument, at which point the orthogonal argument is doing the work, not the lineage.

Strongest disconfirming precedent: PMID 42242233 (Liu, Sandor, Lareau, Satpathy; Cancer Cell 2026; also PMC13309241 / bioRxiv 2025.07.16.665245) ran exactly this design at scale — mtscATAC-seq, 218,715 cells, matched tumour + non-involved lung tissue + peripheral blood in NSCLC and matched tumour + blood in ovarian cancer, with NK cells included. For myeloid cells the clonal answer was YES (TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating monocytes) and the paper's actual payload came from the EPIGENETIC profiles of the precursor monocytes (DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones), not from the yes/no relatedness bit. For NK the study recovered both patterns across patients. That is the signature of a lineage answer that does not gate the next step: the informative layer was a different assay riding along on the same cells.

RULE G4 check reinforces this. The same structural question — "are the tumour-infiltrating cells locally converted or peripherally supplied?" — was already settled in the adaptive field by TCR clonotype, where the barcode is intrinsic and free (Yost et al., Nat Med 2019, PMID 31359002, clonal replacement after PD-1 blockade; Wu et al., Nature 2020, PMID 32103181, peripheral expansion predicts infiltration), and in the myeloid field by PMID 42242233. In neither case did the shared/not-shared bit by itself redirect the programme; the redirection came from state profiling layered on top. X3 would be importing a question whose occupancy already lives in the fields it borrowed the mechanism from, and importing it in its least decidable form.

Verdict: OUT.
b.compartments_needed:
For the claim AS WRITTEN, two compartments simultaneously:
  A = decidual NK (CD56bright CD16-) from decidua basalis/parietalis — first-trimester decidua at elective termination, or term decidua/placental bed at delivery.
  B = tumour-infiltrating NK from a solid tumour — surgical resection or core biopsy.

For the reformulated intra-patient version, up to five:
  B = tumour-infiltrating NK (surgery/biopsy)
  C = matched peripheral blood NK (venepuncture)
  D = adjacent non-involved tissue NK (same surgical specimen)
  E = bone marrow NK progenitors (separate aspirate)
  and, to anchor the "decidual-like" comparison at all, A again as an unpaired cross-donor reference.
b.compartments_obtainable:
NO for the pair the claim actually names (A + B); YES for the reformulated intra-patient set (B + C + D).

A + B paired from one human: not obtainable in practice. Decidua is available ONLY during pregnancy — first-trimester termination or term delivery. Tumour is available only at surgery or biopsy. Pairing them requires a pregnant cancer patient undergoing tumour resection and decidual sampling in the same window; such cases exist as isolated reports but cannot be assembled into a cohort, and the co-occurrence is itself confounded (pregnancy-associated malignancy is not typical tumour biology).

More fundamentally, the fallback of comparing A from donor 1 against B from patient 2 is not a lineage comparison at all. Shared ancestry between cells from different individuals is undefined for both mtDNA variants (individual-private germline haplotype background) and lentiviral barcodes (per-recipient). Unpaired dNK-vs-tumour-NK sampling can only ever regenerate the marker resemblance Phase A already logged as INF_MARKER — it cannot upgrade it to a lineage statement.

B + C + D paired from one human: routinely obtainable, and already done. This is exactly the NSCLC design in PMID 42242233 (tumour resection + non-involved lung + PBMC from the same patient). Adding E requires a separate marrow aspirate — obtainable but an extra invasive procedure, rarely consented alongside tumour surgery. Archived/frozen material is now tractable via cryo-mtscATAC-seq (PMID 41000852), which relaxes the fresh-tissue constraint but does nothing about the A+B pairing problem.
b.compartment_notes:
Post-mortem: not required for any compartment here.
Surgery-only: tumour NK (B) and adjacent normal NK (D) are surgery/biopsy-restricted.
Pregnancy-only: decidual NK (A) is strictly pregnancy-restricted — first-trimester termination or delivery. This is the binding constraint on the claim as written.
Mouse-only: only the literal decidua-plus-tumour pairing is mouse-restricted. A tumour-bearing pregnant mouse is constructible, and the fate-mapping toolkit exists (T-bet fate mapping of decidual NK, PMID 41782473; plus Ncr1-CreER, Confetti, Polylox, CRISPR recorders). But mouse uterine NK are DBA-lectin+ trophoblast-remodelling cells that differ substantially from human dNK, so the model would not test the human resemblance the claim asserts — it would substitute a different comparison and call it the same one.

Overall mouse_only = FALSE because the only tractable version of the question (tumour vs adjacent tissue vs blood NK within one patient) is fully human-obtainable and has already been executed in humans. The mouse would be needed only for the version that is not decidable anyway (B1), so mouse access does not rescue the claim.

Secondary note bearing on B3: even where compartments are obtainable, the CD56bright CD16- VEGF+ population in tumours is typically a small minority of a small infiltrate, so clone-capture depth is marginal — which is what makes the NO branch of B2 uninterpretable rather than informative.

o.already_traced_evidence:
FALSE for the claim AS WRITTEN — but the reformulated intra-patient version is now heavily encroached, and the shortlist must not treat X3 as virgin territory.

WHAT IS NOT DONE: nobody has ever placed decidual NK and tumour NK in the same clonal frame. Zero hits across PubMed and fielded Europe PMC for decidua/decidual crossed with clonal, barcode, mtDNA, or lineage tracing in NK. Two independent confirmations: (a) database silence; (b) an explicit self-declared gap by the field's leading NK-barcoding group — Wu et al., Front Immunol 2022 (PMID 36605190, archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X3B4_PMC9808525.txt) write in their discussion, verbatim: "It will be of particular interest to investigate clonality and relationship in decidual NK cells, a uniquely functional NK population that we have not yet investigated at a clonal level."

THE DECIDUAL-LIKE TUMOUR NK LITERATURE CONTAINS NO LINEAGE METHOD AT ALL. I ran a keyword census over the archived X3 primary sources and read methods on the two most in-vivo-looking candidates:
- Bruno 2013 Neoplasia (PMID 23441128, PMC3579316) and Keskin 2007 PNAS (PMID 17360654, PMC1805591): phenotype + in vitro TGF-beta conversion only; zero clonal/barcode/mtDNA/fate-map terms.
- Post-autoHSCT "decidual-like NK" pair, the closest thing to an in vivo natural reconstitution experiment: iScience 2022 (PMID 36262311, PMC9574507) and Commun Med 2025 (PMID 40437214, PMC12120011). I read both methods sections. Flow cytometry, plasma cytokines, scRNA-seq, in vitro only. The only occurrences of "clonal"/"clone"/"barcod" in either paper are "monoclonal antibody", "cell isolation", and NEBNext library barcoding. No clonal adjudication, despite autoHSCT being a setting where it was feasible.
- Remainder of the phenotypic corpus, all non-lineage: PMID 29763380 (colorectal, angiogenin/MMP9-TIMP2), 29713652 (malignant pleural effusion), 32655841 (renal cell), 34638439 (TIMP1/2), 34469729 (HGSOC), 33277305 (Cancer Discov commentary), 41916960 (PDAC galunisertib 2026), 32983113 (Hawke 2020, VEGF-A independent of ILC1-like conversion).

WHY THIS IS FALSE AND NOT NOT_SEARCHED: ~45 distinct queries across PubMed and Europe PMC (including fielded TITLE_ABS queries), plus 2 WebSearches, plus methods/full-text reads of 5 candidate occupants. The searches converged cleanly and non-ambiguously: every "decidual-like NK" paper is phenotypic, and every NK clonal-tracing paper lacks a decidua. The mandated tool searches (mtscATAC, MAESTER, single-cell mitochondrial, lentiviral barcoding, fate mapping, confetti, Polylox, CRISPR recorder) returned no NK-plus-decidua work of any kind.

HONESTY CAVEAT: the published Cancer Cell full text of the nearest occupant 403'd on fetch, so my NK-specific reading of Liu et al. rests on the bioRxiv full text (PMC12330704) plus the published abstract (PMID 42242233). If peer review added a decidual-signature analysis to the NK section I would have missed it — unlikely, since the published abstract is myeloid-focused and the preprint has zero decidua mentions, but recorded.
o.nearest_occupant:
PRIMARY OCCUPANT — Liu V, Sandor K, Yan PK, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44(7):1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233. Preprint: bioRxiv 2025.07.16.665245, PMID 40777278, PMC12330704 (full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/D3_PMC12330704.txt; Phase A already pulled the abstract as /home/user/aaa/refs/X3_42242233.txt).

WHAT IT DID — it is the same primitive in the same compartment set:
- Somatic mtDNA mutations via mtscATAC-seq, with a "Mitotrek" clonal-assignment framework that prioritises fidelity of clone calls over detection sensitivity. This is exactly "do these two cells share an ancestor".
- 218,715 cells: 124,958 from matched tumour + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + peripheral blood in early-stage NSCLC; 93,757 from matched tumour + peripheral blood in ovarian cancer. That is compartments B (tumour NK), C (matched blood NK) and D (adjacent non-involved tissue NK) of the reformulated X3 design, paired within patient.
- NK are annotated, not discarded: 4 NK/ILC clusters (NCR1+) in the NSCLC atlas, 3 in the ovarian atlas.
- It answers the tumour-NK-vs-blood-NK clonal question, and answers it in both directions in different patients: in ovarian tumour SU-O-005 (the one tumour with substantial NK infiltration) NK showed oligoclonal architecture resembling adaptive lymphocytes and the expanded NK clones were ABSENT from matched peripheral blood — "indicating a tumor-restricted NK response"; whereas in NSCLC donor SU-L-005, 2 of 14 blood-enriched clones were NK-dominated with 25.3% of clone cells recovered in tumour and 8.8% in NILT, i.e. blood NK clones demonstrably infiltrate tissue. Cross-cell-type clone sharing placed NK with monocytes/macrophages/DCs at high sharing, read as recent haematopoietic output without a substantial clonal bottleneck prior to tissue infiltration.

HOW IT DIFFERS FROM X3 — three decisive gaps:
1. NO DECIDUAL COMPARTMENT. "decidu" appears zero times in the full text. Compartment A is entirely absent, so the "decidual-like" half of the claim is untouched by any clonal frame anywhere in the literature.
2. NO PHENOTYPE GATE ON THE dNK-LIKE / PRO-ANGIOGENIC STATE. CD9, CD49a, CD103 and a VEGF-A/pro-angiogenic NK signature are never used to partition NK clones; the single "angiogen" mention refers to tumour endothelium, not NK. So it does not test whether decidual-like tumour NK form a distinct clonal group or are scattered across clones shared with conventional NK — which is the actual discriminating measurement X3 needs.
3. SEVERELY UNDERPOWERED FOR NK. Verbatim: "NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors." The tumour-NK clonal result rests on ONE ovarian tumour plus one lung donor. NK is a secondary observation; the headline and the published Cancer Cell abstract are myeloid (monocyte -> macrophage/DC3).

SECOND-NEAREST — Wu C. et al. (Dunbar group). "Barcode clonal tracking of tissue-resident immune cells in rhesus macaque highlights distinct clonal distribution pattern of tissue NK cells." Front Immunol 2022;13:994498. PMID 36605190, PMC9808525. Lentiviral barcoding of autologous HSPCs, then clonal tracking of tissue-resident NK (liver, spleen, lung) against peripheral blood. Incidentally the closest pre-Liu tumour result: in one macaque bearing a localized liver tumour they sorted NK separately from the tumour region and from both normal liver lobes and found the clonal pattern of each NK subset similar across samples, concluding clonal expansion in liver is homogeneous across the tissue even in the presence of a localized tumour. Differs from X3: macaque not human, n=1 tumour, incidental liver tumour rather than a phenotype-defined pro-angiogenic NK question, no decidua, and no dNK-like gate. Also the source of the explicit "not yet investigated at a clonal level" statement about dNK.

THIRD — Mohamed MA, Li Y, ... Stanic AK. "T-bet Fate Mapping Reveals Gestational Stage-Specific Transcriptional Adaptation of Decidual NK Cells." Am J Reprod Immunol 2026;95(3):e70220. PMID 41782473, PMC12961421 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/X3B4_PMC12961421.txt). Rosa26-RFP x Tbx21-Cre mouse, flow + bulk RNA-seq of fate-mapped RFP+ cells + scRNA-seq of uterus/decidua/placenta across gestation; concludes dNK adapt by transcriptional compensation rather than lineage diversion. This is the only lineage tool ever pointed at dNK — but it is MARKER-HISTORY, not clonal: it records whether a cell ever expressed T-bet, and cannot say whether any two cells share an ancestor. Mouse-only, decidua-only, no tumour arm. It therefore does not touch X3's structure.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HIGH — and this is the most important finding for X3. The claim invokes a general process (plasticity/differentiation: an infiltrating cytotoxic cell acquiring a tissue-imprinted trophic state), and per G4 the borrowed mechanism's occupancy lives in the fields it was borrowed from. Both neighbouring fields have already run this exact structural experiment with lineage tools.

MYELOID — answered with the IDENTICAL primitive in the IDENTICAL compartment set, in the very same paper that is X3's nearest occupant. Liu et al. (PMID 42242233 / 40777278) showed by mtDNA clonal tracing that TME-resident macrophages and type 3 DCs are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and further resolved DC-biased versus macrophage-biased clones whose circulating monocyte precursors already carry distinct epigenetic profiles — concluding intratumoural myeloid differentiation fate "may be peripherally programmed before TME infiltration." That is precisely the recruited-and-converted-in-situ versus pre-committed-subset-selected dichotomy X3 poses, adjudicated clonally, and it landed on the pre-programmed answer. The structural template, the analysis, and even the tissue set are already published.

T CELL — answered with TCR as the natural barcode, years earlier. Yost et al., Nat Med 2019, PMID 31359002: clonal replacement — intratumoural exhausted clones are largely not the ones that expand after PD-1 blockade; the responding clones arrive from outside the tumour. And the tightest analogue of X3's conversion claim: Nat Commun 2021, PMID 33602930, "Common clonal origin of conventional T cells and induced regulatory T cells in breast cancer patients" — TCR sharing establishes intratumoural conversion of conventional T cells into a suppressive Treg state, i.e. the adaptive-immune version of "cytotoxic effector becomes tissue-trophic/suppressive inside a tumour". Foreshadowed by PLoS One 2010, PMID 21049016, intratumoural convergence of effector and Foxp3+ CD4 TCR repertoires.

ILC — ILC3-to-ILC1 conversion has been adjudicated by fate mapping (Mucosal Immunol 2021, PMID 33214656), with c-Maf restraint of the type 1 program mapped in J Exp Med 2020, PMID 31570496.

NET: the myeloid and T-cell fields have both already answered X3's structural question with lineage tools, and myeloid answered it with the same mtDNA primitive, the same tumour/adjacent-tissue/blood compartment triad, and the same patients. What remains genuinely unoccupied is narrow and specific: (i) no decidual compartment has ever entered a clonal frame with NK, from anyone, and (ii) no clonal study has ever gated NK on the decidual-like/pro-angiogenic phenotype. X3's unoccupied residue is the decidual anchor and the phenotype gate — not the tumour-versus-blood NK clonal comparison, which is now taken.

b.why:
TRUE, but only narrowly, and only for a weaker proposition than the claim asserts.

WHAT IS DECIDABLE. The claim's testable core reduces to the rubric's second decidable form, "A and B are the same/different lineage": do intratumoural NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 cells in one NSCLC tumour draw from the same clones, or from clonally disjoint pools? That is a pure clonal-structure question and the primitive answers it directly. It is also live rather than academic, because the paper contradicts itself on exactly this point: the published version's cross-modality section concludes the taNK branches "represent distinct lineages that converge transcriptionally, while retaining their ancestral chromatin marks," while the abstract asserts "an inflammation-driven transition from early GZMK+ NK cells toward an ENTPD1+ effector state." Clonal sharing versus disjointness adjudicates between those two sentences.

WHY THE REVERSIBLE-STATE CARVE-OUT DOES NOT FULLY VOID IT. The carve-out applies to a reversible state *within one lineage*. Here the leading alternative is not a state-flicker model but a two-population model with a genuinely different clonal signature: NK3_GZMK as recently immigrated circulating CD56bright NK (GZMK marks CD56bright, Bratke 2005 PMID 16106370), NK3_ENTPD1 as a pre-existing locally imprinted CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ lung trNK pool that expands in tumour (Brownlie 2021 PMID 33836578). One-lineage versus two-lineage is not a within-lineage state question, so the arrow is refutable.

WHY IT IS ONLY HALF DECIDABLE — the part that matters for B2. The primitive returns shared ancestry and its recency; it never returns the STATE of the ancestral node. So it cannot order the arrow. Shared clonotypes are produced identically by (a) GZMK+ -> ENTPD1+, (b) ENTPD1+ -> GZMK+, (c) a common precursor branching into both, and (d) one clone reversibly flickering through an inducible endpoint — and (d) is not hypothetical here, since ENTPD1/CD39 is an activation-inducible ectoenzyme that the authors themselves induce on healthy-donor blood NK in six days with IL-15+TGF-beta, and the ISG-high program (IFIT3, IFI44, ISG15) is an hours-scale reversible interferon response layered on any NK cell. Direction cannot be recovered from tip states without an assumed root, which is precisely the defect Phase A found in the original analysis (Monocle3 start "defined as the terminal branch within the NK3_GZMK population"; destiny root "selected from the NK3_GZMK cluster").

NET: the claim is REFUTABLE by clonal structure but not CONFIRMABLE by it. Recorded TRUE because a disjoint-clone result would kill the arrow outright; the asymmetry is carried into B2, where it is fatal.
b.action_if_yes:
IF YES — NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 nuclei from the same resection share mtDNA clonotypes above a matched-donor permutation null.

Very next experiment: prospectively sort intratumoural GZMK+ CD39- CD103- NK3 cells from a fresh treatment-naive NSCLC resection and place them into autologous tumour-fragment or autologous tumour-organoid culture for 4-7 days, ± IFN-I and ± TGF-beta, reading out CD39 / CD103 / CD49a / ISG acquisition per retained mtDNA clonotype so that genuine conversion is separated from selective outgrowth of a pre-committed minority (IL-15 and IL-2 drive proliferation, so bulk frequency shifts do not distinguish the two).

This is a real experiment. It is also the branch that fails the filter, for three reasons developed in both_answers_reason: the YES outcome is the near-certain null expectation rather than a discriminating result; it does not separate the claim from the reverse arrow, the branching-precursor model, or reversible flickering; and the follow-up experiment named above is one the field would run regardless of any lineage result — Serger's group has already built essentially this platform (healthy-donor blood NK + IL-15 + TGF-beta + irradiated A549, 6 days).
b.action_if_no:
IF NO — the two states occupy disjoint clonotype sets, with demonstrated power to have detected sharing had it existed.

Very next experiment: a compartment-of-origin assignment on the same patients. Using the paired material already required for the primary test, ask which reference compartment each intratumoural state shares clonotypes with — matched peripheral blood NK (tests the recent-immigrant CD56bright model for NK3_GZMK) versus matched adjacent non-tumour lung NK (tests the Brownlie 2021 pre-existing CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ lung trNK model for NK3_ENTPD1) — with matched intratumoural CD8 T cells run in the same assay as the mandatory artefact control, since NK3_ENTPD1 carries a CD8-Trm program (CD3E, IL32, CTLA4, CXCL13, LAYN) and the original sort was CD56+CD3+ with T cells removed only by a UCell CD3D/CD3G > 0.05 transcriptomic threshold. If ENTPD1+ "NK" clonotypes match the CD8 T clonotype pool, the endpoint cluster is doublets or ambient signal, not an NK state at all.

This branch is genuinely actionable and consequential. It overturns the published abstract's arrow, it removes the concrete instance that claims X1 and X2 in this screen lean on, and it flips the therapeutic model: a fixed pre-seeded CD39+ pool means anti-NKG2A "emergence" is expansion with a hard ceiling rather than induction, which is a different prediction from the one the manufacturing and NKG2A-blockade framing assumes.
b.both_answers_reason:
FALSE — the NO branch is strong, the YES branch is vacuous, and B2 requires both. X4 is OUT.

The YES branch fails on three independent grounds.

(1) NEAR-CERTAIN OUTCOME, SO NEARLY NO INFORMATION. Intratumoural NK descend from a limited seeding pool and proliferate locally. Some clonal sharing between any two NK states in the same tumour is the null expectation under every model on the table — including the two-population model, if both populations derive from the same expanded blood clone. A result you can predict before running it does not select a next step.

(2) NON-DIAGNOSTIC AGAINST THE LIVE ALTERNATIVES. This is the reversible-state problem from B1 landing exactly where the rubric says it lands. Shared clonotypes are equally consistent with GZMK+ -> ENTPD1+, with the reverse arrow, with a common precursor branching into both, and with a single clone reversibly occupying and vacating an inducible CD39/ISG activation state. The primitive gives ancestry and recency but never the state of the ancestral node, so it cannot order these. A YES therefore leaves the claim exactly as uncertain as Phase A found it.

(3) NON-SELECTING FOLLOW-UP. The experiment named in action_if_yes — sorted intratumoural GZMK+ NK into autologous tumour culture, scoring CD39/CD103/ISG acquisition — requires no lineage input, is the standing next step for this biology irrespective of clonal structure, and is a variant of the platform the authors have already built. The lineage result did not choose it. That is "we would conclude the transition is possible and move on."

A further asymmetry compounds this, and it cuts against the branch that WAS actionable. The NO branch is hard to obtain cleanly. mtDNA lineage tracing is only reliable under stringent clonal expansion (PMID 40134031: under weak expansion, subpopulation-specific variants have "limited discriminatory power among different genuine lineages"), and NK cells lack a rearranged antigen receptor to drive it — the one human-NK mtDNA clonal study that succeeded did so in HCMV-driven adaptive NKG2C+ NK, the single stringently expanded NK population (Rückert 2022, PMID 36289449). Combined with the per-donor intratumoural NK yields in this repo's own power table (281-509 NK per NSCLC tumour, zero in 3 of 8 tumour libraries, before subsetting to NK3 and then to two subclusters), a NO result is at material risk of being a power artefact. So the screen faces a likely-uninformative YES and a NO that needs a demonstrated positive control before it can be believed.

Recorded FALSE without hesitation. This is the expected outcome of the filter, not a defect in the claim's biology.
b.compartments_needed:
Five compartments, all needed SIMULTANEOUSLY and ideally from the same individual:

1. Intratumoural NK3_GZMK — CD56bright-like, GZMK+ CD44+ CXCR4+, CD39- CD103-, from NSCLC tumour digest. (Compartment A.)
2. Intratumoural NK3_ENTPD1 — CD39+ CD103+ CD49a+ ISG-high, from the SAME tumour digest, same library. (Compartment B.) A and B must come from one digest or the primary comparison is confounded by donor.
3. Matched adjacent non-tumour lung NK — required to test the Brownlie 2021 (PMID 33836578) alternative that the ENTPD1+ state is a pre-existing lung-resident adaptive-like CD49a+CD103+NKG2C+ pool expanded in tumour rather than a locally converted product.
4. Matched peripheral blood NK, same draw — required to test the recent-immigrant CD56bright model for NK3_GZMK and to supply the non-expanded clonotype baseline against which "shared" is defined.
5. Matched intratumoural CD8 T cells — a mandatory artefact control, not optional. NK3_ENTPD1 carries CD3E, IL32, CTLA4, CXCL13 and LAYN; the original sort gate was CD45+CD19-CD14-CD56+CD3+ with T cells removed only by a UCell CD3D/CD3G > 0.05 transcriptomic threshold, so residual CD3-dim T cells and T-NK doublet nuclei would manufacture exactly the observed endpoint and exactly the observed gradient toward it.

NOT required, and not obtainable in the same patient anyway: bone marrow HSPC to root the tree. Excluded from the design rather than treated as a gap.
b.compartments_obtainable:
TRUE — and this is the one gate X4 passes cleanly. All five compartments are obtainable paired from ONE human at ONE operation. NSCLC resection routinely yields tumour, tumour-adjacent non-tumour lung, and a same-day peripheral blood draw; CD8 T cells come from the same tumour digest.

Verified against material already in this repository rather than asserted. GSE302113 ("Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer," mtscATAC-seq, 38 libraries, /home/user/aaa/out/T3_datasets.tsv) contains five NSCLC donors (SU-L-001 through SU-L-005) each with tumour, adjacent_normal AND blood libraries from the same donor, all clearing the preregistered 20x chrM floor (median coverage 23.8-158.9x, 38/38 libraries) — see /home/user/aaa/out/T4_power.tsv.

NOT post-mortem-only. NOT surgery-plus-transplant-only. NOT pregnancy-restricted. NOT mouse-only. Access is genuinely unconstrained; the constraints are timing, yield and readout, recorded in compartment_notes.
b.compartment_notes:
Four caveats, none of which block access but two of which bear directly on B2.

SINGLE TIMEPOINT, SURGERY-ONLY, NOT RE-SAMPLEABLE. The tumour compartment exists only at resection, in treatment-naive resectable (largely stage I-II) NSCLC, and that tumour cannot be sampled again. There is therefore NO temporal axis available in the compartment where the claim lives. This is the structural reason the YES branch in B2 cannot be rescued by a follow-up timepoint.

YIELD, NOT ACCESS, IS BINDING — and it threatens the NO branch specifically. Per-donor intratumoural NK in GSE302113 runs 281-509 cells, with zero recovered in 3 of 8 tumour libraries. NK3 is one of three NK subcompartments and NK3_GZMK / NK3_ENTPD1 are subclusters within it, so realistic yield is tens of cells per state per donor. Against PMID 40134031 (mtDNA lineage tracing is only reliable under stringent clonal expansion) and the fact that NK lack an antigen receptor to drive such expansion — the sole demonstrated exception being HCMV-driven adaptive NKG2C+ NK in Rückert 2022, PMID 36289449, the one successful human-NK mtDNA clonal study — a disjoint-clonotype result could easily be low power rather than distinct lineage. Prospective CD45+CD3-CD56+ enrichment plus a same-donor positive control (recovering known clonal sharing in matched adaptive NKG2C+ NK) would be prerequisites before any NO is read as biology.

READOUT MISMATCH. The barcode and the state must be read in the same cell. mtscATAC-seq supplies the mtDNA clonotype but assigns GZMK and ISG-high states only through gene-activity scores — the same weak inference Phase A criticised. MAESTER-style mtDNA enrichment from scRNA, or 10x multiome with chrM retention, is required so that state assignment is RNA-level while the clonotype is genotype-level.

THE DIRECTION-FIXING TOOL AND THE COMPARTMENT ARE IN DIFFERENT SPECIES. Kaede photoconversion, parabiosis, Polylox and inducible fate maps — the methods that supply an experimental timestamp and would fix the arrow — are mouse-only, and the myeloid field has already used them to answer this exact structural question (Lee et al., PMID 40523200: root certified by an independent time-stamp, direction left free, answer = two independently seeded ontogenies, not one lineage). But the endpoint state here is human tumour-restricted, absent from 50 non-tumour lung donors and from blood, with no validated mouse NK3_GZMK / NK3_ENTPD1 counterpart, so the question cannot be relocated to the species where the tool exists. The one human timestamp that does exist — donor/recipient chimerism in lung transplant, used by Serger's own co-author group (Falk, doi 10.1101/2023.06.16.543190) — lives in the transplanted allograft, a different compartment from an NSCLC tumour.

o.already_traced_evidence:
No one has adjudicated "intratumoural NK3_GZMK is the clonal ancestor of intratumoural NK3_ENTPD1" with any clonal/lineage primitive. Three independent lines confirm this.

(1) THE CLAIM'S OWN SOURCE PAPER USED NO CLONAL METHOD. Serger C, Rebuffet L, ... Vivier E, Zippelius A. "Cytotoxic CD39+ tumor-associated NK cells respond to NKG2A blockade in lung cancer." Sci Immunol 2026;11(120):eaeb6645. PMID 42247486 (preprint bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.08.26.672316). Abstract: "Trajectory and regulon analyses revealed an inflammation-driven transition from early granzyme K (GZMK)+ NK cells toward an ENTPD1+ (CD39+) effector state." I could not open the Sci Immunol or bioRxiv full text (403), so I inspected the authors' own analysis repository instead (github.com/cserger/Lung_Tumor_NK, mirrored at github.com/RebuffetLucas/Lung_Tumor_NK). Its directories are 01_QC, 02_GlobalHeterogeneity, 07_MultiVelocity_NK3, 08_SCENICplus_Analysis_NK3, 10_DiffusionMap, 11_MultiVelocity_NK3_Full_Reprocessed, 12_Trajectory_Characterization. There is NO mgatk, no mtDNA/mtscATAC, no clonal, no barcode, no TCR code anywhere in the repo. The A->B assertion rests entirely on multi-velocity + SCENIC+ regulons + diffusion-map pseudotime on snRNA/snATAC. It has never been tested against a clonal structure.

(2) THE ONE PAPER THAT COULD HAVE DONE IT, DIDN'T — see nearest_occupant (Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233). Same method, same disease, same four compartments, but NK resolved only as 3-4 "NK/ILC" clusters and NSCLC tumours had too few NK cells.

(3) THE ONLY HUMAN NK mtDNA SUBSET STUDY IS BLOOD-ONLY AND REPORTS A NEGATIVE FOR EXACTLY THE COMPARTMENT X4 NEEDS. Rückert T, Lareau CA, Mashreghi M-F, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022;23:1551-1563. PMID 36289449 / PMC9663309. ASAP-seq + CITE-seq + mgatk mtDNA clonotypes on sorted human peripheral blood NK across CD56bright (explicitly the GZMK+/XCL1+/IL7R+ cluster — the blood counterpart of NK3_GZMK), early CD56dim, mature CD56dim and adaptive NKG2C+ clusters; 7 donors, longitudinal to 19 months. Verbatim, from the archived full text: clonotypes "were significantly associated not only with adaptive NK cells as a whole but also with specific subclusters"; but "such an association was absent in the conventional NK cell compartment ..., suggesting that mitochondrial mutations of conventional NK cells do not flag clonal expansions but might instead be present already on the progenitor level." So the mtDNA primitive has been run over human GZMK+ CD56bright NK versus effector NK states and returned no clone-to-state structure in the non-adaptive compartment. That is a null on a neighbouring question, not an adjudication of X4 — but it is the single most load-bearing prior for whether X4 is even resolvable.

RESIDUAL GAP I AM FLAGGING RATHER THAN GLOSSING: I verified the absence of a clonal method in PMID 42247486 from its abstract, its MeSH terms, and its public code repository — not from its supplementary methods, which I could not open. If a supplementary mtDNA/mgatk pass exists that is absent from the authors' own analysis repo, this record would flip. I judge that unlikely but it is not zero.
o.nearest_occupant:
Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44(7):1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233; preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704 (full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X4_PMC12330704.txt).

WHAT THEY DID: mtscATAC-seq (joint scATAC + mtDNA genotyping) with a new clone-caller, Mitotrek, that "prioritizes fidelity of clonal assignments over detection sensitivity." 218,715 cells. NSCLC cohort: patient-matched lung tumour + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + PBMC from 5 patients. Ovarian cohort: primary tumour + matched PBMC, 5 patients (3 with blood). This is X4's compartments 1, 2, 3 and 4, paired from one human, in the same disease, with the exact primitive X4 proposes. It is the closest a paper can get without being the paper.

HOW IT DIFFERS — four ways, each disqualifying:

(a) NK SUBSET RESOLUTION IS ABSENT. Verbatim: "4 NK cell/ILC clusters (NCR1)" in the joint object and "3 NK/ILC clusters (NCR1)" in the tumour-only reclustering; annotation markers for the T/NK compartment were "CD3D (broad T), CD8A (CD8+ T), CD4 (CD4+ T), GNLY, NCR1 (NK/ILC), FOXP3 (Treg)." GZMK, ENTPD1, ITGAE and ITGA1 never appear as NK annotation axes. NK3_GZMK and NK3_ENTPD1 were never separated, so the A->B clonal test was never posed, let alone answered.

(b) THE NSCLC ARM HAD NO NK CELLS TO TRACE. Verbatim: "depletion of NK cells in the tumor relative to NILT" and "While NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors ...". X4's entire primary comparison is intratumoural-A versus intratumoural-B in lung; that cell yield did not exist in this dataset.

(c) THE ONE NK-RICH TUMOUR WAS OVARIAN, AND THE QUESTION ASKED WAS EXPANSION, NOT ANCESTRY. Verbatim: "one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005) exhibited substantial NK infiltration ... These NK cells lacked chromatin accessibility at CD3D and CD8A loci but showed accessibility at NCR1 and GNLY, confirming their NK identity ... Notably, expanded NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response." That is a compartment-restriction result (tumour vs blood), not a state-to-state ancestry result. Separately, in NSCLC: "we observed expanded NK cell clones in NILT and peripheral blood," and among blood-enriched clones "2 by NK cells from a single donor (SU-L-005)."

(d) THEIR GENERAL NK STATEMENT ACTIVELY UNDERCUTS X4'S RESOLVABILITY. Verbatim: "innate immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, DCs, and NK cells, consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing, suggesting that they originated from recent hematopoietic output without substantial clonal bottlenecks prior to tissue infiltration." Promiscuous clone sharing across innate states is the regime in which "A and B share ancestors" is uninformative — it is what you see whether or not A converts to B. This converges with Rückert's null in conventional NK (PMID 36289449).

SECOND NEAREST, ON THE PRECURSOR ARCHITECTURE ITSELF: Wu C, Espinoza DA, ... Bryceson YT, Dunbar CE. "Clonal expansion and compartmentalized maintenance of rhesus macaque NK cell subsets." Sci Immunol 2018;3(29):eaat9781. PMID 30389798 / PMC7393805. Barcoded autologous HSPC transplant, >4 years. Asked X4's exact structural question one level up — is the CD56bright-like subset the clonal source of the mature effector subset? — and answered NO: oligoclonal CD56-CD16+ NK "remained long-term clonally uncoupled from other hematopoietic lineages, including CD56+CD16- NK cells," KIR-segregated, maintained by "peripheral compartmentalized self-renewal," with "linear NK cell production from multipotent hematopoietic progenitors or less mature CD56+CD16- cells ... negligible during homeostasis and moderate proliferative stress." Differs from X4: macaque, blood, non-tumour, CD16/CD56 rather than GZMK/ENTPD1, and homeostasis rather than an inflamed TME.

THIRD, ON THE TISSUE-VS-BLOOD ARM: Wu C, Liang JA, ... Dunbar CE. "Barcode clonal tracking of tissue-resident immune cells in rhesus macaque highlights distinct clonal distribution pattern of tissue NK cells." Front Immunol 2022;13:994498. PMID 36605190 / PMC9808525. Same barcoded model extended to liver, spleen, lung and GI versus blood. Found tissue-restricted NK clone sets (lung-specific, GI-specific; liver/spleen-shared) and expanded blood DN clones feeding tissue NK — "but absent in CD56+16- TR NK across all tissues analyzed." This is X4's compartment-3/4 question (local product vs pre-existing tissue-resident pool vs recent immigrant) answered with real barcodes — but in macaque, without tumour, and without the GZMK/ENTPD1 axis.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
X4 invokes local differentiation/plasticity plus tissue residency. Every adjacent field has already run this exact structural question through a lineage tool, and the answers are heterogeneous enough that X4 cannot borrow a presumption from any of them.

MYELOID — FULLY OCCUPIED, SAME DATASET, POSITIVE ANSWER. Liu et al. 2026 (PMID 42242233) is the myeloid version of X4 and it worked: TME-resident macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, with DC-biased and macrophage-biased clones whose blood precursors already carry distinct epigenetic profiles — "intratumoral myeloid differentiation fate may be peripherally programmed before TME infiltration." Note what this does to X4: the same authors, same tumours, same assay found that the intratumoural state's origin was NOT local conversion but a peripherally pre-programmed bias. That is precisely X4's Brownlie-2021 alternative, confirmed in the neighbouring lineage of the same tissue.

MOUSE NK — OCCUPIED, AND IT FLIPPED A PSEUDOTIME STORY. Flommersfeld S et al. "Fate mapping of single NK cells identifies a type 1 innate lymphoid-like lineage that bridges innate and adaptive recognition of viral infection." Immunity 2021;54:2288-2304. PMID 34437840 / PMC8528403 (archived). Retrogenic colour barcoding of SINGLE Ly49H+ NK cells transferred into Rag2-/-Il2rg-/- hosts, MCMV, clones read at d8. Verbatim: "progeny derived from single Ly49H+ NK cells showed limited diversification and instead adopted one of two distinct fates"; the two fates "originated from two distinct NK cell lineages present already during the steady state and stably maintained throughout infection" (CD62L+ cNK vs CD62L-CD160+ ILC1-like, splenic-resident). A phenotypic continuum that reads as one lineage differentiating was resolved by clonal fate mapping into two pre-existing lineages. This is the canonical demonstration in the NK field that the lineage primitive can invert a trajectory claim — and it is exactly X4's competing hypothesis.

MOUSE NK->TISSUE-RESIDENT CONVERSION IN TUMOURS — CLAIMED, NEVER BARCODED. Gao Y et al. "Tumor immunoevasion by the conversion of effector NK cells into type 1 innate lymphoid cells." Nat Immunol 2017;18:1004-1015. PMID 28759001; companion Cortez VS et al. "SMAD4 impedes the conversion of NK cells into ILC1-like cells." Nat Immunol 2017;18:995-1003. PMID 28759002. TGF-beta-dependent conversion of CD49a-CD49b+Eomes+ NK into CD49a+ intILC1/ILC1 in the mouse TME, established with "global transcriptomic and flow-cytometry analyses and genetically engineered mouse models" plus adoptive transfer — population-level fate, no clonal barcode. So the mouse analogue of X4 (conventional NK converting locally into a CD49a+ tissue-resident-like intratumoural state) is asserted in the literature but has never itself been clonally adjudicated. Human in-vitro versions exist too (TGF-beta+IL-15, PMID 32332109; IL-35, PMID 40610398) and are equally non-clonal.

T CELL — HEAVILY OCCUPIED VIA TCR AS THE LINEAGE TOOL, AND THE ANSWER IS OFTEN "NOT LOCAL CONVERSION." Yost KE et al., Nat Med 2019;25:1251-1259, PMID 31359002 — clonal replacement: the post-treatment intratumoural exhausted pool was largely NEW clones from outside, not locally converted residents. Wu TD et al., Nature 2020;579:274-278, PMID 32103181 — peripheral clonal expansion predicts tumour infiltration. Pai JA et al., Cancer Cell 2023;41:776-790.e7, PMID 37001526 — TCR lineage tracing of clonal progenitors and long-term persistence during ICB. Krishna C et al., Cancer Cell 2021;39:662-677.e6, PMID 33861994 — multiregional TCR linking tissue-resident T cells to tumour topology. The T-cell field's verdict is that recruitment/replacement is real and frequently dominant over local conversion — which is exactly why X4 must carry compartments 3 and 4, and why a YES on X4 would not be a foregone conclusion.

ILC — OCCUPIED WITH FATE MAPPING. ILC3->ILC1 conversion adjudicated by fate mapping (PMID 33214656, Campylobacter); Bielecki P et al., Nature 2021;592:128-132, PMID 33536623, "Skin-resident innate lymphoid cells converge on a pathogenic effector state" — convergence of resident ILC subsets onto one effector state, the same shape as X4's convergence onto NK3_ENTPD1. Also PMID 38484189 (Blood Adv 2024), clonal + single-cell analysis separating human NK from noncytotoxic ILCs.

NET: the question shape is answered everywhere around X4, with lineage tools, and the answers split — myeloid says peripherally pre-programmed, mouse NK says two pre-existing lineages, T cells say frequently replacement — so no field supplies a default X4 can inherit. The NK-specific slot for this exact pair of intratumoural human states is genuinely empty.
