b.why:
NOT DECIDABLE. Two independent defeaters, either sufficient on its own, plus a third minor one.

(1) THERE IS NO OPERAND B. The primitive answers "do A and B share an ancestor, and how recently." That presupposes A and B can each be POINTED AT — sorted at the bench by a rule fixed in advance and independent of lineage. "Exhausted NK" is not such a rule. The label was assigned by explicit analogy — Gill 2012 (PMID 22544698): "We have termed this phenomenon 'NK-cell exhaustion' by analogy with similar findings in CD8+ T cell biology" — and has never been given operational content in NK cells. PD-1 is near-absent/disputed on NK (in Gill it was negative and consigned to "data not shown"); TIGIT/TIM-3/LAG-3 are non-specific; there is no NK chromatin or DNA-methylation signature of the state (no equivalent of Sen 2016 PMID 27789799 / Pauken 2016 PMID 27789795); and the T cell field's defining enforcer TOX (Khan 2019 PMID 31207603) is a DEVELOPMENTAL requirement in NK cells (Aliahmad 2010 PMID 20818394), so it is unavailable as a definition and is in fact inverted. Under the field's own consensus criteria for the borrowed term (Blank 2019 PMID 31570879) the first anchor — chronic antigen through a clonotypic receptor — is undefined by construction in NK, which have no clonotypic receptor. With no gate for B there is no lineage question, only a naming dispute. There is also a circularity hazard: defining B post hoc as "the cells lineage places downstream of functional NK" uses lineage to define the state and then lineage to prove the transition.

(2) THE REVERSIBLE-STATE TRAP, AND IT SURVIVES STIPULATION. Suppose we generously stipulate B := intratumoural NK that fail to degranulate / produce IFN-g on restimulation. NK effector capacity is a demonstrated BIDIRECTIONAL, DIVISION-INDEPENDENT rheostat. Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) transferred hyporesponsive b2m-/- NK into non-irradiated WT hosts; they reached host-WT IFN-g levels by ~day 4, stably, receptor-restricted (Ly49C+ but not Ly49C-), with NO CFSE dilution. Baseline heterogeneity is likewise established, not hypothetical: a large hyporesponsive fraction exists in every healthy animal by education status (Anfossi 2006 PMID 16901727; Joncker 2009 PMID 19342631), and hyporesponsive NK can preferentially dominate an in vivo response (Orr 2010 PMID 20190757). Consequently both answers produce the SAME clonal structure:
  - Barcodes SHARED between the functional and hypofunctional buckets is predicted by conversion (A->B), by the reverse (B->A, Elliott), by continuous bidirectional traffic, and trivially by one clone being sampled at two rheostat settings on the same day.
  - Barcodes NOT SHARED is predicted by selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing hyporesponsive clone (Mavilio 2005 PMID 15699323 titled the human phenotype as a dysfunctional subset "expanded" in viremic HIV) AND equally by conversion in which the converted cell's functional siblings died or exited the sampled compartment.
Neither observation licenses a direction. The state is not clonally heritable, so it is not a lineage property, and the primitive is structurally blind to it.

(3) RESIDUAL FUNCTIONAL PREDICATE. "Exhausted" means hierarchical functional loss. "A becomes functionally B-like" is out of scope for a primitive that measures only shared ancestry.

NARROW READING THAT WOULD BE DECIDABLE — recorded for completeness, and it is NOT this claim: "is the hypofunctional intratumoural NK pool clonally DISTINCT from, or interleaved with, the functional intratumoural NK pool" is of the same/different-lineage form, and the how-recently term does real work there. But that is R2/T4's question rather than X5's, and it still fails B2 below, so promoting X5 by rewriting it does not rescue it.
b.action_if_yes:
YES = barcodes/mtDNA clones are SHARED across the two buckets; hypofunctional intratumoural NK coalesce recently with functional NK in the same tumour rather than only at the HSPC root.

Very next experiment: sort the hypofunctional bucket and ask whether the state is FIXED or a setting — transfer it into a tumour-free host (or withdraw the cytokine/ligand stimulus), re-read function at 4 and 10 days against a within-recipient comparator, and in parallel run ATAC-seq and DNA methylation on both buckets to ask whether a distinct, stable epigenetic state exists at all.

Note what this is: a reversibility test plus a state-definition assay. Neither uses the lineage primitive. And the reversibility half already has a published answer in the opposite direction (Elliott 2010, PMID 20819924), so the YES branch mostly re-opens a question that has been answered against the claim by a better-controlled design than Gill's.
b.action_if_no:
NO = the hypofunctional cells sit in clones that do not contain functional cells; the two buckets are clonally separate at recent depth.

Very next experiment: sort the hypofunctional bucket and ask what it actually IS — education/licensing status, adaptive PLZF-low NKG2C+ identity (Schlums 2015 PMID 25786176, which carries the same surface reading, the opposite label, and SUPERIOR ADCC), or the CD56-CD16+ expanded subset (Mavilio 2005 PMID 15699323) — then test whether that subset's state is fixed or revertible by transfer/stimulus withdrawal, with ATAC and methylation on both buckets.

That is the identical experiment as the YES branch, reached from the other side. And the conclusion half is close to vacuous on its own: "the label was wrong, these are a pre-existing selected subset" is a re-description the literature has had available since 2005 and has not adopted, so producing it again changes no downstream decision.
b.both_answers_reason:
FAILS, and fails hard — this is the cleanest B2 failure in the tumour group.

(a) THE TWO BRANCHES CONVERGE ON THE SAME EXPERIMENT. Both YES and NO terminate in "now sort compartment B and determine, by non-lineage assays (transfer/withdrawal reversibility test + ATAC/methylation), whether it is a fixed state." That is not a fork; it is one experiment reached by two routes.

(b) WORSE THAN REDUNDANT — IT IS OUT OF ORDER. The convergent next experiment is the one that must be run BEFORE the lineage experiment, because it is what supplies B's definition. You cannot pre-register what "clonally related to exhausted NK" means until "exhausted NK" is a sortable, epigenetically anchored compartment. Running lineage first spends the scarce resource on a question whose operand does not yet exist.

(c) NEITHER BRANCH MOVES A DOWNSTREAM DECISION. The two verified dependencies are unmoved by either answer. The intermittent-versus-continuous IL-15/N-803 dosing decision (Felices 2018 PMID 29415897) follows from the kinetic observation of declining function regardless of ancestry. The anti-TIGIT programme built on the frame (Zhang 2018 PMID 29915296) has already read out — tiragolumab missed primary endpoints in SKYSCRAPER-01 and -02 and in liver, oesophageal and head-and-neck trials, discontinued July 2025 — so a clonal ancestry result arrives after the bet was settled and would not have altered the trial design under either answer.

(d) G4 CROSS-FIELD CHECK CONFIRMS THE ORDERING, IT DOES NOT GREEN-LIGHT THE CLAIM. The CD8 T cell field HAS run the clonal version of this exact structural question and got a real fork: Daniel et al., Nat Immunol 2022 (PMID 36289450), "Divergent clonal differentiation trajectories of T cell exhaustion," used paired scRNA + TCR to resolve Tex-term-biased, Tex-KLR-biased and divergent clones, and tied trajectory to TCR avidity; precursor-product was separately nailed by SORTED-SUBSET transfer (Im 2016 PMID 27501248; Utzschneider 2016 PMID 27533016; Miller 2019 PMID 30778252; Beltra 2020 PMID 32396847). Those clonal steps were informative only because two preconditions held: the destination states were DEFINED FIRST by chromatin (PMID 27789799, 27789795) and consensus criteria (PMID 31570879), and T cells carry a NATIVE clonal barcode (the rearranged TCR), so clonality was read for free alongside phenotype. NK cells satisfy neither: destination undefined, and no rearranged receptor, so the barcode must be exogenous (mouse-only) or endogenous-mtDNA (expensive, low clone resolution). The borrowed field's occupancy shows exactly which prerequisite X5 is missing.

(e) FINALLY, THE ONE DESIGN THAT WOULD BE INFORMATIVE DOES NOT NEED THE PRIMITIVE. If you sort candidate-precursor (functional) and candidate-product (hypofunctional) NK at t0 and transfer them separately, you get the answer with two congenic markers and no barcode at all. That is the T cell field's Anchor-2 experiment, it has never been run for NK "exhaustion," and it is cheap — which means X5's genuinely missing experiment is not a clonal-barcoding experiment. X5 is OUT.

Search caveat (G3): searches run for this row were mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER + NK, barcoding + NK/lymphocyte, mouse fate-mapping/Polylox/CRISPR-recorder + NK dysfunction, and the T cell/ILC cross-field set. The NK-exhaustion-specific occupancy searches returned nothing on point, but they were noisy and I would record that as NOT_SEARCHED rather than a clean FALSE if occupancy were being scored this round; it is not, and nothing above depends on the claim being unoccupied.
b.compartments_needed:
Four things must be in hand at once, from one individual:

A (candidate precursor) — functional NK, contemporaneous. Practical instantiations: (i) matched peripheral blood NK; (ii) NK from uninvolved same-organ tissue adjacent to the tumour; (iii) intratumoural NK passing a LIVE functional gate (surface CD107a degranulation, or IFN-g secretion-capture) after short restimulation.

B (candidate product) — "exhausted" intratumoural NK. NO AGREED GATE EXISTS; this is the reason the row fails B1. Stipulated proxies would be the functional-assay-negative fraction from the same restimulation, or contested surface proxies (NKG2D-lo, TIGIT+, CD56-CD16+, PD-1+), none of which is validated as a state definition.

C (outgroup/root) — matched blood or bone-marrow NK, MANDATORY, not optional. Without a third compartment the "how recently" term cannot be exercised, and A/B sharing is uninterpretable because all NK share an HSPC ancestor by construction.

D (mouse instantiation of the same set) — donor splenic NK at t0, plus tumour, spleen and blood at t1 in the Gill-type transfer model.
b.compartments_obtainable:
TISSUE ACCESS IS THE EASY PART, and this is the only dimension on which X5 scores well. Paired tumour + adjacent uninvolved tissue + peripheral blood from ONE HUMAN is routine at surgical resection (lung, colorectal, renal, hepatocellular, breast). Tumour and adjacent-normal are SURGERY-ONLY — not obtainable from a living donor by any other route — while blood and marrow pair freely. Nothing here requires post-mortem tissue, nothing requires pregnancy, nothing is restricted to mouse. The mouse transfer model additionally gives all four compartments trivially from one animal.

BUT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT ACCESS — IT IS THAT A AND B ARE NOT TWO COEXISTING PLACES. The claim's A is "the same cell BEFORE it became exhausted," which is a time point, not a compartment, and is destroyed by the act of measuring it. Clonal barcoding substitutes SIBLINGS for the ancestral state; that substitution is licensed only if the state is clonally heritable over the sampling window. Elliott 2010 (PMID 20819924) — full reversion in ~4 days with no cell division — says it is not. So the compartment pair that would actually decide X5 is unobtainable IN PRINCIPLE, in every species, for reasons that have nothing to do with consent, surgery, or tissue banking; while the compartment pair that IS readily obtainable decides a different and weaker question.
b.compartment_notes:
Three practical notes that matter if anyone tries this anyway.

(1) THE GATE FOR B IS NOT STATE-PRESERVING. Defining the hypofunctional bucket requires ex vivo restimulation (4-6 h, PMA/ionomycin or tumour targets) to run the functional readout. That manipulation perturbs the very axis being measured, on cells whose state is documented to move on an hours-to-days scale. Worse, intracellular cytokine staining is fix/perm and destroys live-cell sorting, mtDNA genotyping and ATAC quality — so only surface CD107a or cytokine secretion-capture keep cells alive and sortable, and both still require the perturbing culture step. There is no way to sort B without changing B.

(2) HUMAN CLONALITY MUST BE ENDOGENOUS, AND NK GET NO FREE BARCODE. Exogenous barcoding of human NK in vivo is impossible, so the readout would be somatic mtDNA variants via mtscATAC-seq (PMID 36792778) or MAESTER, with the human haematopoietic genealogy precedent at PMID 38253266. Unlike T and B cells, NK have no rearranged antigen receptor, so the native clonal barcode that made the T cell exhaustion trajectory work (PMID 36289450) simply does not exist here — clone resolution would be materially worse in the one lineage where the question is being asked.

(3) THE MOUSE DESIGN THAT WOULD WORK DISSOLVES THE NEED FOR THE PRIMITIVE. Only in mouse can you put one exogenous barcode on one MATURE NK cell (transduce sorted mature NK, then transfer). But that design's t0 sort IS the sorted-precursor-transfer experiment, which yields the answer using two congenic markers and no barcode at all. The primitive adds nothing to the design that would settle the question — a further reason X5 does not belong on a clonal-barcoding shortlist.

o.already_traced_evidence:
No one has adjudicated "intratumoural exhausted NK are the clonal progeny of functional NK" with a clonal primitive. This is a positive finding, not merely an absence: the single paper that assembled EXACTLY the compartment set this claim requires stopped short of the state partition, and I read its primary text rather than its abstract.

Liu VV, Sandor K, Yan PK, ... Lareau CA, Satpathy AT. "Clonal lineage tracing of innate immune cells in human cancer." Cancer Cell 2026;44:1509-1521.e4. PMID 42242233 (preprint PMID 40777278 / PMC12330704; archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_42242233.txt and /home/user/aaa/refs/X5_PMC12330704.txt). mtscATAC-seq, 218,715 cells, matched tumour + non-involved lung tissue (NILT) + PBMC from 5 NSCLC patients, and tumour + PBMC from 5 ovarian patients (3 with matched blood). That is compartments A(i) blood NK, A(ii) uninvolved same-organ NK, B intratumoural NK, and C matched blood outgroup — all four, paired, from one human. What they actually did with NK, verbatim from the text:
  - NK were annotated as a CELL TYPE only: "4 NK cell/ILC clusters (NCR1)". No functional-state partition, no exhaustion gate, no CD107a/IFN-g capture (mtscATAC-seq fixes cells; a live functional gate is not compatible with the assay as run).
  - "Consistent with previous reports of adaptive-like, oligoclonal NK cell responses in human cytomegalovirus infection, we observed expanded NK cell clones in NILT and peripheral blood."
  - "While NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors, one ovarian tumor (SU-O-005) exhibited substantial NK infiltration... Clonal analysis revealed an oligoclonal architecture resembling adaptive lymphocytes. Notably, expanded NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood, indicating a tumor-restricted NK response."
  - Cross-cell-type clone sharing was computed at cell-TYPE resolution ("innate immune cells, including monocytes, macrophages, DCs, and NK cells, consistently exhibited high levels of clone sharing"), never at NK-STATE resolution.
So the question asked was "is the intratumoural NK clone present in blood?" (n=1 tumour, answer: no) — a tissue-compartmentalisation question, not a state-transition question. The functional-vs-exhausted axis inside the tumour was never touched. Their own sentence "NK cells were rarely detected in most tumors" is also the empirical reason nobody has done it: 9 of 10 patients yielded too few intratumoural NK to clone at all.

Human NK mtDNA benchmark, also not the claim: Rückert T, Lareau CA, Mashreghi MF, Ludwig LS, Romagnani C. "Clonal expansion and epigenetic inheritance of long-lasting NK cell memory." Nat Immunol 2022;23:1551-1563. PMID 36289449. Somatic mtDNA mutations as endogenous barcodes in ex vivo human NK; establishes that NK clones are stably maintained in specific epigenetic states over time. PERIPHERAL BLOOD ONLY, HCMV adaptive/memory state, no tumour, no exhaustion, no functional assay.

Barcoded-transplant NK literature (Dunbar lab), the closest thing to a true engineered barcode in NK, none in tumour: Wu C et al. Sci Immunol 2018;3:eaat9781 (PMID 30389798) — barcoded rhesus HSPC transplant; CD56-CD16+ NK are oligoclonal and "long-term clonally uncoupled from other hematopoietic lineages, including CD56+CD16- NK cells". Wu C et al. Front Immunol 2022;13:994498 (PMID 36605190) — same system, tissue-resident NK clonal distribution across liver/spleen/lung/GI vs blood. Wu C et al. Cell Stem Cell 2014 (PMID 24702997); Front Immunol 2019 (PMID 31649681, CMV effect on NK clonal repertoire); Mol Ther Methods Clin Dev 2025 (PMID 40621477, barcoded anti-CD20 CAR into macaque/human NK — a delivery-optimisation paper, no tumour adjudication). Every one of these answers "which NK SUBSET/TISSUE does a clone occupy", never "does a clone straddle a functional and an exhausted state in a tumour".

Mouse: no clonal barcode has been applied to NK in tumours. Searches for Polylox/confetti/CRISPR-recorder + NK returned nothing on point.
o.nearest_occupant:
Two occupants, in different senses. Neither is the claim.

(1) NEAREST CLONAL OCCUPANT — Liu et al., Cancer Cell 2026, PMID 42242233. Has the method (mtscATAC-seq), has all four compartments paired from one human (tumour + NILT + blood), and does report an intratumoural NK clonal result. HOW IT DIFFERS, precisely: it partitions NK by TISSUE, not by STATE. Its NK finding is "expanded intratumoural NK clones were absent from matched peripheral blood" in a single ovarian tumour — i.e. it answers A(i)-vs-B compartment sharing and returns a NEGATIVE, whereas claim X5 asks about A-vs-B within the tumour across a functional/exhausted boundary. It never gated NK on function, never applied an exhaustion definition, and ran a fixed-cell assay that structurally excludes the live CD107a/IFN-g gate that claim X5's compartment A(iii) and B require. n=1 informative tumour. So the specific adjudication is open, and this paper is the demonstration that the reagent exists and the yield does not.

(2) NEAREST OCCUPANT OF THE UNDERLYING BIOLOGY, non-clonal — Dean I, Lee CYC, ... Clatworthy MR, Withers DR. "Rapid functional impairment of natural killer cells following tumor entry limits anti-tumor immunity." Nat Commun 2024;15:683. PMID 38267402. Kaede photo-labelling of tumours plus longitudinal transcriptomics: circulating NK recruited into the tumour rapidly lose effector function and adopt a distinct CD49a+ tissue-residency-like dysfunctional state. This is a population-level fate map with a timestamp, NOT a clonal method — it cannot say whether two cells share an ancestor — but it already answers the directional question X5 is a proxy for ("functional NK entering the tumour become the dysfunctional intratumoural cells") at population resolution, in mouse, decisively. Any clonal version of X5 would be re-answering with a costlier primitive a question this paper has closed.

(3) LOAD-BEARING FOR WHY X5 IS NOT A LINEAGE QUESTION AT ALL — Pouxvielh K et al. "Tumor-induced natural killer cell dysfunction is a rapid and reversible process uncoupled from the expression of immune checkpoints." Sci Adv 2024;10:eadn0164. PMID 39196934. The state is REVERSIBLE and uncoupled from the very surface proxies (checkpoints) that claim X5's compartment B would have to be gated on. A reversible state leaves no clonal signature: a clone straddling both states and a clone confined to one state are both consistent with an interconverting state, so the clonal read-out does not discriminate. This corroborates the B1 failure independently of the occupancy question.

Also checked and NOT the claim: Vo DN et al. Blood Adv 2024;8:2933-2951 (PMID 38484189), DNA-barcode tracing separating human NK from non-cytotoxic ILC along development — clonal, NK, but developmental origin, in vitro, no tumour. Gill S et al. Blood 2012;119:5758-5768 (PMID 22544698), the Gill-type transfer model named in compartment D — adoptive transfer, no barcodes, no clonal resolution.
o.crossfield_occupancy:
HEAVILY OCCUPIED. The structural question "are the dysfunctional/exhausted cells in a tumour the clonal descendants of the functional ones, or a separate lineage?" has been asked and answered with clonal tools in the T cell field, and with the identical mtDNA tool in the myeloid field. NK is the last compartment to be asked, and the answer elsewhere has repeatedly been that the clonal read-out under-determines the state question.

T CELL — answered, multiple times, with the native clonal barcode (TCR):
  - Yost KE et al. Nat Med 2019;25:1251-1259 (PMID 31359002). Paired scRNA+TCR-seq, basal cell carcinoma, pre/post PD-1. The exhausted CD8 TIL pool that expands after PD-1 blockade consists of NOVEL clonotypes not previously detected in the tumour — "clonal replacement". This is exactly the X5 structure (does the exhausted compartment descend from the resident functional one, or arrive separately?) answered with a clonal primitive, with a NEGATIVE answer for the intuitive model.
  - Pai JA et al. Cancer Cell 2023;41:776-790.e7 (PMID 37001526). "Lineage tracing reveals clonal progenitors and long-term persistence of tumor-specific T cells during immune checkpoint blockade" — establishes clonal linkage between TCF7+SELL+ progenitor-exhausted cells in the draining lymph node and their exhausted counterparts in the tumour. The precursor-to-exhausted-product lineage relation is settled.
  - Wu TD et al. Nature 2020;579:274-280 (PMID 32103181) — peripheral clonal expansion predicts tumour infiltration; the blood-to-tumour clonal bridge, i.e. exactly the compartment A(i)-to-B question X5 poses.
  - Luo Y et al. Cancer Immunol Res 2026;14:32-45 (PMID 41081433) — single-cell clonal lineage tracing of neoantigen-specific CD8 fate decisions; the same question at single-clone resolution in mouse.
  - Yamaguchi A et al. Oncoimmunology 2026 (PMID 41787604) — Pdcd1-CreERT2 genetic fate mapping. Notably, PD-1-fate-mapped NK cells in tumours LOST PD-1 and REGAINED FUNCTION, i.e. a genetic fate map has already shown the NK "exhausted" state to be exited, reinforcing that this is a reversible state and not a lineage endpoint.

MYELOID — answered with the SAME mtDNA tool, in the SAME paper, in the SAME patients: Liu et al. (PMID 42242233) resolved that TME macrophages and DC3 are clonally related to circulating and tissue-infiltrating monocytes, and identified DC-biased vs macrophage-biased clones with peripherally programmed fate bias. The myeloid arm of that paper is what an NK arm would have looked like had NK yields permitted and had a state definition existed. The authors could run the NK version and did not.

ILC — partially occupied and methodologically instructive: Vo DN et al. Blood Adv 2024 (PMID 38484189) used DNA-barcode lineage output to place NK relative to non-cytotoxic ILC, showing S3b-NK and S4-NK are closely related while ILC3 is distant. So the ILC field has used clonal tools for lineage-vs-state discrimination among innate lymphocytes; the reason it has not done so for "exhaustion" is that ILC plasticity is likewise treated as a reversible state.

Net: the mechanism X5 borrows (exhaustion) originates in the T cell field, and its occupancy lives there. The T cell field needed an ANTIGEN-SPECIFIC clonal barcode plus a validated, epigenetically anchored state definition (TOX/TCF7) to make the question decidable. Claim X5 has neither — no agreed exhaustion gate for NK, and a native barcode (mtDNA) that is state-agnostic.
